items.title: Public Preview: Azure ExpressRoute resiliency guard
items.description:
Azure ExpressRoute resiliency guard is now available in public preview for ExpressRoute virtual network gateways. The new resiliency model property lets you specify whether a gateway is intended for a single-homed or multi-homed configuration, helping align your deployment with the resiliency requirements of your workloads.

For multi-homed gateways, resiliency guard guides you to connect either two ExpressRoute circuits in different peering locations or an ExpressRoute Metro circuit. Portal guidance and configuration safeguards help identify incomplete setups and reduce the risk of changes that could weaken gateway resiliency. Single-homed configurations remain available for workloads that do not require multi-site resiliency. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing:  Azure Databricks Genie One and Genie Agents Free Usage extended through January 31, 2027
items.description:
Free usage of Genie One and Genie Agents in Azure Databricks is now extended through January 31, 2027, from the previous end date of July 31, 2026. Budget controls do not apply to these products during the promotional period. The promotion covers usage by users only - service principals are excluded, and their Genie One and Genie Agents usage continues to be billed. Genie Code is not included in this promotion: each Genie Code user continues to receive 150 free Databricks units (DBUs) per month, and usage above that allowance receives a 25% promotional discount through January 31, 2027, combined with applicable discounts on the Serverless Real-Time Inference SKU. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Migrate from AWS FSx for Windows File Server to Azure Files with Azure Storage Mover
items.description:
Azure Storage Mover now supports agentless, cloud-to-cloud migration from AWS FSx for Windows File Server (SMB) to Azure Files (SMB), in preview. You can move your Windows file shares off FSx and into Azure Files without deploying or managing a migration agent — the service handles the transfer for you. File data is copied directly from FSx to your Azure file share over a private connection between Azure and your AWS network.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: SharePoint Connector for Azure Databricks
items.description:
The SharePoint connector for Azure Databricks is now generally available. Organizations can use Lakeflow Connect to ingest files from SharePoint into Azure Databricks, helping unify enterprise content with data and AI workflows on Azure. The connector supports incremental ingestion, Unity Catalog governance, and multiple authentication methods for enterprise-scale deployments.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Unity AI Gateway on Azure Databricks
items.description:
Unity AI Gateway is now generally available on Azure Databricks. Unity AI Gateway provides centralized governance for AI models, agents, tools, and MCP services, helping organizations monitor usage, manage costs, apply guardrails, and enforce access controls across AI workloads. Built on Unity Catalog, it extends governance capabilities across both Azure Databricks and external AI services.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Explicit proxy in Azure Firewall
items.description:
Azure Firewall explicit proxy is now generally available. Explicit proxy enables customers to configure applications and browsers to send HTTP and HTTPS traffic directly to Azure Firewall using proxy settings, providing an alternative to route-based traffic steering and enabling more granular control over outbound web traffic. 

The GA release builds on extensive customer validation during public preview, where explicit proxy was enabled across 300+ Azure subscriptions and adopted by approximately 40 S500 customers. Customer feedback gathered during preview directly influenced several key enhancements delivered as part of GA, including support for serving both HTTP and HTTPS destinations through a single proxy endpoint, Managed Identity-based PAC file retrieval, and an improved portal configuration experience. 

A key customer use case for explicit proxy is Azure Arc onboarding in hybrid environments. Organizations can use Azure Firewall as a forward proxy for Arc-enabled servers, enabling secure connectivity to required Microsoft services while maintaining centralized outbound access controls. Combined with support for forward proxy migration scenarios and application-level traffic steering, Explicit Proxy helps customers simplify network operations while leveraging Azure Firewall's existing security capabilities. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Nested confidential (cc_v5) VMs will be retired on September 1, 2026
items.description: On September 1, 2026, the cc_v5 confidential VM series will be retired and will no longer be available for use or purchase. Any affected VM that has not been resized before that date will deallocated. The impacted VM sizes that will be retired are: DCas_cc_v5, DCads_cc_v5, ECas_cc_v5, and ECads_cc_v5.

items.title: Public Preview: Perimeter link feature in network security perimeter
items.description:
Perimeter link (cross-perimeter connectivity) is a network security perimeter capability that allows trusted resources in two different network security perimeters to securely communicate with each other using Managed Identity (MSI), without requiring additional network security perimeter access rules or network configuration changes. It preserves Zero Trust boundaries while enabling controlled service-to-service access across perimeters 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Private Link support over IPv6
items.description:
Azure Private Link over IPv6 enables you to privately access Azure PaaS services, such as Azure Storage and Azure SQL Database, over IPv6-based connectivity. You can now use IPv6 private endpoints to connect from IPv6 clients in an Azure virtual network or from on-premises networks over ExpressRoute. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure DNS enables DNS-based load balancing through Traffic Manager integration
items.description:
Azure DNS now offers a seamless way to integrate with Azure Traffic Manager for DNS-based traffic routing. Customers can now directly associate Azure DNS record set with Traffic Manager profiles without creating CNAME record for trafficmanager.net domain. This improves lookup latency by eliminating a CNAME hop and enables DNSSEC compatibility for load balanced records by removing unsigned trafficmanager.net domain from CNAME lookup chain.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network routing appliance
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network routing appliance is now generally available. It delivers private connectivity across virtual networks, using specialized hardware for low latency, high throughput, and better performance than virtual machines. 

Key benefits and functionalities: 

  • High-bandwidth east-west routing: provisioned bandwidth tiers up to 200 Gbps per instance.  
  • Dual-stack and IPv6 at scale: IPv4, IPv6, and dual-stack virtual networks, including IPv6 access control list enforcement.  
  • Scale-out private access: global and cross-region private endpoint support through a single appliance.  
  • No operational overhead: fully managed with built-in high availability and availability zone resiliency.  
  • Built-in monitoring: throughput, packet, and flow metrics available in Azure Monitor with no diagnostic configuration required. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Trusted Launch as Default
items.description:
Trusted Launch as Default (TLaD) is now generally available for new Azure Gen2 virtual machines and virtual machine scale sets. TLaD automatically enables Secure Boot and vTPM for supported deployments, helping customers establish a stronger security baseline for workloads at no additional cost.

New Gen2 VMs deployed through Azure Portal, Azure CLI, and Azure PowerShell automatically use Trusted Launch by default. Customers deploying through ARM templates, Bicep, Terraform, and Azure SDKs can extend the same experience with a one-time subscription registration. Existing VMs remain unchanged, and any explicitly configured security settings continue to be honored.

Trusted Launch is available on supported x64 and Arm64 Gen2 VM sizes across Azure public, Azure Government, and Azure China regions.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Immutability to the most recent seven days of backups on Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance
items.description:
To enhance backup protection, Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance now automatically apply immutability to the most recent seven days of backups. This capability is enabled by default for all databases, regardless of the configured point-in-time restore retention period. No action or configuration is required.

Note: Support for Azure SQL Hyperscale backups is coming in a future release.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Single-click purchase for public SaaS offers
items.description:
Eligible SaaS products on Microsoft Marketplace now support a simplified purchase experience in Azure portal. Customers can review plan, billing, resource group, contact details, and terms information on a single page for completing the purchase. This experience isn’t currently supported for SaaS offers that use a custom purchasing experience (i.e. Azure native integrations, Model-as-a-Service, Secure Exchange products, etc.).

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Route-Maps for Azure Route Server
items.description:
Route maps for Azure Route Server are now available in public preview, providing fine-grained control over inbound and outbound routing across hybrid connections. Customers can manage routes advertised to and from Azure Route Server BGP peerings with Network Virtual Appliances (NVAs), ExpressRoute gateways, and VPN gateways in the same virtual network. Route-maps provide the following capabilities: 

  • Route summarization: Summarize routes when on-premises networks connect to the virtual network through ExpressRoute or VPN. 
  • Route control: Control routes entering and leaving Azure Route Server between on-premises networks, NVAs, and virtual networks. 
  • Path selection: Modify BGP attributes such as AS-PATH to make routes more or less preferred. 
  • Route tagging: Tag routes by using the BGP Community attribute. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for late-July
items.description:
In late-July 2026, the following update and enhancement was made to Azure SQL: 

  • Regex-based dynamic data masking (DDM) extends the built-in DDM feature with pattern‑based masking to hide sensitive data like emails, phone numbers, and identifiers—centrally enforced at the database layer.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in India South Central
items.description:
Now you can deploy Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in the India South Central Azure region.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Automation supports PowerShell 7.6 runbooks and Runtime environment
items.description:
Azure Automation is pleased to announce: 
  • General Availability of in-support PowerShell 7.6  runbooks
  • Runtime Environment GA, enabling customers to seamlessly upgrade their outdated scripts to supported runtime versions.  
  • Support for Azure CLI commands in PowerShell 7.6 runbooks GA 

Benefits: 

  • Stay current – Access to new language versions for improved security and performance. 
  • Faster Runbook upgrade – Easy portability of runbooks across different versions to keep pace with PowerShell and Python releases. 
  • Granular control – Complete control to configure the script execution environment, without worrying about conflicting module versions. 
  • Efficient Code organization – Eliminate the need to create multiple Automation accounts to segregate different versions of modules or conflicting modules. 

Learn more: 

  • Azure Automation runbook types | Microsoft Learn  
  • Upgrade runbook to latest language version  
  • Create PowerShell runbooks with Azure CLI commands  
  • Language runtime support and retirement policy for Azure Automation | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Announcing: Reservation exchanges for Azure services supported by savings plans will no longer be available starting February 1, 2027
items.description:
Starting February 1, 2027, Azure reservations exchanges will no longer be available for services covered by savings plans.  At the time of this announcement, this includes reservations for the following services:    

  • Compute services: Azure Virtual Machines, including exchanges between non-premium and premium storage, Azure Dedicated Host, and Azure App Service. 

  • Database services: Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Database for MySQL, Azure DocumentDB, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SQL Database, and Azure SQL Managed Instance.  

Each active reservation for impacted services purchased before February 1, 2027, will retain the right to one final exchange after that date.  

This reservation exchange policy update excludes products or services that are deprecated and approaching end of life, as well as cloud environments that don’t currently support savings plans. 

As savings plans coverage expands, reservations for those services will follow this policy and will not support exchanges. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Symmetric keys on Azure Key Vault Premium
items.description:
We’re announcing symmetric keys on Azure Key Vault Premium are now available in public preview. 

This preview enables customers and partners to evaluate symmetric encryption capabilities using the oct-HSM key type and the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm directly within Azure Key Vault. Customers can use AES algorithms to encrypt, decrypt, wrap, and unwrap data while continuing to benefit from Azure-managed security, compliance, and operational controls. 

AES algorithms with 256-bit keys are aligned with CNSA 2.0 requirements and can help organizations prepare for post-quantum cryptography readiness scenarios. 

Key benefits include: 

  • Centralized key management through Azure Key Vault Premium 
  • Support for oct-HSM symmetric keys 
  • AES-based encryption and decryption operations 
  • Simplified integration with existing Azure security workflows 
  • Consistent security and operational controls across Azure services 

Note: Azure portal support for symmetric key management is currently rolling out. During the rollout period, customers can use Azure CLI, ARM templates to create and manage oct-HSM symmetric keys and access the full preview functionality. 

Learn more:

  • About keys  
  • Key types, algorithms, and operations

items.title: Public Preview: Support for SMB Opportunistic Locking (Oplocks) configuration
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files now supports configuration of SMB opportunistic locking (oplocks) for SMB and dual-protocol volumes. Opportunistic locks (Oplocks) improve SMB client caching and are enabled by default. You can configure oplocks on new volumes or update the setting on existing volumes. System default is the default selection and enables opportunistic locks on the volume. A cross-region replication destination volume can use an oplock setting independent of its source volume. 

Learn more:

  • Create an SMB volume for Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn  
  • Create a dual-protocol volume for Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn 
  • What is Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Monitor Logs mirroring into Microsoft Fabric
items.description:
This capability shares telemetry from Azure Monitor Log Analytics workspaces into Microsoft Fabric, making observability data available in OneLake as Delta Parquet, the open format, without duplication and with near real-time availability. All Azure Monitor Logs tiers are supported, including Analytics, Basic, and Auxiliary logs.

Once available in Fabric, Azure Monitor data can be analyzed alongside operational and business data using Fabric capabilities such as Eventhouse, Power BI, Spark.

What you can do:
Organizations can combine telemetry with business context from systems such as ERP and CRM to gain deeper insight into the business impact of operational events, supporting cross-domain analysis, more informed decision-making, and faster action. Organizations can also apply advanced analytics, machine learning, long-term trend analysis, and reporting directly to their observability data.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 is now available for evaluation
items.description:
Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 RC1 is now available for evaluation in the Retail Eval feed. Whilst this release encompasses no customer-facing changes, it represents a major bump in Azure Sphere's underlying Linux kernel version as part of our long-term support and security commitment, as such, this release will operate for an extended evaluation period, until September 2026, enabling additional time for customer evaluation testing.

Whilst we've taken every measure to ensure that this update does not impact any of our contractual surfaces, with over six months of extensive integration and regression testing, we strongly encourage customers to evaluate this release with their in-market applications and to raise any issues with the Azure Sphere product group as early on as possible.

Following this evaluation period, 26.09 will be promoted and deployed broadly to devices in the Retail feed.

The 26.09 RC1 OS Retail Eval release includes a major Linux kernel version bump.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Enclave
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of Azure Enclave for Microsoft Azure, Azure Government, Azure Government Secret, and Azure Government Top Secret. Azure Enclave helps streamline the deployment and management of isolated cloud environments for sensitive workloads across government and other regulated industries. Azure Enclave helps customers quickly deliver their critical workloads while maintaining essential security and isolation. Azure Enclave is designed to isolate virtual networking infrastructure by default and includes controls intended to help ensure connections are explicitly configured and managed. 

With Azure Enclave, customers can: 

  • Quickly deploy secured environments using managed infrastructure and predefined architectural patterns. 
  • Provide access to authorized users in shared environments with controlled data access policies and defined permissions. 
  • Configure secured connections to sensitive data using endpoints you define and control for connectivity between resources. 
  • Apply multiple security controls, including network segmentation, role-based access, and monitoring, to help protect workloads and simplify management. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: NAT64 on StandardV2 NAT Gateway
items.description:
StandardV2 NAT Gateway now supports NAT64, enabling IPv6 workloads to communicate with IPv4-only internet destinations by translating synthesized outbound IPv6 traffic into IPv4 traffic. NAT64 relies on a DNS64-capable resolver to synthesize IPv6 addresses by embedding the IPv4 address within the NAT64 Well-Known Prefix 64:ff9b::/96 – so client traffic is naturally addressed to NAT64 for translation.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Application Routing with Gateway API
items.description:
Managing ingress routing while adopting newer Kubernetes standards can require balancing modernization efforts with existing deployments. Application Routing with Gateway API is now generally available on AKS, bringing the Kubernetes Gateway API to ingress management without requiring a service mesh. 

Existing ingress-nginx-based Application Routing remains supported until November, and customers can migrate to the Gateway API-based model at their own pace using the open-source ingress2gateway tool. This enables technical practitioners to adopt a standardized routing model while maintaining a lightweight footprint and supporting a gradual transition from existing ingress configurations.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Resource placement in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager
items.description:
Managing Kubernetes resources across multiple clusters can require significant manual effort to apply updates and maintain consistency. Resource placement in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager is now generally available and enables platform and application teams to consistently distribute Kubernetes resources across multiple AKS and Arc-enabled clusters.

This release includes the Resource Placement Kubernetes APIs in v1 and introduces a new Azure portal experience for creating, viewing, and managing placements across a fleet. By using placement policies that select target member clusters based on labels and properties, teams can reduce the effort and risk associated with applying, updating, and tracking resources on a cluster-by-cluster basis.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Maximum allowed failures for update runs in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager
items.description:
In fail-fast update rollouts, a small number of member cluster update failures can halt progress across a broader update deployment. Maximum Allowed Failures for update runs in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager, now available in preview, introduces an optional setting that allows update runs to continue when some member cluster updates fail.

Customers can define failure thresholds at either the stage or group level using fixed counts or percentages. This gives platform teams more control over the balance between rollout correctness and continued update progress, enabling more flexible and failure-tolerant update strategies across fleet-managed clusters.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Prepared Image Specification
items.description:
Organizations running large-scale, AI, GPU, Windows, and other performance-sensitive workloads on AKS often experience longer node startup times because new nodes must repeatedly download container images and perform initialization tasks before workloads can run.

With AKS Prepared Image Specification, now in preview, customers can create preconfigured node images that include required container images and customizations ahead of time, enabling new nodes to start in a ready-to-run state. This helps workloads achieve faster and more predictable scaling, reduce application startup latency, and improve operational efficiency during growth and burst traffic events.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Azure now available from new cloud region in India (India South Central)
items.description: Microsoft announces the opening of its fourth datacenter region in India, India South Central, with campuses in Hyderabad, Telangana. The region will provide customers with local, secure, state-of-the-art cloud infrastructure designed with AI readiness as a key focus. It supports growing demand for cloud and AI services, customer digital transformation, local data residency, improved latency, and resilient cloud capacity in India.

items.title: Generally Available: Claude Opus 5 on Azure Databricks
items.description:
Azure Databricks now supports Anthropic Claude Opus 5 through AI Model Serving. Claude Opus 5 is Anthropic's latest model for advanced reasoning, coding, agentic workflows, and professional knowledge work. 

Claude Opus 5 is designed for complex tasks requiring deep reasoning, long-horizon planning, and software development assistance. Customers can use Claude Opus 5 in Azure Databricks to build AI applications and agents on enterprise data.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: HTTP header insertion in Azure Firewall
items.description:
Azure Firewall now supports HTTP header insertion, enabling organizations to add or overwrite HTTP/HTTPS request headers directly from Azure Firewall application rules. This capability helps customers enforce security controls, support tenant restriction scenarios, integrate with backend services, and simplify application access management without relying on third-party proxies or on-premises infrastructure. 

The feature is especially useful for scenarios such as Microsoft Entra tenant restrictions, Azure Virtual Desktop, VDI, SaaS access control, and enterprise egress filtering. By enabling header insertion natively in Azure Firewall, customers can reduce proxy dependencies, avoid routing traffic back on premises solely for header injection, and improve operational efficiency.  

HTTP header insertion is supported in Azure Firewall Premium for HTTP traffic and HTTPS traffic decrypted using TLS Inspection. In Standard and Basic SKUs, it is supported for HTTP traffic. The feature can be configured through Azure Portal, Azure CLI, PowerShell, REST APIs, Terraform, and Azure Firewall Draft + Deploy. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: AI Gateway in Azure API Management
items.description:
The AI Gateway tier for Azure API Management is now available in public preview. Building on the AI gateway capabilities already available across API Management tiers, the new AI Gateway tier provides a dedicated experience optimized for AI workloads.
As organizations operationalize AI, platform teams need a consistent way to securely expose AI assets including AI models, MCP servers, and tools. AI Gateway helps organizations apply consistent security, policies, authentication, observability, and operational controls across AI workloads.

Built on the trusted, enterprise-grade Azure API Management platform, AI Gateway provides portal and programmatic experiences optimized for AI. The experience is centered on models, MCP servers, and tools, making it easier for platform teams to discover, expose, secure, and observe AI assets.

The public preview supports models hosted from Microsoft Foundry as well as models hosted in AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, OpenAI, and Anthropic. It also extends the same consistent controls to MCP servers, created from existing MCP backends, OpenAPI definitions, or connectors, with built-in policy enforcement, OpenTelemetry-based observability, and enterprise authentication.

Learn more: 

  • Announcement blog 
  • Documentation  
  • Build your first AI Gateway resource

items.title: Public Preview: Azure DDoS Protection custom policy
items.description:
Azure DDoS Protection custom policy is now in public preview. This capability provides per-resource control over DDoS mitigation thresholds for protected Standard Load Balancer frontend IP configurations. 

Customers can configure fixed inbound detection thresholds for TCP, UDP, and TCP SYN traffic. Thresholds can be set from 50,000 to 2,000,000 packets per second, helping customers account for predictable or unusual traffic patterns, including planned launches, seasonal peaks, gaming events, and sustained high-volume workloads. 

When a custom threshold is configured for a protocol, Azure uses that threshold instead of adaptive auto-tuning for that protocol. Protocols without a custom threshold continue to use Azure DDoS Protection’s adaptive auto-tuning. 

During public preview, customers can create and manage Custom Policy through the Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure Resource Manager templates, and the REST API. 

Custom policy currently supports inbound traffic for Standard Load Balancer frontend IP configurations. Regional availability is limited during the preview. 

Learn more:  

  • Read the custom policy overview 
  • Manage custom policy using the Azure portal 
  • Manage custom policy using Azure CLI 
  • Deploy custom policy using an ARM template

items.title: Public Preview: Standard service endpoint
items.description:
Standard service endpoint is now available in public preview, introducing a scalable and secure way to connect IaaS workloads to Azure PaaS services under the Private Link family. This enhanced capability overcomes the scale and management limitations of traditional service endpoints by integrating with network security perimeter and using Public IPs as network identifiers, enabling large‑scale IaaS‑to‑PaaS connectivity with stronger security controls.

With standard service endpoint, customers can associate a single public IP or prefix with multiple subnets or virtual networks across subscriptions within the same tenant and region. When combined with network security perimeter organizations can define a perimeter around supported PaaS resources—such as Azure Storage, Azure SQL, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure Key Vault—and restrict access so that only approved networks and workloads can communicate with those resources.

This public preview builds on extensive private preview validation with enterprise and partner customers, delivering improved reliability, simplified configuration while maintaining a strong security posture for large and complex Azure environments. Additionally, The feature has been battle tested for 1P as part of SFI program providing network identification for 42k+ VNets used by 1P service providers, 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Protect sensitive generative AI telemetry in Application Insights and Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Azure Monitor Application Insights now stores generative AI content in a dedicated GenAIContent table (AppGenAIContent in Log Analytics), making it possible to apply newly available access controls to sensitive AI telemetry. Because Application Insights powers observability in Microsoft Foundry, these protections benefit customers using either experience. 

Since these new protections are built into Log Analytics at the platform layer, they extend beyond just generative AI content. You can now easily configure any table in Azure Monitor to use a more restrictive role for data access.

Organizations can use these capabilities to help restrict access to prompts, responses, tool calls, and other AI-generated content that may contain sensitive information such as PII or PHI. This capability is especially relevant for customers in regulated industries such as healthcare, financial services, and government. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: IPv6 support for Azure VPN Gateway
items.description:
IPv6 support for Azure VPN Gateway enables customers to run IPv6 inner traffic through VPN tunnels in a dual‑stack configuration. IPv6 is supported on all production SKU gateways that use standard public IPs.IPv6 inner traffic can be configured for both new and existing VPN Gateway deployments in dual‑stack mode, enabling customers to support IPv4 and IPv6 workloads through the same gateway configuration.Site‑to‑Site VPN enables branch and on‑premises networks to connect to Azure over IPsec/IKE VPN tunnels with IPv6 traffic carried inside the tunnel.Point‑to‑Site VPN enables remote users to connect securely to Azure with IPv6 support in the client address pool and routed traffic configuration.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Functions support for Python 3.14
items.description:
You can now develop functions using Python 3.14 locally and deploy them to Azure Functions plans on Linux. 

Upgrade your apps to Python 3.14 to take advantage of enhanced security, a longer support window, and continued compatibility with the Azure Functions runtime and developer tools. 

Learn more:  

  • Upgrade your app to Python 3.14 
  • Python support in Azure Functions

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Functions Support for PowerShell 7.6
items.description:
Azure Functions support for PowerShell 7.6 is now available in preview. You can now develop apps using PowerShell 7.6 locally and deploy them to Azure Functions plans. 

Learn more:  

  • What's new in PowerShell 7.6 
  • Azure Functions PowerShell versions and their end of support dates

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Defender security assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
items.description:
Microsoft Defender Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server are now generally available. You can use assessments to continuously evaluate the security posture of your Azure PostgreSQL flexible servers and identify vulnerabilities and misconfigurations that may cause security risks. The assessments are tailored to PostgreSQL-specific security best practices and provide actionable recommendations to help you strengthen your security baseline, prioritize remediation efforts, and support compliance requirements. 

If you already have Microsoft Defender CSPM enabled for your Azure PostgreSQL flexible server, no additional setup is required to start using these assessments. An initial set of built-in assessments is available today, with additional assessment coverage planned for future releases. You can see all findings and recommendations in the Azure portal on the resource blade of your Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server or the main Defender for Cloud experience, and the Microsoft Defender portal.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Encryption in Transit for Azure Files NFS Shares in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
items.description:
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now generally supports Encryption in Transit (EiT) for Azure Files NFS v4.1 volumes through the Azure File CSI driver. With EiT enabled, data transferred between AKS workloads and Azure Files NFS shares is encrypted using TLS, helping customers meet security and compliance requirements for production workloads. The capability is integrated with the AZNFS mount helper and Stunnel and can be enabled through storage class configuration without requiring application changes. This capability is available in all Azure regions that support Azure Files Premium (SSD).

Learn more:  

  • Create and Manage Persistent Volumes with Azure Files in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
  • Redundancy support for SSD Azure file shares | Microsoft Learn 
  • How to Encrypt Data in Transit for NFS shares 
  • Use Container Storage Interface (CSI) Drivers on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

items.title: Announcing: Multi-agent orchestration patterns including Magentic in Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework reaches general availability for multi-agent orchestration patterns, including the dynamic Magentic pattern that delivered 38 percent on GAIA and competitive results on AssistantBench and WebArena in published benchmarks. The GA release covers sequential pipelines, parallel collaboration, and Magentic-style coordination, all expressed in the same framework API so teams can swap patterns without rewriting agent code. Customers running complex research, document processing, and operations workflows can now build specialist agents and let the framework handle planning, hand-off, and recovery. The release ships in .NET and Python through the framework on GitHub, with backward compatibility for the preview API and SLA-backed support for production deployments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing: Agent Harness in Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework reaches general availability for Agent Harness, the production runtime for agents built with the framework. Customers running pilots on the preview harness can now move the same agent code into production with backwards compatibility, SLA-backed support, and stable interfaces for tool calls, state, and telemetry. The GA release ships in .NET and Python, supports local development, container deployment, and Foundry Hosted Agents from one binary, and emits OpenTelemetry traces that show up in Foundry observability dashboards without custom wiring. Enterprise customers building internal copilots and customer-facing agents get a single supported runtime instead of stitching together orchestration, retries, and instrumentation. The framework remains open source on GitHub. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing: Multi-agent orchestration SDK with the Microsoft Foundry Agent Framework in C# and Python
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry is now introducing Agent Framework, a unified multi-agent orchestration SDK for C# and Python. This release consolidates patterns previously spread across AutoGen and Semantic Kernel, giving developers a consistent set of abstractions for building, coordinating, and deploying agents. The Microsoft Foundry Agent Framework reduces integration complexity, helps teams avoid conflicting libraries, and streamlines long-term maintenance by providing a single, well-supported model for multi-agent workloads. This release applies to scenarios that require deterministic coordination across tasks, tools, and models, while maintaining language parity for mixed-ecosystem teams. To start using the Microsoft Foundry Agent Framework, install the C# or Python packages and review the integration guidance. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing: Tracing for Microsoft Agent Framework (Python and .NET)
items.description:
In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now offers tracing for the Microsoft Agent Framework in both Python and .NET, helping developers observe how agents reason, call tools, and interact with models during execution. This release is part of the broader hosted agents update and emits OpenTelemetry-compatible spans that you can route to Application Insights or other compatible backends, making it easier to debug failures, identify latency hotspots, and validate behavior before deploying to production. The preview is intended for evaluation and may evolve as schemas, attributes, and sampling controls are finalized ahead of general availability. By giving early access to tracing, Microsoft Foundry helps teams accelerate innovation on multi-step agent workflows without building custom instrumentation. To get started, enable tracing in the Microsoft Agent Framework SDK for Python or .NET and connect your preferred OpenTelemetry exporter. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing: CodeAct pattern and Hyperlight containers in Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework adds the CodeAct pattern in public preview, which lets agents collapse a multi-step plan into a single executable code block rather than chaining one tool call at a time. In representative workloads, CodeAct cut end-to-end latency by roughly 50 percent and token use by more than 60 percent compared with step-by-step orchestration. The framework runs CodeAct programs inside Hyperlight, a Microsoft-built sandboxed container runtime that boots in milliseconds and isolates each execution from the host and from other agents. Developers get the productivity of letting the model write code without giving up the safety properties that enterprises require for production agents. Both capabilities ship through the framework on GitHub in .NET and Python. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing: Episodic procedural memory in Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework adds episodic procedural memory in public preview, a built-in store that lets agents remember successful task patterns and replay them on similar future requests. The framework records action sequences, tool selections, and intermediate decisions as episodes, then retrieves the closest match when a new user request looks similar. Agents become measurably faster and cheaper at recurring tasks because they reuse proven plans instead of re-deriving them from scratch on every run. The capability targets agent developers who currently bolt on custom caching layers or manual few-shot prompts to get this behavior. Episodic memory is configurable per agent, ships in .NET and Python through the framework on GitHub, and integrates with the existing tracing pipeline. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for mid-July 2026
items.description:
In mid-July 2026, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL: 

  • Shortcut Configuration lets you customize keyboard shortcuts for Quick Queries, the Results Grid, and the Query Editor directly within Visual Studio Code—without leaving your editor. You can execute queries, navigate more efficiently, and discover available commands more easily, helping you complete your data tasks faster.  
  • The new Results Grid introduces enhanced state management for improved performance and responsiveness, along with expanded column customization options. You can now freeze, hide, and show columns to better tailor the grid to your workflow. Try it now—enable the Beta Results Grid preview in MSSQL Settings.  

Learn more.

products: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
items.title: Generally Available: Expanding Azure Arc SQL Migration with SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
items.description:
The Azure Arc migration solution now supports SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines as a migration target. Arc-enabled SQL Server instances can now be migrated to both Azure SQL Managed Instance and SQL Server on Azure infrastructure using the same unified workflow.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Advanced platform metrics in Azure Monitor
items.description:
Starting July 15, 2026, advanced platform metrics are available in Public Preview. This update provides enhanced visibility into platform performance, resource health, and operational trends across supported Azure services. With advanced platform metrics, organizations can access additional telemetry and monitoring signals to help identify potential issues more quickly, improve troubleshooting efficiency, and gain deeper operational insights into their Azure environments. The preview enables customers to evaluate the new metrics experience and provide feedback before general availability. 

Learn more:
  • Public Preview: Advanced platform metrics in Azure Monitor
  • Advanced platform metrics (preview)
  • Advanced platform metrics for Azure Blob Storage (preview)

items.title: Announcing: DevUI Agent Inspector for Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework adds DevUI Agent Inspector in public preview, a local debugging surface that shows agent runs as a navigable tree of model calls, tool invocations, and intermediate state. Developers can pause, replay, and edit prompts mid-run, swap models without restarting, and inspect the full payload sent to each tool. The inspector reads the same OpenTelemetry traces that Foundry observability consumes, so what you see locally matches what shows up in production dashboards. DevUI runs as a sidecar process on a developer workstation and connects to agents built with the framework in .NET or Python. The preview is aimed at agent developers who currently rely on log scraping and ad-hoc print statements. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Front Door edge actions
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of Azure Front Door edge actions (serverless compute at the edge).

With edge actions, customers can execute lightweight JavaScript functions during Azure Front Door request processing to make real-time decisions closer to users, improving performance, security, and application flexibility without adding complexity to origin infrastructure.

Common scenarios include A/B testing and canary deployments, header manipulation, request filtering, dynamic origin selection, URL rewrites, authentication at the edge and many more. 

Edge actions integrate seamlessly with Azure Front Door capabilities such as rules engine, caching, routing, and Web Application Firewall (WAF). Built on Hyperlight, Microsoft’s secure micro-VM technology, edge actions provide hardware-backed isolation for customer code execution.

Learn more:

  • Blog announcement 
  • Azure Front Door edge actions documentation

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Databricks SQL Serverless in UK West
items.description:
Starting July 13th, 2026, customers can use Azure Databricks SQL Serverless in the UK West region to simplify analytics workloads while benefiting from instant compute, automated scaling, and reduced infrastructure management.  

Eligible UK West workspaces will see Serverless selected as the default option when creating new SQL warehouses in the Azure Databricks workspace UI. Classic and Pro warehouse options will continue to be available, providing customers with flexibility to choose the warehouse type that best meets their requirements.  

Users with permissions to create SQL warehouses can provision serverless warehouses in eligible workspaces. Availability depends on workspace eligibility requirements, and some workspaces may not have Databricks SQL Serverless enabled by default. Review workspace eligibility requirements and account terms of use. Before creating or upgrading to a serverless warehouse, review the applicable Azure Databricks pricing and billing information for your account.   

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Support for Python-2.7; 3.8 and PowerShell- 7.1; 7.2 will be retired on September 30, 2026
items.description:
Starting October 1, 2026, the specified runtime versions Python 2.7, Python 3.8, and PowerShell 7.1 & 7.2. will no longer be supported by Automation.  

Runbooks using these versions may continue to run but will not receive security updates, bug fixes, or official support.

Recommended action: 

To minimize security risks and take advantage of the latest features and improvements, it is strongly recommended upgrading your runbooks to supported runtime versions of Python and PowerShell.  

You can refer to the following support lifecycle resources for guidance and upgrade to latest versions  

  • PowerShell Support Lifecycle  
  • Python Version Support Status  

Upgrading is required to maintain support eligibility and ensure continued access to security updates and platform features. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Manage Azure Chaos Studio from the Azure CLI
items.description: You can now create and run Azure Chaos Studio resilience Scenarios directly from the Azure CLI with the new az chaos extension — no more hand-assembling REST calls and JSON files. Get started in one step: az chaos setup stands up a workspace, wires up permissions, discovers your resources, and recommends Scenarios (like Zone Down) tailored to what you're running. From there, configure, validate, and run a Scenario in a few clear commands — with built-in --help, tab completion, and table/JSON/TSV output. Install with az extension add --name chaos.

items.title: Generally Available: Open AI GPT-5.6 on Azure Databricks
items.description:
Open AI GPT-5.6 is now available on Azure Databricks. You can use GPT 5.6 (purchased on Microsoft Foundry) via Model Serving Endpoint in Azure Databricks. Through integrations across Foundry and Azure Databricks, you can securely build, deploy, and manage AI applications in the context of their data while enforcing governance via Unity AI Gateway.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Exceptions in WAF for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door
items.description:
Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) helps protect your web applications from common threats and attacks. In some cases, WAF may block requests that are safe and expected for your application. Existing exclusions help reduce false positives by omitting specific request attributes, such as headers, cookies, query string arguments, or body fields, from WAF evaluation while the rest of the request continues to be inspected.

Exceptions provide additional flexibility by allowing specific requests to bypass WAF inspection at the rule, rule group, or managed ruleset level. Exceptions can be defined using request URI, remote IP address, or request header name and value, helping customers tune WAF policies more precisely while keeping other protections active.

To configure Exceptions, navigate to your WAF policy in the Azure portal, select Managed rules, and then add an exception. 

Learn more: 

  • Application Gateway documentation 
  • Front Door documentation

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Chaos Studio Workspaces and Scenarios
items.description:
Azure Chaos Studio now supports Workspaces and Scenarios, a faster, application-centric way to validate how your workloads hold up during real outages.

Point a Workspace at your application's scope—a subscription, resource group, or service group—and Chaos Studio discovers the resources inside it and recommends Scenarios: preconfigured tests that reproduce real-world outage patterns. Select a Scenario, and Chaos Studio injects the right faults, in the right order, across every affected resource, then produces a Scenario report showing exactly what happened.

With Workspaces and Scenarios, you can:

  • Simulate common outage patterns out of the box, including availability zone failures, DNS and Microsoft Entra ID outages, PostgreSQL and SQL Managed Instance failovers, cache stampedes, and messaging disruptions.
  • Keep tests in sync as your app changes—resources are discovered automatically from the Workspace scope.
  • Control the blast radius with a managed identity governed by Azure RBAC.
  • Generate Scenario reports for game days, retrospectives, and compliance frameworks such as DORA.
Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Export historical data from Log Analytics workspace with Export jobs
items.description:
The Log Analytics Export job enables you to export historical data from a Log Analytics workspace to an Azure Storage account based on a specified query and time range. This allows you to extract only the data you need and move it to external systems for further processing or long-term retention.  

Key scenarios include: 

  • Compliance and audit – Export data from specific time periods to support audit requests, legal holds, and regulatory requirements. 
  • Security investigations – Extract relevant datasets for forensic analysis or integration with third-party SIEM solutions.  
  • Advanced analytics and machine learning – Use exported datasets to build and train models in external environments.  
  • Business intelligence and reporting – Combine exported logs with other data sources to enable reporting and analytics across your organization.  
  • Data migration – Move data out of Log Analytics for use in other platforms or long-term storage. 

 Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Network Security Perimeter support for Azure Event Hubs
items.description:
Azure Event Hubs now supports Network Security Perimeter (NSP), enabling organizations to define a logical network isolation boundary for PaaS resources and control public network access through perimeter-based access rules.

With Network Security Perimeter, you can help reduce data exfiltration risks by restricting access to Event Hubs namespaces and managing inbound and outbound connectivity using centralized security controls. This capability complements existing network security features and helps organizations implement consistent network isolation policies across Azure services.
Network Security Perimeter support for Event Hubs enables you to:
  1. Define secure network boundaries around Event Hubs resources.
  2. Control public access using perimeter access rules.
  3. Reduce exposure to unauthorized network traffic.
  4. Apply consistent network security policies across supported Azure services.
This capability is now generally available for Azure Event Hubs.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Confidential Computing support for Azure Event Hubs Dedicated
items.description:
Azure Event Hubs Dedicated now supports Confidential Computing, enabling organizations to protect streaming data while it is being processed in memory. By leveraging hardware-based trusted execution environments (TEEs), customers can help safeguard sensitive event-streaming workloads against unauthorized access, including access to data in use.

This capability is designed for organizations with heightened security, privacy, and compliance requirements, allowing them to process highly sensitive streaming data with additional protection throughout the data lifecycle. Confidential Computing support for Event Hubs Dedicated helps customers strengthen their security posture while maintaining the scale and performance benefits of a dedicated Event Hubs environment.

This feature is available for Azure Event Hubs Dedicated customers. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Red Hat OpenShift in Chile Central
items.description:
Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) is now generally available in Azure Chile Central, expanding regional availability for OpenShift deployments across South America. With the launch of Microsoft’s first Azure region in Chile, customers can now run fully managed OpenShift clusters closer to their users and data, improving performance and reducing latency for cloud-native applications. 

This new region enables organizations to deploy Kubernetes-based workloads while meeting local data residency and regulatory requirements. Built with multiple availability zones, Chile Central supports resilient, production-grade architectures for mission-critical applications running on ARO. Customers can take advantage of consistent OpenShift operations across hybrid and multi-cloud environments, while benefiting from Azure-native integration and enterprise-grade support. 

The availability of ARO in Chile Central provides a strong foundation for regulated industries and enterprises that require in-country infrastructure. It also supports modern application development patterns, including AI-enabled and data-intensive workloads, with improved proximity, control, and scalability.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Entra ID-based access for Azure Blob Storage SFTP
items.description:
Microsoft Entra ID-based access for Azure Blob Storage SFTP is now generally available in all regions. You can now use Entra ID identities including guest users via Entra External Identities to securely connect to Azure Blob Storage over SFTP, without provisioning or managing local SFTP users.

Why it matters

  • Eliminates the operational overhead of managing local SFTP users and credentials.
  • Strengthens security with Entra ID authentication, MFA, and Conditional Access.
  • Accelerates onboarding and enables secure external collaboration with partners and vendors via Entra External Identities (B2B).

Key capabilities

  • Single Sign-On and Multi-Factor Authentication using existing corporate credentials.
  • Conditional Access policies based on user location, device compliance, sign-in risk, and other signals.
  • Unified identity lifecycle — SFTP access is automatically updated or revoked through your existing identity governance processes.
  • Native Azure RBAC, ABAC, and ACL integration — SFTP honors the same authorization model as the REST API, Azure CLI, and other data-plane access methods.

New in GA

  • ABAC + Storage Blob Data Owner: resolved an inconsistency that could cause timeouts when combining ABAC conditions with the Storage Blob Data Owner role.
  • ABAC sub-operations: added support for sub-operations, enabling finer-grained conditional access.

items.title: Generally Available: Support 5x churn in Azure Site Recovery
items.description:
Azure Site Recovery now supports up to 5x churn (500 MB/s per VM). This major enhancement empowers customers to confidently run high IOPS workloads with Azure Site Recovery, ensuring robust disaster recovery for even the most demanding applications like databases, big data and analytics systems, etc. 

Learn More.

items.title: Generally available: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5 on Azure Databricks
items.description:
Azure Databricks now supports Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5 through Azure Databricks AI Model Serving. Claude Sonnet 5 is Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet model to date, delivering near-Opus-level intelligence with Sonnet's cost efficiency and speed. Designed for coding, agentic workflows, and professional work at scale, it is a hybrid reasoning model with adaptive thinking on by default. Claude Sonnet 5's largest gains are in coding and agentic tasks, making it ideal for teams building long-running AI agents, automating multi-file software development, and running high-volume professional workflows where both quality and cost efficiency matter. The model runs securely within the Azure Databricks environment, with access available through pay-per-token Foundation Model APIs. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms. 

Learn More

items.title: Generally Available: New Powershell module:  Az.PostgreSQLFlexibleServer
items.description:
We’re excited to introduce the newly renamed Az.PostgreSQLFlexibleServer PowerShell module, delivering a more streamlined experience for you to manage Azure Database for PostgreSQL with PowerShell. Building on the capabilities of the previous Az.PostgreSql module, the updated module aligns with the new features in the 2026-01-01 preview REST API.

This module brings support for PostgreSQL 18, elastic clusters for scalable workloads, and several enhancements designed to simplify management and improve operational efficiency. Whether you’re provisioning new deployments or managing complex environments, this module enables you to take full advantage of the latest platform capabilities directly from PowerShell.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Document PII playground sample in Microsoft Foundry NextGen
items.description:
Document-based PII detection in Azure AI Language now ships an initial playground experience in the Microsoft Foundry NextGen portal. The playground loads a prepared sample document, runs it through the document-based PII feature, and shows the redacted output side by side with the source so you can see entity categories, confidence scores, and the resulting file fidelity before integrating the API. This first cut focuses on the built-in sample to make first-touch evaluation fast; configuration of your own files and entity selection lands in the upcoming API configuration panel release. The capability uses the existing asynchronous native-file PII pipeline. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Document PII NextGen Playground in Azure AI Language
items.description:
Azure AI Language now offers a refreshed Document PII playground in general availability, giving customers a faster way to evaluate personally identifiable information detection on documents. The playground ships with curated sample inputs and outputs, so practitioners can see how the service handles names, addresses, financial IDs, and health identifiers without uploading their own data first. Reviewers can compare detection results across entity types in a single view, then move to live document uploads when they are ready to test on real content. This release helps compliance, legal, and data protection teams scope a PII redaction project in minutes rather than days. The playground uses the same Document PII model and policies as the production API, so what reviewers see is what they get. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Instant Access via application consistent restore points
items.description:
Azure introduces Instant Access for VM Restore Points, enabling you to restore disks immediately after a restore point is created—without waiting for background data replication.

Key benefits:
  • Faster recovery (lower RTO): Restore disks instantly—no wait for data hydration.
  • High performance from the start: Restored disks are usable immediately while data copies in the background.
  • Consistent recovery: Application-consistent restore points ensure reliable recovery across all VM disks.
  • Flexible controls: Enable Instant Access and configure duration per restore point or collection.
How it works:
  • Create restore points with Instant Access enabled
  • Restore disks immediately after creation
  • Data continues to hydrate in the background for long-term durability
Pricing:

Public Preview: No additional charges apply when using Instant Access. Standard billing for disks and snapshots remains unchanged.  Post General Availability (GA): Two charges will apply:  
  • Storage Charge: Billed only for the additional storage space consumed by Instant Access Snapshots, based on data changes on the source disk after the snapshot is created.  
  • Restore Charge: A one-time fee applies for each disk restored from an Instant Access Snapshot, calculated based on the disk’s provisioned size at the time of restore.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Storage Mover now supports migration from Google Cloud Storage (GCS)
items.description:
Azure Storage Mover now supports cloud-to-cloud migration of data from Google Cloud Storage (GCS) to Azure Blob Storage, helping organizations simplify multi-cloud consolidation onto Azure.

Using the S3-compatible interface, customers can migrate data from GCS buckets through a fully managed, agentless experience with HMAC credentials stored securely in Azure Key Vault, no custom tooling required. For workloads with strict security and compliance needs, migrations can run over private network connections using Azure Private Link and Private Service Connect, keeping data off the public internet and within trusted network boundaries.

With this update, enterprises can consolidate their cloud storage into Azure securely and at scale, reducing operational overhead while meeting their network isolation requirements. Get started migrating your cloud data to Azure.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Client-side data integrity protections in Azure Blob Storage
items.description:
Azure Blob Storage has long supported data integrity validation, starting with MD5 as part of the original HTTP standards and adding CRC64-NVME support in 2019. Today, CRC64-NVME is now integrated into the latest Azure Blob SDKs for .NET, C++, and JavaScript, extending Azure's data integrity protections all the way into client applications. By extending data protection into client applications, customers can verify end-to-end that data written to and read from Blob Storage remains fully intact—byte-for-byte—from the application layer to Azure’s underlying physical storage, using CRC64-NVME checksums. To get started, upgrade to the latest .NET, C++, or JavaScript SDK.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry brings Toolboxes to GA, providing a unified endpoint to invoke the most-used tools in prompt agents and callable outside of prompt agents. Today every agent team hand-assembles its own tool list to solve the same tasks, with no shared artifact to reuse across agents and no agreed way to consume a set of governed tools. Toolboxes provide that artifact: a curated, governed bundle of tools built once in the Foundry portal or in code, configured with governance policies, and reusable across an organization. The tools agents need span MCP servers, REST APIs, skills, and connectors, each with its own protocol and auth model. Toolboxes expose all of them through a single MCP-compatible endpoint so developers stop writing per-tool integration code and admins keep consistent governance over what agents can call. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Migrate from Azure Blueprints by January 31, 2027
items.description:
In September 2023, we announced Azure Blueprints would retire on July 11, 2026. We're extending that timeline to January 31, 2027, with phased retirement beginning July 31, 2026.


What's changing?


July 31, 2026, you won't be able to create new blueprint definitions and versions.

October 31, 2026, you won't be able to modify blueprint definitions or create new blueprint assignments.

December 31, 2026, you won't be able to modify existing blueprint assignments.

When Azure Blueprints retires on January 31, 2027:

  • The API will no longer respond.
  • Azure CLI and PowerShell commands will stop functioning.
  • Azure Blueprints will be removed from the Azure portal.
  • Blueprint definitions, versions, or assignments not exported will be automatically deleted.
  • The blueprint locks "Do Not Delete" and "Read Only" on your resources will stop functioning, effectively setting them to a "Don't Lock" state.
  • Resources you've created through blueprints won't be deleted.

Recommended action

To avoid disruptions, act ahead of the phased retirement dates above. Migrate to Azure deployment stacks for resource grouping, lifecycle, and "deny assignments" enforcement. Publish definitions as template specs or store them in a template folder in Git for versioning. Go to the Blueprints portal to identify your impacted blueprint artifacts and export your data before January 31, 2027.

If you don't take action, Azure Blueprints functionality will decrease as the retirement phases progress but your resources will remain.

items.title: Public Preview: Application Gateway for Containers – Inference gateway
items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers is extending its ingress gateway feature set with new AI gateway capabilities. The new inference gateway capability brings the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension to Application Gateway for Containers, enabling load and model-aware routing for self-hosted generative AI workloads on AKS.

Application Gateway for Containers' inference gateway capability is purpose-built for serving LLMs and other inference workloads, routing requests based on model server signals rather than generic load balancing — improving Time to First Token (TTFT) and reducing timeouts under load.

  • Managed Body-Based Router (BBR): A fully managed router that inspects the request body (such as the model field on OpenAI-compatible APIs) to drive model-aware routing — no custom proxy tier required.
  • Bring your own Endpoint Picker (EPP): Choose the EPP implementation that fits your workload to drive metrics-aware endpoint selection across your InferencePool.
  • Secure inference: Pairs natively with the existing web application firewall (WAF) capability in Application Gateway for Containers, applying OWASP-aligned protections to AI traffic before it reaches your model servers.
  • Improved performance and reliability: Routes around saturated replicas and leverages model server state to lower TTFT, reduce timeouts, and improve GPU utilization.

Learn more:

  • Application Gateway for Containers – AI gateway - Inference gateway
  • Application Gateway for Containers - Overview

items.title: Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files migration assistant
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files migration assistant (with SnapMirror) provides efficient and cost-effective data migration leveraging ONTAP's built-in replication engine for seamless transition from on-premises or CVO/other cloud providers to Azure NetApp Files (ANF). This feature offers benefits aligned with the goal to accelerate and simplify migrations of business-critical applications and data to Azure. The feature is now available in Azure Portal and API experiences,and is now Generally Available in all regions.

Key Benefits

  • Storage-efficient data transfer that reduces network transfer costs for both baseline and incremental updates

  • Low cutover/downtime window ensuring faster and more efficient final updates, minimizing disruption to customer operations

  • Volume migration using migration assistant includes source volume snapshots for primary data protection, and directory and file metadata maintaining security attributes

Learn more:

  • What’s new

  • Migrate volumes to Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Databricks natively storing data in Microsoft OneLake
items.description:
Azure Databricks can now natively write managed Delta tables to Microsoft OneLake. This capability enables customers to use OneLake as a unified storage layer for Azure Databricks workloads without managing separate storage accounts. 

By storing data directly in OneLake, organizations can maintain a single copy of data that can be accessed across Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databricks, reducing duplication and simplifying data management.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Databricks native read access to Microsoft OneLake
items.description:
Azure Databricks now supports native read access to data stored in Microsoft OneLake through Unity Catalog. This capability is generally available. 

Customers can query and analyze data directly in OneLake without moving or copying data, enabling faster access to insights while simplifying cross-platform data access and governance. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Migrate – GitHub Copilot Modernization integration for at scale code assessments
items.description:
Azure Migrate now integrates with GitHub Copilot Modernization (public preview) to deliver at scale code insights. This capability brings together Azure Migrate’s portfolio-level discovery and assessment with GitHub Copilot’s context-aware code analysis. The shared workflow helps migration admins and app developers collaborate more effectively while adhering to organizational security guidelines. Teams can assess multiple applications at once, evaluate Azure compatibility, and make informed refactor-versus-replatform decisions. They can also act on code-fix recommendations and effort estimates to plan modernization with greater confidence and predictability. 

Key benefits:

  • Assess applications at scale: Run Modernize CLI assessments across multiple applications and repositories simultaneously, eliminating repetitive per-app analysis. 
  • Significantly reduce analysis time: AI-driven contextual code changes across large, complex codebases. 
  • Data-driven Refactor versus Replatform decisions: Code insights from GitHub Copilot surface directly inside Azure Migrate, so migration admins and developers work from the same source of truth. 
  • Actionable remediation guidance: Surfaces remediation guidance to fix the issues and make the application ready for Azure.  
  • Plan with confidence: Effort estimates and cloud readiness let teams prioritize workloads and set realistic timelines. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: ICMP Support for Azure Standard V2 NAT Gateway
items.description:
Azure StandardV2 NAT Gateway now supports outbound ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply traffic, enabling customers to use tools such as ping to quickly validate outbound connectivity and troubleshoot network issues from workloads behind StandardV2 NAT Gateway. This support extends to IPv4 and IPv6 for existing and new StandardV2 SKU NAT Gateways. 

Learn more:   

  • ICMP Ping Support through Azure NAT Gateway  
  • Azure NAT Gateway overview  
  • Troubleshoot Azure NAT Gateway

items.title: Public Preview: New project templates and template gallery for Azure Functions in VS Code
items.description:
The Azure Functions extension for VS Code now provides a redesigned Create New Project experience in public preview, featuring a rich, visual template gallery that replaces the multi-step Quick Pick wizard with a searchable, filterable view of project templates. Developers can browse templates by language and use case, search across template names, descriptions, and tags, and start from featured templates. A "Generate with Copilot" mode lets developers describe what they want to build and get a project scaffold generated for them. 

The gallery is populated from a continuously updated, Microsoft-curated catalog of 75+ ready-to-deploy samples that have recently been refreshed across all supported languages, covering common scenarios such as HTTP APIs, event-driven processing, scheduled jobs, data integration, Durable Functions orchestrations, MCP servers, and AI and agent workloads. 

The release also improves the Run Function App experience with smart, runtime-specific pre-start steps that automatically prepare the project — installing dependencies and building the app as needed — before launching the local runtime, so developers can go from create to running in a single click. 

 Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Log Analytics Summary Rules experience
items.description:
A new Azure portal experience for Summary Rules in Log Analytics is now available. 

Summary Rules enable aggregation of high-volume log data at a defined cadence and store it in summarized tables for improved query performance, reporting, or enhanced data privacy. Also, you can ingest logs at lower tier and summarize the important data you need in Analytics tier.

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: GPv1 and Legacy Blob storage account creation
items.description:
As part of our ongoing efforts to streamline the Azure Storage portfolio and deliver enhanced performance, scalability, and cost efficiency, we are announcing the retirement of all General purpose v1 (GPv1) storage accounts. This includes legacy blob storage and Files accounts configurations. 

Key Dates: 

  • October 1st, 2025: Public announcement. 
  • September 1st, 2026: New account creation blocked 
  • October 13th, 2026: Final retirement. All remaining GPv1 accounts will be transitioned to GPv2. 

What’s Changing: 

The following account types will be retired: 

  • General purpose v1 (GPv1) storage accounts (all redundancy options) 
  • Legacy blob storage accounts. 
  • Files storage accounts hosted on GPv1. 

Customers are encouraged to migrate to General Purpose v2 (GPv2) or specialized alternatives such as BlockBlobStorage or FileStorage, depending on workload requirements. 

Automatic migration warning:

After October 13, 2026, all existing GPv1 accounts will be auto migrated over to a GPv2 account, which may result in higher billing costs. Your decision not to migrate an existing GPv1 account will be construed as consent for Microsoft to migrate the account on your behalf. 

Learn more: 

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade  
  • GPv1 storage account retirement overview - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn 
  • Legacy Blob Storage account retirement overview - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Retirement: D-series, Ds-series, Dv2-series, Dsv2-series, and Ls-series Virtual Machines for Azure Batch pools
items.description:
Azure Compute will retire the following Virtual Machine series on May 1, 2028, impacting Azure Batch pools that rely on them:

  • D-series, Ds-series
  • Dv2-series, Dsv2-series
  • Ls-series

After this date:

  • New Batch pools using these VM series cannot be created
  • Existing pools cannot scale out
  • Pools may be forcibly resized to zero nodes
  • Remaining VMs will be stopped/deallocated and no longer covered by SLA

Timeline

  • Now – May 1, 2028: Existing pools continue to run; migration is recommended
  • May 1, 2028: Full retirement; affected pools may become unusable

Required action
Migrate your Batch pools to supported VM families before the retirement date to avoid disruption.

Recommended replacements:

  • For general-purpose pools (D/Ds/Dv2/Dsv2): Dsv5/Ddsv5 or Dasv5/Dadsv5; or Dsv6/Ddsv6 / Dasv6/Dadsv6 for NVMe workloads
  • For storage-optimized pools (Ls): Lsv3/Lasv3 or Lsv4/Lasv4

Migration options:

  1. Scale pool to zero and update VM size using Batch API (2024-07-01 or later)
  2. Create a new pool with supported VM sizes and migrate workloads

Note: VM pricing may change after migration. Refer to Azure VM pricing for details.

items.title: Retirement: Av2-series, F-series, Fs-series, Fsv2-series, G-series, Gs-series, and Lsv2-series Virtual Machines for Azure Batch pools
items.description:
Azure Compute will retire the following Virtual Machine series on November 15, 2028, impacting Azure Batch pools that rely on them:
  • Av2-series
  • F-series, Fs-series, Fsv2-series
  • G-series, Gs-series
  • Lsv2-series

After this date:

  • New Batch pools using these VM series cannot be created
  • Existing pools cannot scale out
  • Pools may be forcibly resized to zero nodes
  • Remaining VMs will be stopped/deallocated and no longer covered by SLA

Timeline:

  • Now – November 15, 2028: Existing pools continue to run; migration is recommended
  • November 15, 2028: Full retirement; affected pools may become unusable

Required action:
Migrate your Batch pools to supported VM families before the retirement date to avoid disruption.

Recommended replacements:

  • Av2 → Dsv5/Ddsv5 or Dasv5/Dadsv5
  • F/Fs/Fsv2 → Dlsv6/Dldsv6, Falsv6, or Dsv5/Ddsv5
  • G/Gs → Lsv3/Lasv3 or Easv5/Edsv5
  • Lsv2 → Lsv3/Lasv3

Migration options:

  1. Scale pool to zero and update VM size using Batch API (07-01-24 or later)
  2. Create a new pool with supported VM sizes and migrate workloads

Note: VM pricing may change after migration. Refer to Azure VM pricing for details.

items.title: Generally Available: SQL MCP Server
items.description:
SQL MCP Server is now generally available, giving customers a secure, high-performance way to build agentic solutions with controlled access to production data. Built for SQL and compatible with PostgreSQL and Azure Cosmos DB, SQL MCP Server is a dynamic, self-hosted data-plane endpoint with caching, multiple data sources, REST, and GraphQL in one solution. Open source and free, it runs well in Azure, on-premises, or in any cloud. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Azure Load Balancer Inbound NAT rule version 1 for Azure VMSS (aka Inbound NAT Pools)
items.description:
Update to our previous communication: We previously announced the retirement of all Inbound NAT rules version 1 resources, which included both single-VM NAT rules and NAT pools for Virtual Machine Scale Sets. We have narrowed the scope of this retirement to Inbound NAT pools only. 

NAT pools are being retired because they provide the same functionality as Inbound NAT rules v2, which offer improved performance and is the recommended option for Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS). 

Understanding the difference: 

Inbound NAT rules version 1 includes two resource types: 

  • Inbound NAT rules version 1: Port forwarding to a single virtual machine. This feature is not affected. 
  • Inbound NAT pools: Port forwarding to Virtual Machine Scale Set instances. This feature is retiring. 

On September 30, 2027, Inbound NAT pools in Azure Load Balancer will be retired. Starting November 15, 2026, you will no longer be able to create new Inbound NAT pools. Existing configuration will continue to function until September 30, 2027. 

Recommended action: 

To avoid potential service disruptions, we recommend that you migrate to Inbound NAT rules version 2 in Azure Load Balancer by September 30, 2027.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Entra server principals on Azure SQL Database
items.description:
Microsoft Entra server principals (logins) for Azure SQL Database is now generally available. You can now use CREATE LOGIN ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER in the virtual master database, bringing parity with SQL logins for your Microsoft Entra identities.

With Entra logins, you can assign server roles to Entra principals, automate user and database provisioning using service principal logins, and enable Entra-only authentication to disable SQL authentication entirely. If you're already using Entra logins on Azure SQL Managed Instance or SQL Server 2022, you now get the same experience on Azure SQL Database. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL
items.description:
