As of March 31, 2026, new Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL accounts can no longer enable Azure Synapse Link. Existing customers will remain fully supported until March 31, 2029, when Azure Synapse Link will reach end of life.

We encourage all customers to begin migrating to Mirroring for Microsoft Fabric — the recommended go-forward solution for Cosmos DB analytics workloads.

Mirroring for Microsoft Fabric delivers the same zero-ETL hybrid transactional and analytical processing (HTAP) capabilities as Azure Synapse Link, with meaningful improvements:

  • Open Delta Parquet format stored in Microsoft Fabric OneLake — accessible by Fabric Spark, Fabric SQL, Power BI Direct Lake, Azure Databricks, and more

  • No schema nesting limits — removes the 1,000 property and 127-level depth restrictions of Synapse Link

  • Free replication storage — mirrored data storage is included at no cost up to your Fabric capacity limit (e.g. F64 = 64 TB of free OneLake storage)

  • Free replication compute — data replication does not consume Request Units (RUs) or impact transactional performance

  • Full Microsoft Fabric ecosystem integration — unified data management across OneLake, enabling AI and analytics scenarios at scale

To get started with migration, visit Cosmos Mirror Synapse Migration. 

If you have questions about this retirement or your migration path, please contact your Microsoft account manager or reach out directly at cosmosdbsynapselink@microsoft.com

items.title: Retirement: Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) will be retired on August 31, 2026
items.description:
The Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) has remained in public preview and does not have a path to general availability (GA). 

As part of our ongoing efforts to align Azure networking services with current security and reliability standards, this preview client will be retired.

Timeline and Impact: 

  • August 31, 2026 – Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) is retired

  • September 1, 2026 – The Linux preview client is no longer supported for Azure VPN Gateway Point-to-Site (P2S) connections

After August 31, 2026, connections using the Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) may fail, which could result in loss of access to Azure resources through Point-to-Site (P2S) VPN connections.  

Recommended action:

To help ensure uninterrupted connectivity, transition your Azure VPN Gateway Point-to-Site (P2S) configuration to support alternative Linux VPN clients and distribute said clients to users before September 1, 2026.

For guidance on supported Point‑to‑Site VPN options and configuration steps, see the Azure VPN Gateway documentation.  

Risk/mitigation:

Update your VPN gateway configuration and your end-user clients through your standard change management process to minimize user disruption.

Help and Support :

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A  If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support request.

items.title: Public Preview: Agent mode for GitHub Copilot in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
items.description:
You can now use Agent mode for GitHub Copilot in SSMS to work with your database: investigating performance problems, tuning queries, reviewing maintenance and configuration, identifying security concerns, troubleshooting errors, and assisting with operational workflows.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: PostgreSQL Hub for Azure Developers
items.description:
PostgreSQL Hub for Azure Developers brings together key AI and application development resources for PostgreSQL on Azure. It includes curated sample apps and solution accelerators, tutorials, and structured learning pathways to help you build everything from core applications to AI agents. Featured resources stay current with the latest updates.

The hub also provides a space to connect with other developers. You can start discussions, share knowledge, and collaborate more closely with Microsoft and ecosystem experts as the community continues to grow.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure NC RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition v6 Series Virtual Machines
items.description:
Azure NCv6-series virtual machines (VMs) are now generally available in the Azure Southeast Asia and West US 2 regions. NCv6 VMs are powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition graphics processing units (GPUs) with each GPU featuring 96 GB of GDDR7 memory, and enable both leading-edge graphics and generative artificial intelligence (AI) compute workloads. The VM host is equipped with Intel Xeon™ 6 "Granite Rapids" 6900P series central processing units (CPUs), providing all-core turbo frequencies up to 4.2 GHz for demanding pre- and post-processing steps.  

NCv6 offers fractional GPU support and general purpose and compute optimized VM sizes. The general purpose NCv6 VM sizes provide larger amounts of CPU memory for demanding generative AI inference and independent software vendor (ISV) computer-aided design (CAD)/computer-aided engineering (CAE) simulations, while the compute optimized NCv6 VM sizes offer reduced memory to enable customers with less memory intensive workloads to cost optimize their deployments. 

Note: For customers using the NCv6-series VMs under public preview, please see here for guidance on how to navigate the preview to general availability transition.

items.title: Generally Available: Premium SSD v2 disks now support non-zonal Azure Virtual Machines
items.description:
Azure Premium SSD v2 disks now support non-zonal, single-instance Azure virtual machines in select Azure regions with Availability Zones (AZs). Customers can now deploy Premium SSD v2 with non-zonal virtual machines without selecting an Availability Zone. This allows customers to bring the performance and price benefits of Premium SSD v2 to workloads that have not transitioned to zonal configurations. 

Azure Premium SSD v2 is a next-generation block storage option for Azure virtual machines that delivers sub-millisecond latency and strong price performance for IO-intensive workloads such as SQL Server, Oracle, SAP, Cassandra, MongoDB, big data and analytics, and gaming workloads running on virtual machines or stateful containers. 

Pricing for non-zonal Premium SSD v2 disks is the same as zonal Premium SSD v2 disks. Customers pay for provisioned storage capacity, along with any additional IOPS and throughput provisioned above the baseline performance.   

Learn more:     

  • Documentation  
  • Premium SSD v2 Disk Storage pricing.

items.title: Generally Available: Maintenance control for Azure Database for PostgreSQL - reschedule, apply on demand, view and download
items.description:
Enhanced maintenance control capabilities are now generally available for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. These new capabilities give you greater visibility and flexibility in managing platform maintenance events, helping reduce disruption to your workloads. You can now view upcoming maintenance events directly in the Azure portal, CLI, and APIs, including details such as maintenance type, expected downtime, and deferral eligibility. With the ability to reschedule maintenance by up to 14 days, you can align updates with your business schedules and avoid peak usage periods. Additionally, you can choose to apply maintenance on demand at a time that works best for your environment, improving predictability and control. These enhancements eliminate the need for support requests to defer maintenance and help reduce the risk of unexpected downtime, making it easier to operate production workloads with confidence. These capabilities are available in all regions where Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is offered. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Site Recovery support for Linux Azure VMs with NVMe disk controllers.
items.description:
Azure Site Recovery now supports replication and disaster recovery for Linux Azure Virtual Machines running on NVMe-enabled Generation 2 VM families, such as the Da/Ea/Fa v6-series and Ebsv5/Ebdsv5 in the Azure-to-Azure scenario. This support is limited to RHEL 9, SLES 15 and Ubuntu 24 distros of Linux. 

This enhancement allows customers to enable disaster recovery and replication for their Azure VMs running high-performance, I/O-intensive workloads (limited to ASR churn support) with the NVMe disk controller. This capability is supported across all Azure public cloud regions.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Foundry agent security capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Cloud are transitioning to a Microsoft Agent 365 license
items.description:
Starting July 1, 2026, Microsoft Foundry agent security capabilities previously available through Microsoft Defender for Cloud will transition to a Microsoft Agent 365 license. Agent protection in Defender will be powered by Agent 365 observability logs and the Microsoft 365 agent registry — providing a unified source of truth for Microsoft Foundry agent inventory, real-time threat protection through a unified blocking platform, and consistent posture across cloud environments. 

For tenants with an Agent 365-eligible license, these experiences will continue to be available through the Microsoft Defender portal. Equivalent Microsoft Foundry agent experiences currently available in Azure portal experiences are migrating to the Microsoft Defender portal for all customers. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Managed Redis now supports Entra ID based RBAC for data management
items.description:
With role-based access control (RBAC) for Azure Managed Redis data access, you can precisely control who can read, write, or administer your Redis data using Microsoft Entra ID—without relying on shared keys. Built on top of Redis Access Control Lists (ACLs), this update enables fine‑grained, role‑based permissions aligned with your enterprise identity system. 

You benefit from stronger security through least‑privilege access, simplified compliance with auditable role assignments, and safer multiple‑team collaboration with scoped data access. By eliminating key management, you also reduce operational overhead and streamline onboarding of new apps and teams. 

Overall, you gain enterprise‑grade data security and governance for Redis—without added complexity. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Ingestion Volume Change dashboard in Metrics Usage Insights
items.description:
Metrics Usage Insights now includes an Ingestion Volume Change dashboard to help you compare ingestion volume over time. Quickly detect spikes or drops in time series counts and event ingestion rates, enabling faster investigation of cost changes and more effective capacity planning.

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Guest RDMA on Azure Boost
items.description:
Guest RDMA is now in preview on Azure, starting in the UK South region, bringing high-throughput, ultra-low latency networking directly into guest VMs within the same region. 

By using Azure Boost to enable RDMA in the guest OS, applications can bypass the traditional networking stack and offload transport to the NIC, reducing CPU overhead and improving communication performance.  

Key benefits include low latency through kernel bypass, high throughput of up to 100 Gb/s in preview depending on VM SKU, and lower CPU usage from hardware-based data movement.  

The preview is designed for workloads with frequent or large data transfers, including AI/ML training and inference, distributed storage and databases, and HPC workloads.  

In preview, Guest RDMA supports VM-to-VM connections within the same VNet and region. Load balancers, private endpoints, VNet encryption, flow logging, UDRs, and IP forwarding are not yet supported, but are planned for GA.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Voice sync for avatar support in Voice Live API in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now supports avatar voice sync with custom voices in the Voice Live API, allowing developers to pair branded or persona-specific text-to-speech voices with real-time avatar experiences. This update helps teams building virtual agents, digital humans, and immersive customer engagement scenarios preserve their existing voice identity while taking advantage of low-latency, lip-synced avatar rendering, removing the previous limitation that restricted avatar pairing to a curated voice set. By unifying custom voices and avatars in a single low-latency pipeline, the capability reduces integration complexity for live conversational scenarios such as kiosks, retail assistants, and accessibility experiences. As a preview, regional availability and configuration semantics may continue to evolve before general availability. To get started, configure your custom voice and avatar in the Microsoft Foundry Voice Live API and review the updated avatar guidance in the documentation. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Files assessments are now available worldwide using Azure Migrate
items.description:
We’re pleased to announce that Azure Migrate now generally supports discovery and assessment of SMB and NFS file shares hosted on Windows and Linux servers. This gives customers a complete, data-driven view of their file share environment and a clear path to migrate to Azure Files. The capability entered preview in mid-February and is now generally available worldwide. The adoption during public preview has been strong, with hundreds of customers creating file share assessments, actively planning and executing migrations to Azure Files. 

Key benefits include:   

  1. Discover and review on-premises SMB/NFS shares from Windows/Linux environments   
  2. Group, tag, and filter shares for better planning   
  3. Generate business cases comparing Azure Files and on-premises costs   
  4. Assess shares with Azure Files SKU recommendations based on region, redundancy, media type, and performance   
  5. Alternately, evaluate move to Azure VMs for quick lift and shift rehost  

This enhancement streamlines migration planning, reduces guesswork, and speeds up transitions to Azure Files, especially for complex environments.    

Getting started: Use Azure portal to set up discovery and run Azure Files assessments in your Azure Migrate project. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Ingest OTLP signals into Azure Monitor with the OpenTelemetry Collector
items.description:
Azure Monitor's support for native ingestion of OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) signals is now generally available. This enables you to send telemetry data directly from OpenTelemetry-instrumented applications and platforms to Azure Monitor. You can configure your OpenTelemetry Collector to send data directly to Azure Monitor cloud ingestion endpoints to ingest OTLP metrics, logs and traces using Microsoft Entra for authentication.

You can enable OTLP data ingestion in Azure Monitor using Application Insights OR by manually creating the required data collection endpoints, rules and workspaces. The Application Insights-based approach is recommended for most scenarios as it automates resource creation and includes built-in application performance management experiences.

Ingested OTLP metrics are stored in Azure Monitor Workspaces and can be queried and alerted upon with Prometheus query language (PromQL). OTLP logs and traces are stored in Log Analytics workspaces using new OpenTelemetry tables and semantics.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: AI pipelines in Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
AI pipelines for Azure HorizonDB is now available in public preview. AI pipelines let you describe an AI data ingestion workflow, chunking, embedding, extraction, generation, and ranking, declaratively in SQL, and run it as a fault-tolerant pipeline inside the database.  

Execution is durable: pipelines survive crashes, retry failed steps automatically, checkpoint incremental work, and resume long-running jobs from the last completed step. 

This removes the boilerplate ingestion service that many GenAI applications rebuild today. Pipelines run on change, so embeddings stay in sync as source rows are inserted or updated, and only new or changed rows need to be re-embedded. 

When the embedding model, dimensions, or chunk size change, backfill reprocesses every row as a single durable instance that resumes from the last checkpoint instead of restarting from zero. AI pipelines are part of the azure_ai extension, built on pg_durable, and work with AI model management, pgvector, DiskANN vector search, and full-text search to provide an end-to-end retrieval path inside one database. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Discovery
items.description: Microsoft Discovery is now generally available, providing research and development organizations an enterprise platform for building and governing agentic AI workflows across scientific and engineering disciplines. Also available in preview is the Microsoft Discovery app, a local desktop experience that helps researchers and scientific teams begin working with agentic discovery today without requiring cloud infrastructure.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL as a knowledge source in Foundry IQ
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry adds Azure SQL Database as a first-class Knowledge Source in Azure AI Search, available in public preview. Enterprise developers and solution architects building Copilot, RAG, and agentic experiences can now expose authoritative tables and views from Azure SQL as searchable, retrieval-ready knowledge for Knowledge Bases, RAG pipelines, and Foundry agents. The capability uses the same indexer-based ingestion patterns developers already know in Azure AI Search and aligns Azure SQL with SharePoint, OneLake, and other Knowledge Sources under one configuration model. Copilots and agents can ground responses in current operational data, including customer profiles, transactions, and reference tables, without custom pipelines or duplicate retrieval systems. The result is a unified knowledge layer where structured business data and unstructured content are queried through a single framework for more accurate, enterprise-ready AI. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: APIM Support for Foundry Models in Azure AI Search
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry brings Azure API Management support to all Foundry model integrations in Azure AI Search, now in public preview. Enterprise platform engineers and AI solution teams running large-scale RAG pipelines can place Foundry and Azure OpenAI models behind APIM for the GenAI Prompt Skill, embedding models, and vectorizer operations used at indexing and query time. APIM provides traffic shaping, load balancing, custom domains, identity governance, and private connectivity in front of every model endpoint a Search workload depends on. Customers can eliminate indexing failures caused by endpoint throttling or outages, stabilize high-throughput ingestion, and consolidate authentication and policy management into a single control plane. Operations teams gain consistent observability and audit trails across enrichment dependencies, while RAG systems hold accuracy and freshness as content volume grows. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Tool search in Microsoft Foundry toolboxes
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry adds tool search to Foundry toolboxes in public preview, giving developers and admins a fast way to find the right tool inside large, multi-team catalogs. As your toolbox grows, sending every tool definition on every turn gets expensive. Tool Search retrieves only the most relevant tools at runtime, keeping the model’s context focused and efficient. Instead of browsing lists, the agent describes its intent, discovers the right tools, and executes. Toolbox builders also need control over how tools are surfaced, and tool search provides this. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Foundry IQ
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry IQ reaches general availability, giving developers a managed knowledge layer that grounds agents in enterprise data without rebuilding retrieval pipelines for each project. Teams connect SharePoint, OneLake, Azure Blob, and other sources once, then Foundry IQ handles ingestion, chunking, vector indexing, and access enforcement using the calling user's permissions. Agents query a single knowledge base and receive ranked, source-cited results, so answers stay tied to the documents customers control. Foundry IQ runs inside the same Foundry project as the agent and shares its identity, observability, and content safety configuration. Customers can ship grounded copilots faster, reduce duplicated retrieval code across teams, and keep sensitive data inside the tenant boundary. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Fabric IQ Ontology Knowledge Source in Microsoft Foundry IQ
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry IQ now treats a Microsoft Fabric Ontology as a federated knowledge source in public preview, giving agents a way to query the semantic layer customers already curate in Fabric. Foundry IQ translates natural language questions into ontology-grounded queries and SQL against the entities, relationships, and bindings the Fabric team has defined, then returns results with citations back to the underlying Fabric tables. Analytics and platform teams can expose governed business definitions to agents without exporting data or maintaining a parallel schema. The source plugs into the same Foundry IQ retrieval flow as document and database sources, so a single agent call can combine ontology-grounded answers with unstructured knowledge. This release helps customers bring trusted business semantics into agentic applications. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Private Connectivity for Azure AI Search and Foundry Knowledge Bases
items.description:
Azure AI Search and Foundry Knowledge Bases now support private, end-to-end network connectivity between search resources and Foundry services. Customers can route ingestion, enrichment, retrieval, and agent traffic over Shared Private Link or Network Security Perimeter so data never traverses the public internet. This release is built for organizations running RAG pipelines, Knowledge Bases, and Foundry agents on regulated or sensitive data, where compliance teams require full network isolation. Existing search indexes, indexers, and Knowledge Base configurations continue to work; customers add private connectivity through the portal or ARM templates. Combined with Azure RBAC and customer-managed keys, this brings Foundry knowledge workflows in line with the same network controls already used for Azure AI Search production deployments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Content Understanding chunking and image verbalization in Azure AI Search
items.description:
Azure AI Search now supports Content Understanding chunking and image verbalization in public preview, expanding the built-in skill that parses rich documents during indexing. Indexers can split documents into semantically meaningful chunks and generate text descriptions of embedded images, charts, and diagrams in the same pass. Retrieval-augmented generation apps benefit because each chunk carries the visual context that used to be lost when images were stripped out. Customers indexing slide decks, technical manuals, and scanned forms get higher answer quality without running a separate vision pipeline. The skill plugs into existing integrated vectorization workflows, so teams can add it to current skillsets without rebuilding indexes from scratch. This release ships under the same Azure AI Search billing and data residency commitments customers already use today. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor Service Level Indicators (SLI)
items.description:
Azure Monitor now includes Service Level Indicators (SLIs) and Service Level Objectives (SLOs), giving teams a clearer way to measure how customers actually experience their applications. Instead of relying only on infrastructure signals like CPU or isolated alerts, SLIs help determine whether an issue is truly affecting users. This shifts the focus from simply asking whether an app is up to understanding whether it is fast, reliable, and meeting expectations. With SLIs and SLOs, teams can cut through operational noise and answer the question that matters most: are we delivering on our customer promise?

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: MAI-Voice-2 in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry now offers MAI-Voice-2 in public preview, a first-party voice model from the Microsoft AI team. MAI-Voice-2 generates natural speech across more than 10 languages and supports voice cloning from a short reference sample, plus voice prompting so developers can shape tone, pacing, and style with plain instructions. Customers can build multilingual virtual agents, accessibility experiences, and audio content workflows without stitching together separate cloning and prompt-engineering tools. Because MAI-Voice-2 is sold directly by Microsoft, it ships with the same billing, content safety, and responsible AI policies as other Microsoft-published models in Foundry. Developers can deploy it through the Foundry catalog and call it alongside other speech and language models in a single project. 

Learn more.

items.title: General Availability: Backup your ledger files for audit with Azure confidential ledger’s new tool
items.description:
Ever wondered how to allow auditing personas (i.e. security analyst in your organization or security assessment contractor) the ability to view your ledger files and establish trust in the cryptographic proofs themselves? With the new localized, web ledger explorer tool, ledger files can be imported to verify the authenticity of the ledger and the ledger data in its entirety. This tool enables a simple experience in viewing the merkle-tree proof visually to ensure all ledger contents are chained together.  

Administrators of the ledger instances continue to have access to the ledger explorer feature in the portal experience, which provides similar view into the ledger contents.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: User feedback logging in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
This feature introduces end user feedback logging semantics that enables developers to capture structured feedback signals from real users interacting with AI agents—such as thumbs up/down, ratings, or custom annotations—and automatically associates that feedback with the underlying request traces in Azure Monitor. By standardizing how feedback is logged and correlated with agent runs and telemetry, the feature closes the loop between user experience and system behavior, allowing teams to analyze quality, detect issues, and continuously improve models based on real-world usage. Captured feedback flows through existing observability pipelines, making it available alongside performance and evaluation metrics, and can be fed into downstream evaluation and optimization workflows so that production signals directly inform ongoing model tuning and product iteration. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Text Analytics for Health NextGen Playground in Azure AI Language
items.description:
Azure AI Language brings the next-generation Text Analytics for Health (TA4H) playground to general availability in the Microsoft Foundry portal. Clinical informatics teams and ISVs can paste discharge summaries, doctor's notes, or research abstracts and see extracted diagnoses, medications, symptoms, and time references with UMLS entity linking and relation extraction in a single view. The playground returns FHIR-structured output alongside the standard JSON response, so teams can validate downstream integration with electronic health record systems before writing a line of code. Supported input languages, entity categories, and assertion detection match the production service. The same Foundry resource powers both the playground and the REST API. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Self-serve custom photo avatar creation in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry brings self-serve custom photo avatar creation to GA in the Foundry NextGen fine-tuning portal. Enterprise customers building voice agents with avatars or producing content with avatar and speech often need a branded avatar instead of a standard one, but until now the only path ran through a manual white-glove engagement that was slow and dependent on internal teams. With this release, customers create custom photo avatars directly in the portal through a guided self-serve workflow, integrated alongside other model customization capabilities in NextGen fine-tuning. Teams iterate on a brand-aligned avatar in hours rather than weeks and deploy to production scenarios such as customer-facing voice agents and interactive training content, removing the bottleneck that limited avatar creation to a small number of partners. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Agent-to-agent (A2A) support for Prompt agents and Hosted agents in Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service adds agent-to-agent (A2A) communication in public preview for Prompt agents and Hosted agents that use the responses protocol. Agents can call other agents by name through a managed endpoint, with identity, content safety, and audit logging applied to every hop. Developers can model multi-step business processes as a small set of cooperating agents instead of a single monolithic prompt, then trace the full conversation across agents in Application Insights. Because A2A is a first-class protocol in Agent Service, agents written with Agent Framework, LangGraph, or direct code can all participate in the same network without protocol shims. This release helps teams move from single-agent prototypes toward production multi-agent systems with the same enterprise controls already used for individual agents. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Red Hat OpenShift in Belgium Central
items.description:
Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) is now generally available in Azure Belgium Central, expanding regional availability for OpenShift deployments across Europe. With the launch of Microsoft’s first Azure region in Belgium, customers can now run fully managed OpenShift clusters closer to their users and data, improving performance and reducing latency for cloud-native applications. 

This new region enables organizations to deploy Kubernetes-based workloads while meeting local data residency and regulatory requirements. Built with multiple availability zones, Belgium Central supports resilient, production-grade architectures for mission-critical applications running on ARO. Customers can take advantage of consistent OpenShift operations across hybrid and multi-cloud environments, while benefiting from Azure-native integration and enterprise-grade support. 

The availability of ARO in Belgium Central provides a strong foundation for regulated industries and enterprises that require in-country infrastructure. It also supports modern application development patterns, including AI-enabled and data-intensive workloads, with improved proximity, control, and scalability. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Rubric evaluator in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry introduces rubric evaluators for measuring agent quality, now in public preview for single-turn and multi-turn agent flows. Rubric evaluators enable developers to define context-specific evaluation criteria using agent prompts, production traces and context-specific files with weighted dimensions and optional human review, ensuring that quality is measured against what truly matters for each scenario. This establishes a reliable baseline that is powering downstream workflows, including evaluation, optimization, regression testing and deployment gates.  

Learn More

items.title: Generally Available: Custom Voice portal experience in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Azure AI Speech moves the Custom Voice authoring experience into the Microsoft Foundry portal in general availability. Approved Custom Voice customers can now upload voice talent recordings and consent statements, run data quality checks, train neural voice models, and deploy to endpoints from the same Foundry project that hosts their text-to-speech, Speech-to-text, and Voice Live workloads.  They can also train Personal voice in Foundry. The experience replaces the previous Speech Studio Custom Voice flow with consistent Foundry navigation, role-based access, and project-scoped resources. Existing custom voice models, test scripts, and endpoints carry over without retraining. Custom Voice remains a Limited Access feature, so customers must already be approved through the intake form before they can use the portal. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Evaluations with Intelligent Trace Sampling
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry observability introduces intelligent trace filtering and sampling for evaluations in public preview. Instead of running evaluations against all production traces, Foundry now select a representative subset of traces using a multi-stage MinHash farthest-first diversity algorithm, including deduplication, hard filers, aggregation and diversity-based selection for evaluation. This approach improves cost efficiency while producing significantly higher lexical diversity and diverse coverage compared to random sampling. Intelligent sampling is particularly effective for: evaluation and benchmarks, rubric generation and finetuning dataset curation.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Foundry for Visual Studio Code (June Build 2026 refresh)
items.description:
The Microsoft Foundry extension for Visual Studio Code reaches general availability with a Build 2026 refresh that brings the full model catalog, model playground, and Hosted agent deployment into the editor. Developers can sign in with their Azure account, create or open a Foundry project, browse over 1,900 models with filters for publisher and capability, and deploy a model into the project without leaving VS Code. The extension also generates starter code for Python, .NET, JavaScript, or Java in the SDK and authentication style the developer prefers. For Hosted agents, the extension supports both local development and one-click deploy to Foundry Agent Service, with side-by-side model and agent playgrounds for fast iteration. 

Learn more

items.title: Public Preview: Domain filter for specialized model discovery in Foundry model catalog
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry model catalog adds a domain filter in public preview, helping developers narrow the catalog of over 1,900 models to the ones trained for a specific industry or use case. Filters cover domains such as robotics, biomedical sciences, materials discovery, and coding. The filter sits alongside existing filters for publisher, modality, deployment type, and capability, so a developer searching for a robotics-tuned reasoning model can find it in a few clicks instead of scrolling through hundreds of general-purpose entries. The same filter is exposed through the catalog REST API, which lets internal model-discovery portals built on top of Foundry surface domain-specific shortlists for their developer audiences. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Observability developer experience in Azure Developer CLI (azd)
items.description:
Use the Azure Developer CLI (azd) CLI evaluation experience to add a measured quality loop to an agent created with Microsoft Foundry. It empowers users on the hosted-agent lifecycle in azd, where you create, provision, deploy, initialize evaluation assets, run a first evaluation, inspect the run, and reuse the evaluation recipe for later runs. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: TextPII NextGen Playground updates in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now offers an updated TextPII NextGen Playground with a refreshed API Configuration Panel, including preview features introduced at Ignite 2025. This update lets developers test predefined PII categories, redaction modes, and language settings interactively before integrating the API into production workflows. By providing a single interactive environment to validate configurations against sensitive text inputs, the playground reduces the learning curve for new preview capabilities and helps teams govern the AI lifecycle by catching misconfigurations early. The experience supports common PII detection scenarios such as document sanitization, transcript redaction, and dataset preparation for analytics. Preview availability and exact configuration options may evolve before general availability. To get started, open the TextPII playground in Microsoft Foundry and explore the updated configuration panel. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Conversational PII NextGen Playground in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now offers a Conversational PII (ConvPII) NextGen Playground with transcript input and an API Configuration Panel, enabling developers to validate PII detection across multi-speaker dialogue before integrating the API. This update helps you test conversation-format inputs such as call center transcripts and meeting recordings, iterate on configuration settings, and assess accuracy for informal, multi-turn language. By providing an interactive environment for experimentation, the playground reduces iteration cycles and lowers the risk of shipping misconfigured PII detection into production conversational workloads. The capability targets developers building privacy-aware analytics, support automation, and compliance pipelines that rely on accurate redaction in spoken or chat-based content. Preview availability and configuration options may evolve before general availability. To get started, open the ConvPII playground in Microsoft Foundry and try a sample transcript. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing: Confidential Live Migration for Intel TDX confidential VMs in Azure
items.description:
Microsoft is announcing Confidential Live Migration in Azure, a new capability designed to improve operational flexibility and availability for Intel® TDX Confidential VMs during platform servicing. Confidential Live Migration helps move a Confidential VM to another host with limited interruption while maintaining protections against privileged software access. The capability supports attested transfers, destination authorization, and protected migration of VM memory and execution context. This capability will roll out gradually for DC/ECesv6 and DC/ECedsv6 series, with additional details to be shared ahead of general availability.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager
items.description: Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager is now in public preview, offering a unified, goal-driven experience to design, assess, and improve application resiliency across Azure. It brings together capabilities across Availability Zones, Azure Advisor, Chaos Studio, Azure Monitor, and Copilot into a single workflow for end-to-end resilience. With AI guidance, actionable recommendations, and built-in drills, organizations can proactively build, improve, and validate resiliency end to end.

items.title: Public Preview: Advanced full-text search in Azure DocumentDB
items.description:
Now you can unify your search operations in a single database. Azure DocumentDB has added fuzzy search, proximity search, more language support, and BM25 ranking to its full-text capabilities, bringing vector and advanced text search operations together. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server: DuckDB extension
items.description:
You can now install the DuckDB extension in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Simple log alerts in Azure Monitor
items.description:
We are excited to announce the General Availability of Simple log alerts in Azure Monitor, available starting today. This feature is designed to provide a simplified and more intuitive experience for monitoring and alerting, enhancing your ability to detect and respond to problems in near real-time. Unlike Log Search Alerts that aggregate rows over a defined period, Simple Log Alerts evaluate each row individually.

Key Benefits:
  • Simplified Query Language.
  • Low Latency Alerting.
  • Support multiple log plans, including Analytics and Basic Logs.
Pricing Information:
The cost for Simple log alerts is based on 1-minute frequency Log alert.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Code-first observability for Foundry Agents in VS Code
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry brings code-first observability to agent developers in public preview, delivered as an observe skill inside the Foundry Plugin for VS Code Copilot Chat. Developers run the full evaluation-driven optimization loop from the editor through natural language commands. The skill orchestrates Foundry MCP tools to auto-generate context-specific evaluators and starter datasets from the agent definition, run batch evaluations, download and cluster failures by root cause, propose prompt improvements, deploy new agent versions, and compare versions side by side. Developers stay in their coding environment instead of jumping to the portal, which shortens the agent development loop and lowers the barrier to consistent observability. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Agent kit for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
Your AI coding agents just got smarter about building high-performance database applications. The Azure Cosmos DB Agent Kit is now generally available, bringing proven best practices directly into your development workflow. Whether you're designing data models, optimizing queries, or architecting globally distributed applications, your agents now have the expertise to guide every decision. 

With more than 100 actionable rules covering everything from partition key strategies to SDK optimization patterns, the Agent Kit helps you avoid common performance pitfalls and build applications that scale efficiently from day one. Your agents understand the nuances of Cosmos DB, helping you to prevent hot partitions, determine which queries will cause runaway costs, and configure resilience for production workloads. You benefit from faster development, fewer performance surprises, and applications that work smarter with your database. The Agent Kit integrates seamlessly into your coding workflow, providing real-time guidance whether you're in Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot, or your favorite AI coding environment. You can learn best practices faster, make the right architectural choices, and catch optimization opportunities earlier. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for early-June
items.description:
In early June 2026, the following update and enhancement was made to Azure SQL: 

Now you can use AES 256 symmetric keys to configure transparent data encryption (TDE) with customer-managed keys in Azure SQL Database. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Secure, Modern Access to Azure Files on macOS with MS Entra ID
items.description:
Azure Files now supports access from macOS using Entra ID authentication (Public Preview), enabling secure, identity-based access to file shares for cross-platform teams. This expands support for modern workflows, allowing users on macOS to seamlessly access and collaborate on shared data alongside Windows environments. Key benefits include:  

  • Enhanced security posture: Password-less access from macOS using Entra ID - no credential prompts or storage account keys—enforced by Conditional Access, MFA, and AES-256 encryption 
  • Reduced operational overhead: Eliminate key management; access is provisioned and governed through Entra ID groups  
  • No Active Directory dependency: Enable full access to Azure Files using cloud identities - no domain controllers required  
  • True identity-based access model: Kerberos authentication with Azure RBAC and NTFS ACLs for precise, layered access control  
  • Accelerated AI workflows: Seamless access to large datasets from macOS to support faster experimentation and development 

Reach out to azurefiles@microsoft.com with questions. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: File share centric management model (Microsoft.FileShares) for Azure Files
items.description:
The new file share service management experience for Azure Files is now generally available for NFS 4.1 shares on SSD storage. Powered by the Microsoft.FileShares resource provider, file shares are now top-level Azure resources that you can create, secure, scale, and bill independently, without a storage account.

Key benefits:
  • Top-level resource with a familiar, NAS-like management model.
  • Independent performance for each share through the provisioned v2 billing model, with dynamic scaling up and down and no noisy-neighbor impact.
  • Share-level security and networking, including per-share billing, encryption in transit, policies, and network configuration.
  • Support for up to 10,000 shares per subscription per region, with approximately 2.5× faster provisioning.
  • Snapshot support: up to 200 incremental, point-in-time snapshots per share, with metadata editing capability.
  • Per-share billing for cost tracking.
Learn more:
  • Simpler, scalable file share management in Azure - now generally available
  • Planning for an Azure Files deployment
  • How to create a file share
  • Scalability and performance targets

items.title: Public Preview: Azure API Management introduces a Unified Model API for multi-model AI applications.
items.description:
As organizations adopt multiple LLM providers, developers often need to handle different API formats, SDKs, and integration patterns for each model vendor. This increases application complexity and makes provider switching, failover, and governance more difficult. 

With the Unified Model API, Azure API Management enables organizations to standardize on a single client-facing API format — such as the OpenAI Chat Completions API — while transparently transforming requests to various backend providers, including OpenAI and Anthropic models. 

This allows teams to: 

  • Use a consistent client SDK and API format across multiple LLM providers 

  • Switch or fail over between model providers without client-side changes 

  • Simplify application development for multi-model AI architectures 

  • Apply centralized governance, security, and observability across heterogeneous model backends 

By abstracting provider-specific differences behind a unified API layer, Azure API Management helps organizations build more portable, resilient, and governable AI applications. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Unified Text Translation API in Azure AI Translator
items.description:
Azure AI Translator's unified Text Translation API reaches general availability, giving developers a single endpoint that fronts neural machine translation, large language model translation, small language model translation, Adaptive custom translation, and classic Custom Translator. Applications send one request and pick the engine that best fits each piece of content based on language pair, latency target, and quality requirements. The unified API consolidates years of customer feedback asking for fewer SDKs and less plumbing between translation modes. Existing v3 customers can stay on the v3 GA endpoint, while teams that want LLM-grade quality on long or domain-specific content can opt into the new GA API and pay only for the requests routed to LLM. The service retains regional data residency, Microsoft Entra authentication, and per-region service endpoints.  

Learn more.

items.title: Preview: Azure Cobalt 200 Arm-based Dpsv7, Dplsv7, Epsv7, Mpsv4, and Lpsv5-series Virtual Machines
items.description:
The general purpose Dpsv7 and Dplsv7, memory-optimized Epsv7, high-memory Mpsv4, and dense storage Lpsv5 VMs are now available in preview. These virtual machines deliver significant enhancements over the previous generation Cobalt 100 VMs, offering improved CPU performance, greater scalability, and expanded configuration options to meet the demands of a wide range of workloads. 

Key improvements include:

  • Up to 50% improvement in CPU performance (workload dependent)

  • 20% improvement in remote storage IOPS with NVMe

  • 10% better remote storage throughput with NVMe

  • 15% improvement in network bandwidth

Learn more.

items.title: Global PTU Reservations Are Now Region-Agnostic
items.description:
Global Provisioned Throughput (PTU) reservations are now region-agnostic, enabling a single reservation to cover Global PTU deployments across multiple regions. 

Why it matters:

  • Optimize savings: One reservation can apply across regions, improving utilization and reducing stranded capacity. 

  • Increase flexibility: Deploy workloads where capacity is available without needing region-specific reservations.

  • Simplify cost management: Consolidate reservations instead of managing multiple regional commitments.

This builds on the benefits of provisioned throughput—predictable performance, allocated capacity, and cost savings for high-throughput workloads.

Learn more:  

  • What is Provisioned Throughput for Foundry Models?  
  • Save costs with Microsoft Foundry Provisioned Throughput Reservations

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management Premium v2 and Standard v2 now support wildcard custom hostnames.
items.description:
As API estates grow, managing individual custom domains and certificates for every subdomain can quickly become operationally complex and difficult to scale. Without wildcard support, every new subdomain — whether payments.api.contoso.com, inventory.api.contoso.com, or orders.api.contoso.com — requires its own hostname registration and certificate, meaning a team onboarding ten new API surfaces generates ten separate domain and certificate management tasks.  

With this update, Azure API Management Premium v2 and Standard v2 now support wildcard entries in custom hostnames,  allowing a single entry like *.api.contoso.com  and a single wildcard certificate to cover all subdomains automatically — no per-subdomain configuration required. This helps teams:  

  • Simplify certificate and domain management at scale  
  • Reduce operational overhead for rapidly growing API environments  
  • Maintain consistent branded API endpoints across dynamic subdomains  
  • Accelerate onboarding of new API surfaces without repeated hostname configuration  

By extending this capability to both Premium v2 and Standard v2, Azure API Management makes flexible and scalable domain management accessible to more organizations without requiring higher-tier deployments.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Backup for Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can now enable vaulted backups for Azure Cosmos DB accounts, protecting mission-critical data with secure, isolated, and resilient backups. Azure Backup for Cosmos DB, now in preview, supports cyber-resiliency and compliance needs, even in scenarios involving accidental deletion, malicious activity, or ransomware. With vaulted backups, Azure Backup maintains an independent copy of your Cosmos DB data in a vault that is isolated from the source account, strengthening protection against operational and security risks.  

Key capabilities:  

  • Off-site, isolated protection. Store Cosmos DB backups in an Azure Backup vault, isolated from the source account to enable recovery even if the source is compromised.  
  • Resilience. Vaulted backups protect against accidental deletion, insider threats, and ransomware scenarios.  
  • Policy-based, automated backups. Configure scheduled backups using Azure Backup policies, reducing manual efforts and improving consistency. 
  • Long-term retention for compliance. Retain backups for extended durations of up to 10 years to meet regulatory and audit requirements.  
  • Built-in protections such as encryption, soft delete, immutability, and role-based access control help safeguard backup data in the vault.  

Billing will be enabled from July 1, 2026.  

Learn more: 

  • Documentation  
  • Azure Backup pricing 
  • Pricing calculator

items.title: Generally Available: Voice Live integration with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service is now generally available for Voice Live integration, allowing developers to connect real-time speech-to-text and text-to-speech to a Foundry Agent without writing their own audio pipeline. Existing agent capabilities — including tool calling, knowledge, memory, guardrails, and enterprise integrations — continue to work seamlessly and are now enhanced with low-latency speech interactions. The agent provides a real-time streaming voice channel with interrupt handling, turn-taking, barge-in support, connection management, natural voices, and avatars for production phone and web experiences. For customers building customer service agents, learning companions, and in-car assistants, this provides a single supported path from Foundry agent logic to live audio input and output, instead of requiring them to stitch together Speech, the agent runtime, and WebRTC on their own.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Policy Coverage for Model Router in Foundry Models
items.description:
Azure Policy now provides centralized governance for deployments using the model router. Organizations can define and enforce routing standards across their environment, helping ensure that model selection aligns with security, compliance, and operational requirements.

Built-in policy definitions allow teams to govern deployment regions, approved model lists, required routing rules, and logging configurations. Administrators can apply policies across management groups and subscriptions, identify deployments that drift from approved configurations, and remediate issues using existing Azure governance workflows.

Because the integration is built on Azure Policy’s native framework, customers can use familiar tools for compliance monitoring, exemptions, remediation, and reporting without additional engineering effort. This enables regulated organizations to adopt new models more quickly while maintaining consistent governance and control across the enterprise. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts
items.description:
We’re excited to announce the General Availability of Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts! Using dynamic thresholds means you don't have to know the right threshold for each Log alert rule - Dynamic thresholds calculate the most appropriate thresholds for you.

Key benefits
Dynamic thresholds apply advanced machine learning and use a set of algorithms and methods to:
  1. Learn the historical behavior of log query results.
  2. Analyze these results over time and identify hourly / daily / weekly seasonal patterns.
  3. Calculate the most appropriate thresholds for log alert rules.
  4. Adapt automatically to changes in data patterns and adjust the threshold accordingly.
  5. At-scale monitoring - in rule monitoring multiple dimensions - the Dynamic threshold is calculated individually, per dimension combination.
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Rolling updates in Flex Consumption
items.description:
Rolling updates are now generally available in the Flex Consumption plan, delivering zero-downtime deployments with a simple configuration change.

Instead of forcefully restarting all instances during code or configuration updates, the platform gracefully replaces live instances by draining batches every few seconds while dynamically scaling out the latest version to meet demand. This approach ensures uninterrupted execution and resilient throughput across HTTP, non-HTTP, and Durable workloads - even during intensive scale-out scenarios.

How to enable:

  1. In the Azure Portal, enable it from the Configuration blade 

  2. Update your ARM/Bicep template with `properties.functionAppConfig.siteUpdateStrategy.type` set to `RollingUpdate`

  3. For Durable Functions, configure an orchestration match strategy (see guidance).

Known limitations:

  • Scale-out issues may occur with low HTTP concurrency; recommended value is 16.

  • No automatic rollback; roll forward by redeploying the last healthy version.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Github Copilot modernization
items.description:
GitHub Copilot modernization agent is now generally available
  • Coordinated orchestration from estate to code. Scale application assessments and upgrades across your entire app portfolio with GitHub Copilot modernization agent (GA), connecting high-level estate planning to hands-on code transformation. 
  • Modernize your way. Custom skills (GA) let teams and partners extend agent behavior with domain-specific expertise, tailoring modernization to the patterns and institutional knowledge unique to their environment 

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Storage optimized Lasv5 and Laosv5 Azure VM series
items.description:
The Lasv5 and Laosv5 storage optimized VMs, based on the 5th Gen AMD EPYC™ processor (Turin), are in preview. 

Lasv5-series is designed for storage-intensive workloads requiring high disk capacity, throughput, and I/O, while Laosv5-series is well-suited for workloads requiring significantly higher local storage capacity and performance. 

Lasv5 and Laosv5 VMs have sizes ranging from 2-160 vCPUs, with 8GiB of memory and 720GB of local NVMe disk capacity per vCPU. Both support 200Gbps of network bandwidth and deliver up to 35% better average CPU performance. The Lasv5 VMs offer up to 30.7TB of local storage capacity, while the Laosv5 VMs offer up to 138TB of local storage capacity. 

Compared to the previous generation Lasv4 VMs, Lasv5 VMs have: 

  • 33% larger maximum local storage capacity 
  • New 128 and 160 vCPU sizes 

Compared to the previous generation Laosv4 VMs, Laosv5 VMs have: 

  • 500% larger maximum local storage capacity 
  • New 48, 64, 96, 128, and160 vCPU sizes 

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: multiparty analytics with Azure Confidential Clean Rooms
items.description:
Microsoft is announcing the preview of multiparty analytics with Azure Confidential Clean Rooms, resulting in fully managed service that allows customers and their partners to securely analyze privacy sensitive datasets with Apache Spark based big-data analytics (Spark SQL) in a confidential computing based environment which protects their raw data from other collaborators and from the Azure operator by performing the computation in a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). Privacy sensitive datasets include personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI) and cryptographic secrets.

Organizations across industries are increasingly looking to supplement their data with data from business partners, to build a complete view of their business. For example, brands, publishers, and their partners need to collaborate using datasets containing Intellectual Property (IP) to improve the relevance of their campaigns. Data clean rooms help solve this challenge by allowing multiple organizations to share granular data and analyze combined datasets in a secure environment which provides guarantees against exfiltration of raw data.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Event Grid - MQTT v5 Subscription Identifier
items.description:
Azure Event Grid Standard Namespace now supports MQTT v5 subscription identifier capabilities in GA. 

Now each MQTT subscription can include an identifier that is delivered with incoming messages, enabling applications to route events immediately based on subscription context rather than parsing topic strings. This results in cleaner application logic and faster message handling for scenarios such as dashboards, alerts, and analytics pipelines.

items.title: Azure Container Linux (ACL) now generally available on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
items.description:
Azure Container Linux is a container-optimized, immutable operating system for AKS node pools — derived from Flatcar Container Linux and built on Azure Linux RPM packages. It delivers a locked-down, minimal host purpose-built for running containerized workloads at scale. 

Key features include: 

  • Immutable by design — The root /usr directory is read-only with dm-verity integrity verification. There is no package manager on the host — what ships in the image is what runs in production. This eliminates configuration drift and ensures consistent node state across your fleet. 
  • Container-optimized — Minimal OS footprint with only the components needed to run Kubernetes workloads. 
  • Out-of-the-box security — SELinux in enforcing mode applies strict least-privilege policies to all processes. Trusted Launch with a Unified Kernel Image (UKI) verifies boot integrity from firmware through kernel, ensuring nodes haven't been tampered with before they join your cluster. 
  • Derived from Flatcar — Built on Flatcar Container Linux's proven architecture: declarative node configuration, systemd-first service management, and an operational model designed for fleets of immutable nodes. 

  • Built on Azure Linux — Powered by the Azure Linux RPM ecosystem with Microsoft's security patching cadence, CVE response SLAs, and integrated support through Azure. 

Learn more and get started:  

  • Tech Community blog post 
  • Azure Container Linux Documentation 
  • Azure Linux Documentation 
  • Azure Linux on GitHub

items.title: Public preview: Azure Linux 4.0 for Azure Virtual Machines and VM Scale Sets
items.description:
Azure Linux 4.0, Microsoft's first-party Linux distribution purpose-built for Azure, is now available in public preview for Azure Virtual Machines and VM Scale Sets. It brings a modernized stack — including Linux kernel 6.18 LTS, dnf5 package manager, glibc 2.42, OpenSSL 3.5, and Python 3.14 — optimized for Azure compute, storage, and networking. It delivers faster VM startup and provisioning with a reduced package footprint and a security-first design. 

  Key highlights: 

  • Azure-tuned kernel — Linux 6.18 LTS with improved Hyper-V integration, GPU/AI accelerator support, and new hardware drivers 
  • Secure by default — Secure Boot, Trusted Launch, SELinux support, kernel hardening, and SBOMs published with target SLSA Level 3 
  • Minimal footprint — Ships only the packages required for cloud workloads, reducing attack surface from day one 
  • No additional OS licensing cost — Included with Azure compute; no separate OS licensing fees or support contracts 
  • Microsoft-owned supply chain — From kernel to CVE response, enabling fast-track Critical/High CVE patches with monthly security updates 
  • Predictable lifecycle —full support with LTS kernel and annual HWE kernel updates for new hardware platforms 
  • Container images — Base, and distroless images available on Microsoft Container Registry (MCR)

 Learn more:

  • Azure Linux 4.0 Build blog post   
  • Azure Linux on GitHub 
  • Release notes

items.title: Generally Available: OpenTelemetry Metrics, Visualizations, and Enhanced Monitoring in Azure Monitor for Azure VMs and Arc Servers
items.description:
OpenTelemetry metrics and visualizations in Azure Monitor are generally available, delivering an enhanced, unified monitoring experience for Azure Virtual Machines and Arc Servers. This release consolidates key monitoring capabilities into a single experience and introduces a simplified onboarding experience, helping customers more efficiently observe, diagnose, and optimize their environments. 

Previously, VM monitoring visualizations were powered by metric data from Log Analytics which continues to be fully supported. Customers now also have the option to power these visualizations using OpenTelemetry (OTel) Gues OS metrics, offering a more cost-efficient and performant solution.  

With this release, you can: 

  • Reduce monitoring costs and improve troubleshooting efficiency with faster metric query response times using OTel metrics 
  • Simplify setup with a unified onboarding experience, including support for selecting existing Data Collection Rules (DCRs) 
  • Onboard and configure monitoring at scale through the Monitoring Coverage, ARM templates, or Bicep templates 
  • Enable recommended alerts to accelerate issue detection and reduce configuration overhead 
  • Leverage Dashboards with Grafana for at-scale visibility and per-process insights across your VM environments 

Learn more: 

  • https://aka.ms/vmiv2docs   
  • Collect and customize OpenTelemetry metrics for Azure virtual machines - Azure Monitor

items.title: Public Preview: Automatic OS Image Upgrades for VMSS Flex
items.description:
Automatic OS Image Upgrades for Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) using Flexible Orchestration are now in public preview, enabling consistent, fleet-wide OS updates with reduced manual effort. This capability extends automated image upgrades to VMSS Flex, helping customers maintain secure, compliant, and up-to-date infrastructure at scale while lowering operational overhead. 

With this release, Azure shifts from per-VM patching to platform-driven, orchestrated updates applied across the entire scale set. Updates are rolled out using health-based progression, ensuring upgrades continue only when instances remain healthy, improving reliability and reducing risk.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 26.06 is now available
items.description:
Azure Sphere OS version 26.06 is now available in the Retail feed. This release includes updates to Azure Sphere OS only; it does not include an updated SDK. If your devices are connected to the internet, they will receive the updated OS from the cloud.

This release includes quality and underlying build system updates and addresses several CVEs.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Container Apps Sandboxes
items.description:
Teams building agentic applications, multi-tenant platforms, development environments, and CI/CD systems have often had to stitch together custom infrastructure to run untrusted code safely, preserve state across sessions, and handle bursty demand without paying for idle capacity. Azure Container Apps Sandboxes addresses that challenge with a new first-class resource type in Azure Container Apps that provides fast, secure, ephemeral compute environments with built-in suspend and resume capabilities. 

Each sandbox runs in its own hardware-isolated microVM boundary, supports standard OCI container images, and starts in sub-second time. It can preserve memory, disk state, and preloaded libraries in a snapshot, so workloads resume quickly from the same point without incurring a cold start reload penalty. For technical practitioners, this means they can now run AI-generated or otherwise untrusted workloads in strongly isolated environments, preserve execution context across long-running tasks, and scale from zero to thousands of concurrent sandboxes using the same Azure foundation that also powers offerings such as GitHub Sandbox, hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service, and Azure Container Apps Express. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Functions now supports hosting MCP Apps
items.description:
Developers building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers often rely on plain text responses even when user interactions required richer experiences, such as visual data exploration, complex configuration, real-time status monitoring, or multi-step workflows, which leads to excessive back-and-forth and limited usability. 


Azure Functions now supports building and hosting MCP Apps using the Azure Functions MCP Extension. MCP Apps enable servers to return interactive user interfaces that render directly within chat experiences, including forms, dashboards, and rich media viewers. This capability is available for Python, TypeScript, .NET, and Java, allowing developers to build MCP Apps using familiar languages.

With MCP Apps on Azure Functions, developers can now deliver richer and interactive experiences directly in conversations, reducing conversational friction, streamlining complex workflows, and making it easier for users to explore data and monitor live information without leaving the chat.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Functions now includes managed connectors to integrate with 1400+ of your favorite systems
items.description:
Azure Functions now includes managed connectors - the same 1,400+ connector ecosystem behind Logic Apps and Power Platform - as first-class triggers and operations. This enables customers to build integrated systems across the broader ecosystem such as Office 365, Teams, SharePoint, Salesforce, and other SaaS services, using familiar Functions workflows. 

With connectors natively available, developers can build event-driven integrations without custom polling logic or manual SDK integration, simplifying development and reducing integration friction. 

This feature eliminates the need to build custom integration logic, enabling direct connections to services like Microsoft 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP, Dynamics, and 1400+ other systems. You can now write event-driven Functions that respond to SaaS events or output to external systems using familiar Functions syntax, reducing integration complexity and time-to-market. 

Learn more: 

  • Azure Functions integration with managed connectors documentation  
  • Azure Functions integration with managed connectors in Azure Functions samples

items.title: Public Preview: Serverless agents runtime for Azure Functions
items.description:
Azure Functions now supports building AI agents as a first-class workload using a markdown-first programming model in public preview. With this release, developers can author event-driven serverless agents in natural language. 

The serverless agents runtime helps developers build agents that respond to conversations, react to events, and take actions across enterprise systems without writing framework boilerplate or per-service integration code. Developers can use any Azure Functions trigger — HTTP, timer, queue, Service Bus, Event Hub, Cosmos DB, blob, Event Grid, and new connector-backed triggers (Teams messages, Outlook mail, calendar events) — to run an agent. Agents can also call connectors as tools, consume remote MCP servers, run sandboxed code and browser automation in Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions, and optionally expose a built-in chat UI, HTTP chat API, and MCP server endpoint with no extra code. 

In preview, the serverless agents runtime is supported on the Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan. This enables scale-to-zero economics, managed identity, VNet integration, and Application Insights observability for agent workloads on Azure.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Copilot-assisted coding & agent skills to build, deploy, and run Azure Functions faster in VS Code, CLI, and azd
items.description:
Developers are already using AI coding assistants to build Azure Functions apps today, but the quality of the help varies widely. It depends on which underlying model the assistant is using and how recent its training data is, which means developers often get advice based on outdated APIs, deprecated patterns, or generic guidance that misses Azure Functions best practices. 

Azure Functions now provides a set of AI assistant plugins and agent skills in public preview that close that gap. With a quick one-step install, developers can equip their AI coding assistant — including GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex — with current, Azure Functions expertise that activates automatically as they work in VS Code, the CLI, and azd. The skills cover the end-to-end developer loop: local setup, project and function creation, deployment with tools, diagnostics for deployment and runtime issues, app health and inventory inspection, and best-practices review of existing Function Apps. They follow the Agent Skills open standard, are grounded in official Azure documentation, and integrate with relevant MCP servers so the assistant always works from the latest guidance and Azure best practices — not whatever its base model happened to learn at training time. 

The result is more accurate, more consistent, and more current AI assistance for Azure Functions, regardless of which assistant or model the developer chooses.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Built-in Grafana dashboards for Azure Functions
items.description:
Azure Functions now provides built-in Grafana dashboards. Customers now get a zero-setup, single pane of glass for the health, performance, and scale of their function apps directly in the Azure portal: no Grafana instance to provision, no data sources to wire up, and no extra cost.

The default dashboard is purpose-built for Azure Functions and brings together the signals that matter for operating a function app, including execution volume, success and failure rates, latency, resource utilization, scale activity, and recent errors correlated with application telemetry. Customers can duplicate and customize the dashboard to fit their team's needs.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Go language support on Azure Functions
items.description:
Azure Functions now supports Go as a first-class language option in public preview. With this release, developers can author event-driven serverless apps in Go using the Azure Functions Go programming model and SDK, while still benefiting from Azure Functions capabilities such as triggers, bindings, and integrated observability. 

Go support helps teams that standardize on Go deliver cloud-native APIs, automation, and integration workloads without introducing a second language stack. Developers can use familiar Go tooling and patterns while building Functions that respond to HTTP requests, scheduled events, messaging systems, and storage events. 

In preview, Go language is supported on the Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan. This enables rapid scaling, pay-per-use economics, and streamlined deployment for Go workloads on Azure. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Override Scale Rules in Azure Functions on Azure Container Apps
items.description:
Azure Functions on Container Apps has traditionally used platform-managed scaling, where triggers are automatically translated into KEDA scale rules. With the new allowScalingRuleOverride property, customers can now choose to override platform-managed scaling and define their own custom KEDA scaling rules.

When scaling override is enabled, the platform skips automatic KEDA rule generation and applies customer-defined scaling rules while continuing to run on the same native Functions on Container Apps architecture, available in API version 2026-03-02-preview and later.

This enhancement is especially useful for scenarios where there are gaps in platform trigger support, where automatically generated KEDA rules may lead to unintended scaling behavior, or where workloads require custom queue thresholds, HTTP concurrency tuning, or standardized scaling policies across services.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Additional support for OpenTelemetry destinations (New Relic, Dynatrace, Elastic)
items.description:
Azure Container Apps enhances its OpenTelemetry (OTel) capabilities by expanding support for third-party observability platforms. This update introduces additional endpoint options for commonly used monitoring tools such as New Relic, Dynatrace, and Elastic, extending the existing managed OpenTelemetry experience with simpler setup for additional third-party observability platforms.  

This update makes it easier to send logs, metrics, and traces to more destinations without deploying or managing your own agents. Teams can now use a more consistent OpenTelemetry-based pipeline across Azure Monitor, Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, Elastic, and OTLP-compatible endpoints, with less configuration overhead and more flexibility to route telemetry where they need it, including support for OTLP/HTTP endpoints, enabling integration with any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Monitor HTTP traffic in Azure Container Apps
items.description:
In addition to platform-level logs, Azure Container Apps now adds a dedicated Azure Monitor diagnostic setting category, ContainerAppHTTPLogs, that exposes detailed HTTP access logs for incoming traffic and is designed for high-volume request data. With this capability, customers can now troubleshoot ingress and request-flow issues with much greater precision, making it easier to investigate failed requests, latency, retries, WebSocket disconnects, routing behavior, and backend connectivity problems.  

This gives teams a dedicated, scalable traffic logging surface for scenarios where platform-level signals alone were not enough to quickly understand request-level behavior. The result is faster issue resolution, less operational friction, and stronger confidence in running and scaling high-traffic, business-critical applications on Azure Container Apps.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Confidential Compute support on Azure Container Apps
items.description:
Customers running regulated or sensitive containerized workloads often need stronger protection for data while it is actively being processed, especially in scenarios that require higher isolation and stricter compliance controls. 

Confidential Compute in Azure Container Apps provides hardware-backed Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) through workload profiles, extending protection to data in use in addition to data at rest and in transit. With this capability now generally available, teams can run higher-trust workloads in Azure Container Apps with stronger isolation for sensitive data and a clearer path to meeting stricter compliance and data sovereignty requirements. 

This release enables Azure Container Apps workloads to use hardware-enforced isolation mechanisms that protect sensitive data while it is being processed and help prevent unauthorized access to in-memory data, including from the underlying infrastructure. Teams can now deploy confidential workloads on a serverless container platform with stronger protections for data in use. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Defender for Cloud support for Azure Container Apps (Serverless Containers Posture)
items.description:
Customers can now bring Azure Container Apps environments into Microsoft Defender for Cloud’s Serverless Containers Posture experience, helping security teams extend posture management across more of their container estate from a single workflow. This makes it easier to gain visibility into Container Apps resources and assess risks across areas such as identity, networking, and container or image configuration. 

With this capability, teams can more consistently evaluate risk across container environments and use attack path analysis to identify potential exposure faster. The result is a more unified security posture, less manual effort, and stronger confidence when securing Container Apps deployments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Linux emulator (vNext)
