items.description:
We are announcing the general availability of the Azure Cosmos DB Linux emulator (vNext), a cross-platform, Docker-based emulator for local development and testing against Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. 


The vNext emulator runs as a lightweight Docker container on Linux, macOS, and Windows, with native support for both x64 and ARM64 architectures. You can use it to develop and test your applications locally without incurring Azure service costs or needing an internet connection. 


Since public preview, the emulator has shipped continuous updates that have significantly improved SDK compatibility and expanded Cosmos DB feature coverage. 


With this release, you get a local development experience that includes support for core operations, a wide range of query capabilities, and added support for vector search and Azure Cosmos DB Shell integration. The emulator also includes health probe endpoints for readiness checks, and OpenTelemetry integration for observability. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: OmniVec, an open-source embedding toolkit for Azure
items.description:
You can now automate embedding generation from multiple data sources into Azure Cosmos DB and other Azure destinations. Building AI applications often requires stitching together data extraction, embedding generation, and writing to vector databases into a custom pipeline. You have to write extraction logic for each source, integrate with embedding APIs, and build your own sync mechanism to keep embeddings current as source data changes. OmniVec, now in public preview as an open-source project, handles this pipeline end to end, deployed in your own Azure subscription. 


You configure your data sources, select an embedding model, and deploy with a single azd up command. OmniVec pulls data from sources like Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Blob Storage, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; generates embeddings; and writes them to Azure Cosmos DB and other destinations on Azure. 


OmniVec handles content extraction, chunking, and incremental sync out of the box. It supports Microsoft Foundry as well as self-hosted models. You get a web UI, CLI, and REST API for managing sources, models, destinations, and pipelines. 


The project is MIT-licensed and available on GitHub.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Integrated embeddings for Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL
items.description:
Building AI applications on Azure Cosmos DB just got simpler. With integrated embeddings, now in public preview, Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL can automatically generate and maintain embeddings for your data, without the need to build a separate pipeline. 


Now you can configure your container's vector embedding policy with one or more source properties, a target property, and a Microsoft Foundry model endpoint. Cosmos DB handles the rest: as items are created or updated, embeddings are generated and kept in sync automatically. 


Before this announcement, developers had to write integration code to call embedding APIs, build change-tracking logic to keep embeddings current, and manage the glue code that connects data changes to embedding generation. Integrated embeddings removes this entire layer of complexity, letting you focus on your application logic. 


 Azure OpenAI embedding models via Microsoft Foundry are supported in the initial release. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Safe key rotation for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
The safe key rotation feature helps you confidently rotate your Azure Cosmos DB account keys by providing visibility into when each key was last used. Without this insight, you risk rotating a key that may still be actively used by your applications, which can lead to unexpected service disruptions. 


With safe key rotation, you can identify active and inactive keys before taking action, enabling you to make informed decisions and improve your security posture. This capability supports safer migrations, including transitioning to Microsoft Entra ID, by ensuring keys are no longer in use before disabling access. By reducing operational risk and increasing transparency, safe key rotation helps you maintain application reliability while strengthening key management practices.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Agent Memory Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can now accelerate the development of agentic applications with the new Agent Memory Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB. This toolkit provides a customizable, code-first solution to help you build scalable, durable, and cost-efficient memory systems for your AI agents, without having to design complex pipelines from scratch. 


With the Agent Memory Toolkit, you can easily store, update, and retrieve agent memories using a simple interface, while the toolkit handles key tasks such as data processing, embedding generation, and retrieval orchestration behind the scenes using Azure Durable Functions. The toolkit eliminates the need to manually integrate multiple services and simplifies a common architecture pattern used for agent memory systems. 


You benefit from faster time to production, improved retrieval relevance, and a more consistent and scalable memory foundation for your applications. Whether you are building conversational agents, copilots, or multi-agent workflows, the toolkit helps you focus on your application logic instead of infrastructure. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Semantic reranker in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can now improve the relevance of any Cosmos DB query or search with the public preview of semantic reranker in Azure Cosmos DB. Semantic reranker analyzes the meaning of your queries and your data to reorder results based on contextual relevance rather than keyword matching alone. This ranking is especially useful for AI-powered applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), question answering, and agentic apps. 


With semantic reranker, you can deliver more precise and reliable results without building complex ranking pipelines or tuning scoring logic manually. It works directly with your existing Cosmos DB queries—including vector, full-text, and hybrid search—enabling you to quickly enhance result quality while maintaining low operational overhead.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Agentic Retrieval Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
We are announcing the public preview of the Agentic Retrieval Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB. Motivated by GraphRAG and multiple-hop reasoning problems, this new capability helps you build advanced retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications that go beyond single-pass retrieval by dynamically identifying information gaps and iteratively retrieving additional context. The toolkit combines hybrid search across vector and full-text indexes, diversity-aware document selection, and multiple-round reasoning to produce more complete, grounded responses. 


With agentic retrieval, you can improve answer quality for complex, multiple-step questions where relevant information is spread across many documents or data sources. The retrieval pipeline adapts in real time by generating follow-up queries, retrieving new evidence, and refining responses until it has sufficient coverage. This approach reduces redundancy, increases recall, and delivers higher-fidelity results for copilots, agents, and knowledge-intensive applications built on Azure Cosmos DB. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB global secondary indexes
items.description:
Global secondary indexes (GSIs) for Azure Cosmos DB are now generally available, giving you a powerful way to accelerate query performance without adding complexity to your application code. GSIs are read-only containers that automatically stay in sync with your source container using the change feed. Each GSI has its own throughput, partition key, and indexing policy, so you can optimize them for any query pattern. 


With GSIs, you can convert expensive cross-partition queries into efficient single-partition lookups by storing data under a different partition key. Using GSIs means lower Request Unit (RU) consumption, reduced latency, and better performance isolation for your workloads. You can isolate a subset of your workload, such as creating vector or full-text search indexes in the GSI to support AI applications, without impacting transactional operations on the source container. 


Adding a GSI to a new or existing container allows you to maintain query efficiency even as your workload requirements evolve.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management adds support for Agent-to-Agent (A2A) APIs
items.description:
As organizations build more agentic applications, agent-to-agent communication is becoming a critical part of enterprise AI systems. But in many environments, agent traffic operates outside existing API governance layers — making it difficult to apply consistent security, visibility, and operational controls.  

With support for JSON-RPC–based A2A APIs, Azure API Management enables platform teams and developers to manage agent interactions alongside REST, GraphQL, MCP tools, and AI model APIs using the same API management platform they already rely on. This allows organizations to apply existing security, mediation, and governance policies to agent traffic, observe and trace agent interactions end-to-end, and manage agent APIs within a unified operational model instead of introducing separate gateways or disconnected tooling for agents.  

By bringing A2A APIs into the same governance and observability framework as the broader API ecosystem, Azure API Management helps organizations scale agentic systems with enterprise-grade security, control, and operational consistency.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management workspaces now support the built-in gateway
items.description:
Organizations using workspace-based API management models previously needed a dedicated workspace gateway and Premium tier deployment to take advantage of API Management workspaces increasing both cost and operational complexity.  

With this update, Azure API Management customers can now associate workspaces directly with the built-in gateway, extending workspace support across additional tiers and all regions supported by API Management. This helps organizations:  

  • Use workspaces in any API Management tier (except for Consumption)  
  • Create workspaces in any region supported by API Management  
  • Take advantage of built-in gateway capabilities that are not available in workspace gateways, such as multi-region deployments, custom hostnames, or Private Link connectivity  

By bringing workspaces to the built-in gateway, Azure API Management makes it easier and more cost-effective for organizations to adopt team-based API governance and delegated API management models at scale.  

This feature is currently rolling out to v2 tiers of API Management and will start rolling out to classic tiers around July or August.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management now supports AI gateway capabilities for Anthropic and Vertex AI models.
items.description:
As organizations integrate external AI providers into production applications, platform teams need consistent ways to secure, govern, and observe model interactions across providers. Without centralized controls and telemetry, managing compliance, troubleshooting issues, and monitoring usage becomes increasingly difficult.  

With this update, Azure API Management extends AI gateway capabilities to Anthropic and Google Vertex AI models, enabling organizations to apply runtime policies, security controls, and observability across external model endpoints.  

This allows teams to:  

  • Apply runtime governance and security policies, such as content safety, token limits, or semantic caching, for Anthropic and Vertex AI models  
  • Collect logs, traces, and metrics for Anthropic and Vertex AI model traffic   

By extending policy enforcement and observability to Anthropic and Vertex AI models, Azure API Management helps organizations operate multi-model AI environments with stronger consistency, security, and enterprise control. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Logic Apps Codeful Workflows with Logic Apps Standard SDK.
items.description:
Modern integration and automation teams increasingly want the flexibility of writing workflows directly in code while still benefiting from managed orchestration, enterprise connectors, and cloud-scale operational capabilities. Traditional workflow models can create friction for pro developers who prefer imperative programming patterns and code-first development experiences.  

With Codeful Workflows, Azure Logic Apps extends Logic Apps Standard with a code-first authoring and execution model built on .NET and a first-class Logic Apps Standard SDK. This allows developers to:  

  • Implement and structure workflows directly in code using imperative programming patterns  
  • Develop, and test workflows locally, running workflows locally and in the cloud.  
  • Leverage Logic Apps Standard connectors and operational capabilities from code-first workflows 
  • Accelerate workflow development using familiar .NET tooling and AI-assisted code generation  

By bringing a code-first experience to Logic Apps, Codeful Workflows helps organizations empower traditional developers to build integration and business process workflows faster without needing to create and maintain custom orchestration frameworks or boilerplate integration code.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Logic Apps MCP Server.
items.description:
As organizations adopt AI agents and MCP-based tooling, integration teams often need to build and maintain custom API layers just to make existing workflows callable by agents. This additional plumbing increases development effort, operational complexity, and time to production.  

With the GA release of the Azure Logic Apps MCP Server, developers can now expose existing Logic Apps workflows as MCP-compatible tools that AI agents can directly discover and invoke — without writing custom API code. This allows teams to:  

  • Expose existing Logic Apps workflows as AI-callable MCP tools in minutes  
  • Enable discovery and invocation from agent platforms such as Microsoft Foundry and Copilot Studio  
  • Reuse existing enterprise automation and integration logic within AI workflows  
  • Reduce the complexity and overhead of building custom integration layers for agents  

By enabling Logic Apps workflows to participate directly in MCP-based agent ecosystems, the Logic Apps MCP Server helps organizations accelerate agentic automation while maximizing reuse of existing enterprise integrations.

items.title: Public preview: Connector Namespace
items.description:
Integrating apps with SaaS and line-of-business systems today means writing custom API client code, managing credentials, and handling retries, pagination, and webhooks for every service.

Connector Namespace is a fully managed service providing pre-built connectors to services like SharePoint, Salesforce, Outlook, and SAP. Each connector exposes typed actions and event triggers through a shared connection model, while the platform handles auth, credential rotation, polling, webhook delivery, and remote MCP hosting.

Key features: 

  • Managed connections: reusable, authenticated bindings with built-in credential storage and rotation 
  • Strongly-typed SDKs for C#, Node.js, and Python, plus HTTP access  
  • Managed connector MCP servers hosting: deploy connector-as-MCP-server so agents can invote them as tools with custom wrappers 
  • Hosted MCP servers: deploy from a catalog of supported servers with managed dependencies, configuration, auth, and more 
  • Flexible compute: use with Azure Functions, Container Apps, App Service, or your own infra 
  • Enterprise security: VNet, private endpoints, RBAC, and Azure Monitor built in.  

With Connector Namespace, you integrate apps and AI agents through a consistent model, reuse connections, go from connector to MCP server in minutes, and let the platform handle auth and reliability so you ship faster with fewer moving parts. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management now supports content safety controls for MCP and A2A APIs.
items.description:
As organizations deploy more agentic applications and MCP-based tools, enforcing consistent safety and compliance policies across agent interactions becomes increasingly important. Many teams today rely on fragmented or custom implementations for content filtering and policy enforcement, creating operational complexity and increasing risk.  

With this update, Azure API Management extends content safety capabilities to MCP tools and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) APIs, enabling centralized enforcement of safety controls across agent-based workflows.  

This allows organizations to:  

  • Apply consistent content safety policies across models, MCP tools, and A2A agent interactions  
  • Reduce the risk of unsafe, harmful, or non-compliant outputs  
  • Centralize governance and policy enforcement for agentic systems  

By bringing content safety controls into the API management layer, Azure API Management helps organizations operate AI agents and MCP ecosystems with stronger governance, compliance, and enterprise-grade safeguards.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure API Management now supports token metrics for all token types
items.description:
As organizations adopt advanced AI models, understanding token consumption is becoming more complex. Traditional metrics focused primarily on prompt and completion tokens often fail to capture newer token categories such as cached, reasoning, or thinking tokens — limiting cost visibility and operational insight.  

With this update, Azure API Management now enables organizations to log metrics for a broader range of token types into Application Insights, extending observability beyond standard token tracking. This allows teams to:  

  • Track usage for cached, reasoning, thinking, and other token types, in addition to previously supported prompt, completion, and total tokens  
  • Collect token metrics across model providers and API formats, including OpenAI Chat Completions API, OpenAI Responses API, and Anthropic Messages API models across Microsoft Foundry, OpenAI, Amazon AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and other providers  
  • Build more accurate dashboards for AI consumption and cost analysis  
  • Improve budget monitoring and alerting across AI workloads  
  • Gain deeper operational visibility into evolving model behaviors and token economics  

By expanding token observability, Azure API Management helps organizations better manage AI usage, optimize costs, and improve governance across modern generative AI applications.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management Premium v2 now supports multiple custom domains
items.description:
Organizations often need to expose APIs, developer portals, and management endpoints under different branded or organizational domain names- — for example, api.contoso.com for external partners, apis.hrportal.contoso.com for an internal HR platform, and dev.europe.contoso.com for a regional developer portal. Until now, achieving this level of separation frequently required additional API Management instances, increasing operational complexity and cost.  

With this update, Azure API Management Premium v2 enables multiple custom domains within a single instance across gateway, developer portal, and management endpoints. This allows organizations to:  

  • Configure distinct hostnames for different endpoints and audiences  
  • Align API experiences with business units, products, or regional brands  
  • Simplify domain-scoped networking and security policies  
  • Reduce the need for separate APIM instances solely for domain separation  

For enterprises managing large and distributed API estates, this provides greater flexibility in how APIs and developer experiences are exposed while improving operational efficiency and maintaining centralized governance.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager for Arc-enabled clusters
items.description:
Managing Kubernetes clusters across hybrid and multi-cloud environments is fragmented by default: different consoles, different tools, different operational models. Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager now supports Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes in GA, so any CNCF-compliant distribution can join a fleet as a member cluster.

Once Arc-enabled clusters are joined as members, teams get centralized visibility into cluster health across their entire Kubernetes estate. From there, Fleet Manager's intelligent workload placement distributes namespaces, configurations, and applications across any member cluster, regardless of where it runs.

For customers running mixed estates today, this reduces reliance on third-party multi-cluster tools (and the ongoing licensing that comes with them) while keeping a consistent operational model across AKS, on-premises, and other clouds.

Learn more

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Center now supports agent registration, agent assessment, and Git-based synchronization.
items.description:
As organizations increasingly build autonomous AI agents to automate workflows and orchestrate enterprise tasks, developers need a centralized way to discover, govern, and reuse these capabilities across teams.  

With this update, Azure API Center enables teams to:  

  • Register new agents directly into the enterprise catalog  
  • Automatically ingest and synchronize agents from Git repositories  
  • Keep agent definitions aligned with evolving source-controlled codebases  
  • Make production-ready agents discoverable and reusable across the organization  
  • Assess agent quality before catalog registration using an automated LLM-as-a-Judge framework that scores agents across safety, reliability, and behavioral completeness  

Agents are becoming foundational enterprise assets capable of planning, reasoning, and executing multi-step tasks on behalf of applications and developers. By bringing them into a governed catalog, Azure API Center helps teams reduce duplication, improve reuse, and accelerate AI application development. This enables developers to confidently discover and integrate trusted agents without needing to rebuild capabilities that already exist elsewhere in the organization.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Center now provides a data plane MCP server for enterprise-wide discovery of APIs and AI assets.
items.description:
As organizations adopt MCP-based tooling and AI agents at scale, developers need a simpler way to discover and connect to the growing ecosystem of enterprise MCP servers, tools, APIs, and AI assets.  

With this update, Azure API Center introduces a data plane MCP server that acts as a unified enterprise discovery endpoint — enabling agents and developer tools to access the full catalog of registered MCP servers, tools, APIs, and AI assets through a single connection.  

This enables teams to:  

  • Provide agents with centralized access to enterprise APIs and AI assets  
  • Eliminate the need to manually configure connections to individual MCP servers  
  • Automatically expose newly registered MCP servers and tools without reconfiguration  
  • Simplify discovery and consumption across a rapidly growing enterprise catalog  

By acting as a unified enterprise discovery endpoint, Azure API Center helps organizations operationalize AI ecosystems with stronger discoverability, governance, and developer productivity — while reducing integration complexity for agentic applications.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally available: Generally available: Managed system node pools in AKS Automatic
items.description:
Provisioning and maintaining system node pools in AKS requires ongoing work to handle scaling, patching, and availability. Managed system node pools in AKS Automatic remove that responsibility. The platform provisions and operates the infrastructure for core Kubernetes system components, so teams do not need to create, scale, or update system node pools.

System workloads run separately from application workloads, reducing contention and improving application reliability. Platform-managed updates also keep system components current without manual intervention. For teams running production workloads on AKS, this removes a layer of cluster management and simplifies day-to-day operations.

Learn more

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Logic Apps Automation SKU for agentic business process automation.
items.description:
As organizations move toward agentic automation, developers increasingly need a simpler way to combine workflows, APIs, and AI agents into production-ready business processes. Today, building these systems often requires stitching together multiple Azure services, managing infrastructure complexity, and creating custom orchestration layers across workflows and AI agents.  

With the new Azure Logic Apps Automation SKU, developers can build AI-driven business process automation using Logic Apps workflows and Microsoft Foundry Hosted Agents within a unified platform experience.  

This enables pro developers, startup engineers, SaaS builders, and enterprise development teams to:  

  • Orchestrate workflows, APIs, and Foundry Hosted Agents together in a single platform  
  • Rapidly build and scale AI-driven business processes  
  • Create or invoke Foundry agents directly within workflow automation  
  • Use built-in evaluation, guardrails, and observability capabilities for production-grade AI automation  
  • Reduce infrastructure setup and operational complexity across agentic systems  

As the market shifts toward agentic business process automation, the Logic Apps Automation SKU helps organizations combine deterministic workflows and AI-driven reasoning into scalable enterprise automation powered by Azure’s enterprise foundation and Microsoft Foundry AI capabilities.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Knowledge as a Service with Azure Logic Apps.
items.description:
Most RAG implementations today are complex. Teams must build ingestion pipelines, manage chunking and embeddings, configure vector stores, wire up retrieval layers, and then operate the entire system in production.  

With Azure Logic Apps, RAG becomes a native workflow capability instead of a custom infrastructure project. Developers can:  

  • Upload documents directly into a workflow  
  • Automatically ingest, chunk, and vectorize content  
  • Use retrieval as a built-in workflow step  
  • Build grounded and personalized AI experiences without managing separate RAG infrastructure  

This fundamentally changes the developer experience from building and operating RAG pipelines to simply using retrieval within application logic and automation workflows. By collapsing complex RAG orchestration into a few workflow steps, Azure Logic Apps helps developers move faster from prototype to production for grounded AI agents and intelligent business applications.

items.title: Public Preview: Anyscale on Azure
items.description:
Now in Public Preview, Anyscale on Azure is a cloud-native managed Ray platform for machine learning engineers and AI developers who need to run Python workloads at massive scale without compromising speed or control. It brings the power of Ray’s distributed execution together with Azure Kubernetes Service to create a purpose-built platform for modern, large-scale AI systems. Anyscale on Azure helps AI teams move from a single-machine experiment to production-grade systems running across hundreds or thousands of CPUs and GPUs both in Azure Kubernetes clusters.  By eliminating the infrastructure and distributed systems burden, teams can focus on building better models, iterating faster, and shipping AI into real products.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Logic Apps now enables developers to invoke Microsoft Foundry Agents directly from workflows.
items.description:
Organizations building AI agents often face a disconnect between where agents are built and where business processes are automated. Now, with improved integration between Azure AI Foundry and Azure Logic Apps, developers can now more easily operationalize Foundry AI agents within enterprise workflows.  

Azure AI Foundry provides the platform where agents are built, grounded, evaluated, and hosted using enterprise data, models, and tools. Azure Logic Apps provides the orchestration layer where workflows, APIs, schedules, and business events trigger and coordinate enterprise processes.  

Together, this enables developers to:  

  • Invoke Foundry Hosted Agents directly from Logic Apps workflows  
  • Orchestrate agents alongside APIs, connectors, and enterprise systems  
  • Trigger AI-driven workflows from business events or schedules  
  • Run production-grade agentic business processes with built-in observability and scale  

This integration helps organizations operationalize AI agents within real-world business automation workflows.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB all versions and deletes change feed mode
items.description:
The Azure Cosmos DB all versions and deletes change feed mode is now generally available, giving you complete visibility into every change that happens in your containers. Unlike the default latest version mode, which surfaces only the most recent state of an item, all versions and deletes captures every create, update, and delete operation in the order it occurred, including intermediate changes between reads and TTL expirations. 


This mode opens up scenarios that were previously difficult to build. You can replicate data between locations without implementing soft deletes, trigger logic on every incremental change even when multiple updates happen between polls, and set up auditing workflows that fire on delete operations. Each change includes metadata identifying the operation type, so your application can handle creates, updates, and deletes with distinct processing logic. 


To get started, enable continuous backups on your Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL account, which automatically creates the all versions and deletes change log. You can then consume it through the change feed pull model or change feed processor in supported SDKs. Changes are available to read within your configured continuous backup retention period. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: New Azure Cosmos DB cost estimator
items.description:
Plan your Azure Cosmos DB deployment with confidence. The Azure Cosmos DB cost estimator is now in public preview, giving you a fast, accurate way to model throughput, storage, regions, and capacity mode before you provision a single account. Whether you are building a new transactional app, modernizing a legacy database, or pricing out AI workloads with vector search, the estimator turns your design choices into a monthly cost projection in minutes. The pricing model reflects current Azure list rates and Microsoft's canonical vector cost methodology, so you can compare configurations, share a quote with your team, and walk into your next architecture review with a number you trust. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Change partition keys in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL API
items.description:
You can now change the partition key of an Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL container directly from the Azure portal with just a few clicks. The process supports both online and offline modes by copying data from the source container to a new container through the Change Partition Key option in Data Explorer.


Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Introducing AI Assistant in the Azure Cosmos DB extension for Visual Studio Code
items.description:
You can now use AI assistance in the Azure Cosmos DB extension for Visual Studio Code to work with your data faster and with less manual effort. You can ask questions in plain English and get optimized Azure Cosmos DB queries, use chat participant commands to explain and refine queries, and rely on intelligent auto completion while writing queries and code. 


You also get an Azure Cosmos DB Shell experience powered by Model Context Protocol (MCP), so the agent can use Shell operations to navigate your databases and containers and execute the right queries for you. You can spend less time on syntax, reduce trial-and-error, and move from idea to insight more quickly. Whether you are exploring data, troubleshooting queries, or building application logic, you get a more guided and productive development experience directly in Visual Studio Code. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: MCP Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can use the MCP Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB, now in general availability, to connect your AI agents and copilots to operational data with enterprise-ready reliability. This release gives you a standardized way to expose Cosmos DB capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP), so your teams can build faster, reduce custom integration effort, and scale agent experiences with more confidence. You get a production-focused foundation for secure access patterns, easier tool integration across your AI workflows, and a clearer path from prototype to real-world deployment. 


Whether you are modernizing existing Cosmos DB applications or launching new agentic solutions, this release helps you deliver data-aware experiences more quickly while maintaining the control and consistency your organization expects.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Per-partition automatic failover for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
Per-partition automatic failover (PPAF) is now generally available in Azure Cosmos DB, bringing faster recovery and higher availability to your mission-critical applications. 


With PPAF, you no longer need to fail over an entire account during a regional disruption. Azure Cosmos DB automatically fails over only the impacted partitions, while healthy partitions continue serving traffic. This approach sharply reduces disruption, shortens recovery times, and removes the need for manual intervention during outages. 


PPAF helps you meet stringent availability and durability requirements without redesigning your application or operating multiple write regions. You can run highly resilient workloads with predictable performance, while Azure Cosmos DB transparently handles partition-level recovery behind the scenes.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Cosmos DB distributed transactions
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of distributed transactions in Azure Cosmos DB. You can now perform atomic operations across items and partitions, with changes committing together or rolling back automatically on failure. 


Distributed transactions eliminate the need for complex application logic to coordinate updates, helping you preserve data integrity and simplify application design. This capability integrates seamlessly with Azure Cosmos DB's consistency and availability models, providing predictable behavior as your applications scale.


Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Relational Database to Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL Migration Assistant
items.description:
You can now more easily migrate from relational databases such as Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and MySQL to Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. The Migration Assistant in the Azure Cosmos DB extension for Visual Studio Code guides you through a structured workflow: discovery, assessment, schema conversion and provisioning. It uses GitHub Copilot language models and Azure Cosmos DB Agent Kit skills to analyze your application and schema, generate a target NoSQL design with ready-to-provision containers, and convert the application code. All migration artifacts are saved to a .cosmosdb-migration project folder in your workspace so you can pause, resume, inspect, modify and share the outputs as part of your normal development process. 


Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Service-managed failover in Azure DocumentDB
items.description:
Azure DocumentDB is excited to announce the general availability of service-managed failover for multi-region clusters. In the event of a regional outage, Azure DocumentDB will automatically fail over the globally distributed cluster from the primary region to the secondary region, without any user intervention needed. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Graceful failover with zero data loss guarantee
items.description:
Azure DocumentDB is excited to announce the general availability of graceful failovers that promote replica clusters while guaranteeing zero data loss. This feature is an addition to the already existing force promote feature, which immediately promotes a replica cluster in the event of availability loss.


Force promote favors availability over consistency and thus does not wait for unreplicated data to make its way to the replica cluster before being promoted. 


With the graceful promote feature, you can now promote a regional cluster to the primary in the event of changing application traffic patterns. This feature is ideal when there is no availability loss on the primary but simply a change in traffic that requires database requests to be made to the closer regional cluster.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Change streams (multi-shard) in Azure DocumentDB
items.description:
You can build real-time, event-driven applications with change streams in Azure DocumentDB, now in public preview and featuring multi-node support. You can capture live data changes with controlled polling, helping you power instant analytics, automation, and synchronization across distributed systems while reducing operational overhead. 

You can start streams from any point in the last 30 days to support replay, recovery, and backfill scenarios, giving you greater flexibility in handling delayed or missed events. You gain deeper visibility into changes with enhanced update descriptions, and pre-image support provides access to the document state before updates for auditing and compliance needs. 

You can also fine-tune performance with improved polling through configurable MaxAwaitTimeMs, allowing better control over latency and resource usage. With native support across major drivers including —Python, C#, Node.js, and Go— along with integrations for Apache Kafka and Azure Functions, you can seamlessly integrate change streams into your workflows and scale your applications with confidence.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure DocumentDB Migration Extension in Visual Studio Code
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of the Azure DocumentDB Migration Extension for Visual Studio Code. With this release, you can create, run, and manage migration jobs directly from Visual Studio Code to move data from your on-premises or cloud-based MongoDB deployments to Azure DocumentDB. 


You no longer need to provision extra infrastructure or rely on complex migration tooling. Instead, you can use a familiar developer environment to plan and execute migrations with secure connectivity, zero additional cost, and precise control over the databases and collections you want to move. 


This release helps you simplify modernization projects, reduce migration effort, and minimize disruption to your applications by enabling migrations without service interruptions. Whether you are moving a single workload or multiple databases, you can complete the process faster while maintaining flexibility and visibility throughout the migration journey. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure DocumentDB instant free tier clusters
items.description:
With near-instant provisioning of free tier clusters, you can get started immediately on Azure DocumentDB. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB is a PostgreSQL-compatible database service engineered for performance and built for what's next. It delivers future-proof autoscaling storage up to 128 TB, up to three times faster performance than self-managed PostgreSQL, and rapid compute scalability reaching 3,072 vCores, so you can support your most demanding workloads with confidence. 

Now available in public preview, Azure HorizonDB is designed for mission-critical applications that require enterprise-grade security, reliability, and scale. With Azure HorizonDB, you can build smarter, more scalable applications using in-database, pre-provisioned AI models; advanced capabilities like DiskANN vector indexing for fast, filtered vector search; and native semantic operators that enable intelligent query experiences. Familiar PostgreSQL extensions and seamless GitHub Copilot integration help streamline development so teams can move from idea to impact faster. Integrated into the Microsoft ecosystem, Azure HorizonDB makes it easy to connect to Azure AI and analytics services without added complexity, so you can focus on innovation, not integration. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure HorizonDB Agentic Advisor Solution Accelerator
items.description:
Agentic Advisor Solution Accelerator for Azure HorizonDB is now generally available. You can use this financial services-focused reference solution to build multi-agent applications in Python using LangGraph and Mem0, with Azure HorizonDB as the data and intelligence layer. 


The accelerator demonstrates how you can combine advanced graph generation and querying, hybrid search with full-text search, DiskANN advanced filtering, and Azure HorizonDB AI functions to create more context-aware, explainable, and responsive advisor experiences. With this accelerator, you can jump-start development of agentic applications that reason over structured, unstructured, and relationship-rich data while using Azure HorizonDB's built-in AI capabilities to simplify retrieval, memory, and decision support workflows. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Advanced filtering for DiskANN vector search in Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Advanced filtering for DiskANN vector search in Azure HorizonDB is now available in public preview. With this release, you can combine vector similarity search with metadata filters such as category, date range, price, or tenant ID without the performance penalties that typically come with filtered vector queries. DiskANN advanced filtering delivers lower latency on filtered vector search compared to traditional approaches, enabling you to build AI-powered retrieval applications that are both precise and fast at scale. Whether you are building an agentic application, a product recommendation engine, or an enterprise search experience, you can now apply complex filters alongside vector similarity in a single query and get results in milliseconds, even across millions of vectors. This capability runs natively inside your Azure HorizonDB instance alongside your relational data, eliminating the need for a separate vector database or external search service. You retain full transactional consistency, use familiar PostgreSQL SQL, and benefit from DiskANN's industry-leading performance on disk-resident indexes. Advanced filtering works seamlessly with pgvector, Azure AI integrations, and the broader HorizonDB AI retrieval stack, including BM25 full-text search and graph traversal. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: BM25 full-text search in Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
BM25 full-text search is now available in public preview for Azure HorizonDB. Now you can get production-quality keyword search powered by BM25, the same relevance ranking algorithm used by Elasticsearch, Solr, and Azure AI Search, running entirely inside your PostgreSQL database as a native extension. 


You no longer need to deploy and manage a separate search service to get high-quality text search. The full-text search extension replaces PostgreSQL's built-in ts_rank with BM25 scoring, which delivers significantly better relevance through term frequency saturation, document length normalization, and inverse document frequency weighting. It's faster than native PostgreSQL full-text search with Generalized Inverted Index (GIN) indexes on complex, multi-keyword queries. The extension also supports fuzzy matching for typo tolerance, phrase search with configurable word proximity, and Boolean query syntax (AND, OR, NOT) capabilities that previously required an external search engine. 


By combining pgvector with DiskANN for vector similarity search, you can now build hybrid search applications that deliver both keyword precision and semantic understanding in a single SQL query using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Your data stays in one place, you use familiar PostgreSQL, and you eliminate the operational burden of syncing data to an external search service. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: MCP toolkit for Azure DocumentDB
items.description:
Azure DocumentDB now supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), available in public preview. With the MCP toolkit, you can connect AI agents and LLM-powered applications directly to your DocumentDB database, enabling natural language queries, document retrieval, and data operations without writing custom integration code. 


You can build agentic workflows that read and write to your DocumentDB collections, perform vector similarity search, and retrieve contextually relevant documents as part of a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline. These capabilities are exposed through a standardized protocol that works with any MCP-compatible AI client.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL Database provisioning in the MSSQL extension
items.description:
The MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code now introduces Azure SQL Database provisioning in public preview, starting with the free tier so you can create and connect to a fully managed cloud database directly from your editor at no cost. 


With a guided wizard on the Deployments page, you authenticate with your Azure account, then configure your subscription, resource group, server, and database on a single page. Your connection is added automatically the moment provisioning completes. You never leave Visual Studio Code, and you don't have to pay to get started. You choose what happens when the free monthly limit is reached: auto-pause until the next calendar month or continue at standard serverless rates. 


Whether you are prototyping a new application, validating a proof of concept, or experimenting with vector search and AI-ready workloads, you now have a fully managed Azure SQL Database ready to query in minutes. From there, you can continue into Schema Designer, where GitHub Copilot helps you design and evolve your data model visually. You can then go to data API builder, where GitHub Copilot generates back-end endpoints directly from your schema. Together, these experiences give you an end-to-end path from a provisioned database to a working back end, all inside Visual Studio Code. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Data API builder with built-in GitHub Copilot in MSSQL extension
items.description:
The MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code now offers data API builder with built-in GitHub Copilot integration as generally available, bringing guided back-end generation into your development workflow. 


You can generate REST, GraphQL, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints from your SQL database schema inside Visual Studio Code without manually configuring infrastructure or connection strings. You select tables, define CRUD operations, and configure settings such as authorization roles, primary keys, route behavior, and column-level exposure through an API design interface. 


The generated data API builder configuration file stays synchronized with your selections, can be previewed in the extension, and added to your workspace for transparency and version control. You can modify it manually or use GitHub Copilot to plan and generate updates. 


This release also streamlines endpoint design, configuration review, and guided generation. You can now go beyond table-level selection and choose which columns are exposed in the generated API. Columns are exposed by default, but you can turn off exposure for sensitive, unsupported, or unnecessary fields such as password hashes, social security numbers, internal flags, or stale data. 


With a few steps, the extension runs a local data API builder container using your database connection. This workflow helps you move from validated schema to a working back end, so you can build faster without switching tools. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: GitHub Copilot integration in Schema Designer for the MSSQL extension
items.description:
The GitHub Copilot integration with Schema Designer is now generally available in the MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code, expanding the visual schema design experience with AI-assisted capabilities. Based on developer feedback and evolving workflows, this integration enables you to explore, design, and modify database schemas using natural language.

You can describe the tables or changes you want, and GitHub Copilot plans and generates proposed updates inside Schema Designer. Each schema change is previewed visually, color-coded, and tracked in a dedicated Change Tracking panel with familiar source control-style labels such as Add (A), Modify (M), and Delete (D). You can clearly differentiate between your own edits and AI-generated suggestions, inspect detailed modifications, and review changes before they are applied.

Moreover, Schema Designer now supports ORM script generation for migration, helping you move from visual schema changes to migration-ready scripts more efficiently. Whether you’re starting a new project or updating an existing one, this guided experience helps you move confidently from an idea to a validated data model.

From there, you can continue into Data API builder in the MSSQL extension, where GitHub Copilot plans and generates back-end endpoints from your schema. Together, these experiences give you an end-to-end path from database design to a working back end in minutes.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL updates for June
items.description:
In June 2026, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL: 
Execute SQL queries, document with Markdown, and mix kernels like Python using SQL Notebooks in the MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server self-service quota management experience
items.description:
Managing your quota is now faster, simpler, and more transparent. Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server supports self-service quota management through the Azure Quotas blade in the Azure portal. You can view your current quota usage and limits, request quota increases, and track the status of your requests all directly from the portal without needing to file a support ticket. 


Previously, requesting a quota increase required you to navigate to Help + Support and submit a support request, which could take 24 to 48 hours to process. Now, you can submit quota adjustment requests through the centralized Azure Quotas experience, where eligible requests are evaluated and approved automatically, significantly reducing wait times. 


This streamlined experience gives you real-time visibility into quota utilization across your subscriptions, helping you plan for capacity needs and avoid deployment interruptions.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for MySQL now available in new regions and expanded availability zones
items.description:
Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server continues to expand its global footprint with new regional availability and enhanced availability zone support. You can now deploy Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server in the Denmark East, Austria East, and Belgium Central regions, bringing Azure-managed MySQL closer to your workloads with full support for zone-redundant high availability and geo-redundant backup. This update enables you to meet local data residency requirements while taking advantage of enterprise-grade reliability and low-latency access. 


Additionally, several regions have been expanded with a new availability zone: Taiwan North, Japan West, South Central US, and US Gov Arizona. This support gives you more options for distributing your workloads across physically separate datacenters within the region. You can build resilient, zone-redundant architectures and improve capacity availability for mission-critical MySQL deployments. 


These updates reinforce our commitment to providing you with a globally distributed, highly available managed MySQL service. To get started, visit the Azure portal to create or migrate your Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server in these regions. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Benchmark evaluations for fine-tuned models in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Choosing the right AI system is rarely as simple as picking the newest or largest model — and agents add their own layer of variability on top. A model that wins on a public leaderboard can still underperform on the reasoning, math, or domain-knowledge questions that matter for your application, and an agent that solves one task well can regress on another after a prompt or tool change. The only way to know is to measure, on the same benchmark, under the same conditions, every time something changes. 

Benchmarks in Microsoft Foundry (preview) make that kind of measurement a first-class part of the development workflow. You can run well-known open-source benchmarks against any model deployment or agent in your project, compare runs side by side in the evaluation group view, and drive the whole flow from the portal or the REST API. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Deployment Templates support packaging deployment configurations in registries for curated deployment
items.description:
Deployment templates in Azure Machine Learning add public preview support for deploying from registries, expanding the set of model registries that customers can use as the source for a templated deployment. Deployment templates package a model, deployment configuration, and container information into a reusable artifact that platform teams can share with development teams. This update makes it easier for platform owners to standardize how a team deploys curated models from registries, while preserving governance through the template itself. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: CLI and SDK support for Deployment Templates
items.description:
Deployment templates in Azure Machine Learning add CLI and SDK support in public preview, so platform teams can create, update, delete, and manage templates from infrastructure-as-code pipelines instead of only the portal. The new commands work with az ml deployment-template create, list, show, update, and delete, and the Python SDK exposes the same operations through the azure-ai-ml client. Teams can check deployment templates into Git, review them in pull requests, and manage them through Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions exactly like other Azure resources. They can deploy the model packaged with deployment templates by using az ml online-deployment create or the equivalent operation in the SDK. This enables repeatable, auditable rollouts of standardized model deployments across many projects in an organization without manual portal steps. 

Learn more

items.title: Generally Available: Speech SDK 1.50 for Azure AI Speech
items.description:
Speech SDK 1.50 ships as a generally available release across all supported languages: C#, C++, Java, JavaScript, Python, Objective-C, Swift, and Go. The release rolls up the latest speech-to-text and text-to-speech features behind a stable API surface and is published to the standard NuGet, Maven, npm, PyPI, and CocoaPods feeds. Existing apps can move to 1.50 with a package version bump in most cases. The SDK continues to support real-time and offline scenarios against local devices, files, Azure Blob Storage, and input/output streams. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Region-agnostic reservations for Global PTU in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry adds region-agnostic reservations for Global Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) at general availability, letting customers commit to PTU capacity once and consume it from any supported region. Previously, a reserved PTU commitment was tied to a single region, which created friction for customers that operated multi-region applications or wanted to shift workloads as traffic patterns changed. With region-agnostic reservations, finance teams can sign one reservation contract and engineering teams can deploy models in whichever Azure region best fits a given workload, with the reservation discount applied automatically. Reservations cover supported Foundry Models including Azure Direct first-party models such as GPT-5 and GPT-4.1. Existing region-bound reservations continue to honor their original terms. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: OneLake Catalog integration for Foundry IQ Knowledge Sources
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry IQ adds public preview support for OneLake Catalog as a knowledge source, so agents can ground responses on lakehouse tables, files, and shortcuts already governed in Microsoft Fabric. Data engineers register the OneLake catalog once and Foundry IQ ingests the cataloged items, respecting Fabric permissions and sensitivity labels at query time. Analysts get agent answers that cite the same curated datasets used in dashboards and reports, instead of duplicate copies sitting in a separate vector store. The integration removes a common gap between BI data and AI applications, letting customers reuse their Fabric investment for agent grounding. Setup uses the same connection flow as other Foundry IQ knowledge sources. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Image serving in Foundry IQ knowledge bases
items.description:
Foundry IQ knowledge bases now surface document-extracted images at query time in public preview. When ingestion pulls figures, screenshots, and diagrams out of PDFs, slides, and Office files, Foundry IQ retains each image alongside the text it appeared with and can return it as part of a retrieval result. Agents can show the original chart to the user instead of describing it secondhand, so answers about technical diagrams, product photos, and report figures stay anchored to the source artwork. Customers building support assistants, internal research tools, and knowledge portals can render visual context inline without building a separate image pipeline. The capability is available across all Foundry IQ-supported document types. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Managed identity for Foundry billing calls from Azure AI Search
items.description:
Azure AI Search now supports managed identity authentication for the billing operations it issues against Microsoft Foundry resources, replacing the prior key-based flow. Customers assign a system-assigned or user-assigned identity to the search service, grant it the appropriate role on the Foundry account, and skill executions that call Foundry models for embeddings, chat completions, or extraction bill through that identity. Security teams remove another long-lived secret from their environment, simplify rotation, and gain Entra-based audit trails for cross-service calls. The change is available in all regions where Azure AI Search and Microsoft Foundry are colocated, and applies to indexer skillsets that invoke Foundry models. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: GenAI prompt skill and chat completion in Azure AI Search knowledge sources
items.description:
Azure AI Search makes the GenAI prompt skill generally available, letting indexers call chat completion models during enrichment without custom code. Authors point the skill at a Foundry-hosted model, write a prompt template that references field values, and receive structured output written back to the index. The same chat completion capability is also available inside knowledge sources, so retrieval-augmented agents can run a quick model call against retrieved chunks before returning results. Customers use the skill for content classification, summarization, entity normalization, and field cleanup in the ingestion pipeline, replacing prior workflows that required separate functions or Logic Apps. Authentication supports managed identity, so calls stay inside the customer tenant. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Content Understanding extractionMode for documents
items.description:
Content Understanding in Microsoft Foundry now supports an extractionMode setting that lets you choose how documents are analyzed. Pick a layout-aware mode for structured documents where tables, sections, and reading order matter, or a faster text-only mode when you only need clean Markdown for downstream RAG indexing. The same Analyze API call returns field values with confidence scores and source grounding, so downstream automation can branch on whether human review is required. extractionMode is exposed in both the Foundry portal analyzer schema and the REST API, and is part of the GA `2025-11-01` API version. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer supports ASPX pages and Lists
items.description:
The Azure AI Search SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer now indexes ASPX site content and SharePoint Lists in addition to document libraries. The indexer connects through a Microsoft Entra application registration with application or delegated permissions, picks up new and changed items incrementally, and removes deleted items on the next run. Inclusion and exclusion rules let you scope ingestion to specific sites, libraries, lists, or folders, and additional columns can be brought through as searchable fields. The same indexer continues to support basic ACL preservation and Microsoft Purview sensitivity label ingestion in preview.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Purview sensitivity label auditing in Azure AI Search
items.description:
Azure AI Search now emits audit events for Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels carried alongside indexed documents. When the SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer is configured to preserve and honor sensitivity labels, query-time filtering decisions and label changes flow into Microsoft Purview activity logs. Security and compliance teams can review who queried labeled content, when label values changed, and how those changes affected search visibility. The capability builds on the existing sensitivity label ingestion preview and requires no schema changes to existing indexes. Configure auditing through your Microsoft Purview tenant settings. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Photo Avatar standard and custom in Azure AI Speech
items.description:
Photo Avatar in Azure AI Speech is now generally available in standard and custom flavors. Standard Photo Avatar produces a talking head video from a single photo at 512x512 resolution, and custom Photo Avatar lets you fine-tune the look from your own image with one minute of consent audio for the matching voice. Both modes run through the same batch synthesis and real-time synthesis APIs already used for video avatars, so existing avatar code paths keep working. Photo Avatar is built on the VASA-1 model family and integrates with Voice Live for low-latency, two-way conversational scenarios where you need a face on the agent. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Adaptive custom translation in the Azure AI Foundry NextGen playground
items.description:
Adaptive Custom Translation (AdaptCT) is generally available in the Azure AI Foundry NextGen playground for Azure Translator. AdaptCT enables enterprises to adapt translations to domain‑specific terminology using small datasets—eliminating the need for traditional model retraining. AdaptCT allows developers to update multilingual content in minutes by indexing high‑value examples and applying them dynamically at translation time (few-shot) to ground selected LLM. 

This approach helps organizations: 

  • Launch multilingual product features faster 
  • Maintain terminology consistency across evolving content 
  • Reduce operational overhead for translation workflows 
  • Deliver localized customer experiences at scale 

AdaptCT turns translation into an agile enabler for global growth—supporting real‑time updates across support content, product documentation, and dynamic digital experiences. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure AI Translator SDKs for the latest text translation API
items.description:
Azure AI Translator publishes generally available SDKs that target the latest text translation REST API across four languages: C#/.NET, Java, JavaScript, and Python. The SDKs expose Translator API v4 SDK to GA across all four supported programming languages, giving developers a single client surface to choose between traditional neural machine translation and LLM-based translation per request. Teams building multilingual products and support content have had to manage two parallel translation paths, with different SDKs, request shapes, and quality profiles, making it hard to mix models within one workflow. 

With the new SDK, developers can set the translation model, output tone, target gender, and adaptive settings on every call from the same Translator client. The release simplifies integration code, makes feature parity across .NET, Python, Java, and JavaScript clients consistent, and aligns the SDK surface with Translator API v4 capabilities including LLM model selection and the latest adaptive translation features.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Document translation for image files (synchronous, single document)
items.description:
Azure AI Translator now supports synchronous single-document image translation at general availability. Customers can submit a standalone image file (JPEG, PNG, and similar formats) through one synchronous API call and receive the translated result immediately, with original layout fidelity preserved. The service combines OCR and translation behind a single endpoint, so teams no longer need to build and maintain a custom OCR plus translation pipeline. Pricing is clear on a per-image basis, and the feature inherits the enterprise security posture and regional coverage of Document Translation. Common scenarios include real-time translation for mobile apps, retail signage, restaurant menus, kiosks, and form-based experiences. Early customers include Stanley Black and Decker, USCIS, and UD Trucks. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Content Understanding NextGen in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry brings Content Understanding into the portal in public preview, ending the context switch to the standalone Content Understanding Studio for everyday work. Developers get Read and Layout playgrounds inside Foundry for OCR text extraction and structural document analysis covering tables, figures, sections, and hyperlinks, all reachable through Foundry model discovery. Prebuilt document and image analyzers appear as first-class Foundry resources, with sample documents, upload, run, and results views in Markdown, table, or JSON. 

A direct bridge to Content Understanding Studio remains available for advanced workflows like custom analyzer creation, labeling, and performance tuning. Teams building document intelligence solutions can now manage models, agents, deployments, and document analyzers in one workspace. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Incremental SharePoint permissions sync for Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ
items.description:
Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ Knowledge Sources add incremental SharePoint permissions sync in public preview, keeping document-level, site, and library access control lists current as SharePoint permissions change. Enterprises store business-critical content in SharePoint and expect AI-powered search, RAG, and agent experiences to enforce the same access rules. 

Today, carrying SharePoint permissions forward into indexing workflows is partial, so downstream AI experiences can drift from current SharePoint state. With incremental sync, permission updates apply on every indexer run, removing the need for full re-indexing when ACLs change. Supported scopes cover document-level ACLs, site (ASPX) ACLs, and list and library ACLs. SharePoint policy evaluation stays out of scope. Security and compliance teams gain a more reliable foundation for enterprise agents and RAG apps built on SharePoint content. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: MCP Server Knowledge Source in Microsoft Foundry IQ
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry IQ now supports external MCP servers as federated knowledge sources in public preview, expanding retrieval beyond data customers index themselves. Teams can register MCP servers from systems like Salesforce, Atlassian, Confluence, and ServiceNow, then query them alongside indexed sources in a single agentic retrieval call. Foundry IQ handles cross-source selection automatically, choosing which sources to consult per query and merging results with citations. Because the federation uses MCP, partners and customers can plug in any compliant server without building a custom connector. Source-system permissions still gate the data, so an agent only retrieves records the calling user can see. This release helps organizations make agents useful against systems of record without copying data into a separate index. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Trace Replay and trace visualizations for Foundry agents
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry observability adds Trace Replay and new trace visualizations in public preview, giving agent developers a faster way to debug multi-step runs. The replay view rewinds a captured trace step by step, showing the model, tool, and inter-agent calls in the order they happened along with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage. Updated visualizations group nested spans by agent and tool so engineers can spot the step that introduced an error or a latency spike without scrolling through raw OpenTelemetry data. Traces flow into Azure Monitor Application Insights, so teams keep one observability backend for production AI workloads and the rest of their Azure services. Setup uses the existing Foundry tracing configuration.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Custom Avatar and Custom Video portal in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Azure AI Speech brings the Custom Avatar and Custom Video authoring experiences into the Microsoft Foundry portal in general availability. Approved customers can upload an actor's video recording, fine-tune a custom video avatar, and generate synthetic talking-head videos through the same Foundry project that runs their text-to-speech and Voice Live workloads. The portal also supports Photo Avatar, where a single reference image plus the Microsoft VASA model produces a head-only avatar. Customers can pair an avatar with a custom neural voice, a personal voice, or the new voice-sync-for-avatar option, then call the result through batch or real-time synthesis APIs. Custom Avatar remains a Limited Access feature gated by responsible AI review and an intake form. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Toolbox connectors and triggers in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry adds connectors and time-based triggers to the Foundry Tools toolbox in public preview, giving enterprise developers and automation engineers a native way to build event-driven AI agents. Foundry agents today are invoked only through direct API calls or user interactions, leaving teams to build custom orchestration outside Foundry whenever an agent needs to react to a business event. With this release, agents respond automatically to events from Microsoft 365, Azure, and third-party systems, and fire on schedules such as every day at 7am. Developers use the same centrally managed toolbox endpoint for discovery and authentication, while admins retain governance over which connectors and triggers are approved for enterprise use. Reactive, event-driven agent automation now ships without custom orchestration code or per-connector integration work. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Neural HD voice update (HDv2.5) in Azure AI Speech
items.description:
Azure AI Speech is rolling out an updated Neural HD text-to-speech model, moving customers from DragonHDLatest to HDv2.5. The update raises audio quality scores, adds style and paralinguistic tag support for English voices, and reduces word error rate in secondary locales such as Spanish, French, German, and Japanese. Customer-facing voice experiences (call center agents, IVR menus, assistant readouts) sound more natural and expressive without changes to the calling code; the existing endpoints and SSML markup continue to work. Speech teams operating multilingual deployments get more consistent quality across markets, which reduces the gap between primary and secondary languages. HDv2.5 is rolling out in public preview across existing Neural HD regions; rollout completes alongside the broader Speech monthly update cycle. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Serverless indexers in Azure AI Search
items.description:
Azure AI Search now offers a serverless option for native indexers in public preview, removing the requirement to provision and manage indexer compute for ingestion workflows. Indexer execution scales with workload demand, so customers stop paying for idle capacity during off-peak hours and stop over-provisioning to handle bursts. The MVP supports document ingestion and enrichment patterns commonly used in RAG pipelines, Foundry Knowledge Bases, and AI-driven applications backed by Azure AI Search. Existing native indexer definitions continue to work; customers opt into serverless execution on a per-indexer basis and keep their current data sources, skillsets, and target indexes. The release is aimed at enterprise developers and platform engineers running large or bursty ingestion jobs who want lower operational overhead and usage-aligned cost.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: MAI-Image-2.5 in Microsoft Foundry model catalog
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry adds MAI-Image-2.5 to the model catalog in public preview, the next generation of Microsoft's in-house image generation model. The release improves photorealism, prompt fidelity, and generation speed compared with MAI-Image-2, and is tuned for marketing creative, product visualization, and content production workloads rather than open-ended consumer art. Enterprise customers get Foundry-native deployment with the same governance, regional availability, and content safety controls already used for other MAI models, plus consumption-based pricing per image. The model is available through Global Standard deployments and composes with other Foundry capabilities, so teams can chain image generation with grounding, retrieval, and agents inside a single workflow. 

Learn more

items.title: Public Preview: MAI-Transcribe-1.5 in Microsoft Foundry model catalog
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry adds MAI-Transcribe-1.5 to the model catalog in public preview, Microsoft's next-generation speech-to-text model. The release adds improved accuracy with noticeably lower word error rate on long-tail locales than the previous generation, plus faster real-time and batch transcription with predictable latency. Target workloads include call center analytics, media captioning, voice agent transcription, and meeting recording. MAI-Transcribe-1.5 is available via Global Standard deployments with Foundry-native governance, regional support, and content safety controls shared across MAI models. It is available through Azure Speech. 

Learn more

items.title: Public Preview: Purview sensitivity labels in Azure AI Search knowledge sources
items.description:
Azure AI Search adds Microsoft Purview sensitivity label support to knowledge sources in public preview. Labels applied at the source system flow through ingestion into Azure AI Search and into the knowledge bases that ground Foundry agents and copilots, so chunk retrieval, vector search, and multi-step agent reasoning all respect the same access and privacy classifications defined by enterprise security teams. Customers building secure agentic workflows over regulated data get end-to-end label fidelity instead of having to rebuild access enforcement at the retrieval layer. The capability is a prerequisite for downstream Purview-aware agent orchestration scenarios. Existing knowledge sources continue to work; sensitivity awareness turns on per source. The release covers indexed Purview-labeled content surfaced through the Knowledge Source API. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Hosted Agents in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service reaches preview for Hosted Agents, the container-based runtime that lets developers bring their own agent code in any framework and deploy it to Microsoft-managed infrastructure. Each Hosted Agent runs in a per-session VM-isolated sandbox with persistent filesystem state, automatic scale to zero, and a dedicated Microsoft Entra agent identity wired up at deploy time. The release supports the Responses, Invocations, Activity, and A2A protocols in a single agent, OpenTelemetry tracing, and bring-your-own virtual network for outbound traffic. Customers running Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, or custom orchestration code get a managed host with SLA-backed support instead of operating containerization, scaling, and identity plumbing themselves. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Purview admin access auditing for sensitivity-labeled content in Azure AI Search
items.description:
Azure AI Search adds Microsoft Purview admin access auditing for sensitivity-labeled content in public preview. Admin operations that touch Purview-labeled documents inside Azure AI Search, knowledge retrieval, and Foundry IQ knowledge bases now flow into Microsoft Purview's unified audit log alongside Microsoft 365 events. Security and compliance teams running AI Search in regulated industries get end-to-end visibility for the same admin actions they already track in SharePoint, Exchange, and OneDrive, instead of having a blind spot on the search and agentic retrieval surface. The capability covers index management, source configuration, and access changes on labeled content, and respects existing Purview retention and access controls. Existing AI Search resources gain auditing without code changes. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Foundry Memory preview refresh
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry refreshes the Foundry Memory public preview with a redesigned storage model, new retrieval controls, and tighter integration with the Foundry Agent Service tool surface. Agents using Memory can now write, search, and update user-scoped and session-scoped memories through a single tool, with built-in semantic deduplication and TTL controls that keep memory stores from drifting over time.
