The refresh adds region availability, content safety filtering on memory writes, and improved observability so memory reads and writes appear as first-class spans in Foundry tracing. Customers running pilots on the previous Memory preview continue to work; the refresh ships as an opt-in upgrade in the Foundry portal and through the agent tool catalog. The release targets agents that need stable user context across multi-turn and multi-session interactions. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server pg_ivm extension
items.description:
Now customers can install the pg_ivm extension in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database PostgreSQL - Flexible Server cross-tenant customer-managed keys
items.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server now supports cross-tenant customer-managed keys (CMK), in public preview, allowing you to encrypt your data at rest using an Azure Key Vault key that resides in a separate Microsoft Entra tenant from the database service. 


This capability is designed for software as a service (SaaS) providers and enterprises that need to maintain strict separation of duties and ownership of encryption keys, enabling their customers to retain full control over key lifecycle management while PostgreSQL runs in a service provider's tenant. 


With cross-tenant CMK: Your PostgreSQL data is encrypted using a key you own and manage. The database service never has access to your key material. You can rotate or revoke keys at any time without downtime. 


Authentication between PostgreSQL Flexible Server and the customer-owned key vault is handled using federated identity with Microsoft Entra ID access across tenants. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Defender security assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
You can now use Microsoft Defender security assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL to continuously evaluate your database security posture and identify potential vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. This feature helps you strengthen your security baseline, prioritize remediation based on risk, and align with best practices and compliance requirements. You can proactively protect your PostgreSQL workloads with integrated insights directly in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Pre-upgrade validation checks for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
You can now proactively validate Major Version Upgrade (MVU) readiness for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server before initiating the actual upgrade process. New pre-upgrade validation checks allow you to independently run upgrade compatibility validations and identify potential blockers ahead of time, helping reduce failed upgrade attempts and improve operational predictability. 


The validation process checks your server against Azure PostgreSQL upgrade policies and PostgreSQL pg_upgrade -check compatibility requirements. It surfaces actionable guidance for issues such as unsupported extensions, replication slots, prepared transactions, configuration mismatches, and other upgrade constraints. You can resolve identified issues, rerun validations as needed, and proceed with the upgrade only when your environment is ready. 


By shifting validation from inline execution during upgrade to a proactive pre-flight step, this capability helps improve first-time upgrade success rates, reduce troubleshooting effort, and simplify upgrade planning for production workloads.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Oracle schema conversion to Azure PostgreSQL in Visual Studio Code
items.description:
You can now convert Oracle database schema objects to Azure Database for PostgreSQL-compatible schema directly in the PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code. The experience provides a project-based workflow for Oracle to Microsoft for PostgreSQL offerings, using Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server as a scratch database for validation and testing during schema conversion. The workflow automatically flags items that can't be converted as Review Tasks, so you can address them before applying the generated artifacts. 


With this release, you can move schema conversion into a guided Visual Studio Code experience instead of managing the process across separate tools. You can load Oracle schemas, run conversion, validate converted objects, review flagged items, and then apply the generated PostgreSQL artifacts with more visibility into what was converted and what still needs attention. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: LLM Speech API in Azure AI Speech
items.description:
Azure AI Speech makes the LLM Speech API generally available, delivering state-of-the-art LLM-powered transcription and translation for audio files, with multi-lingual support across 25 languages (90+ locales), improved accuracy, expanded regions, and enhanced prompt-tuning capabilities. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Managed virtual network for evaluations in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry makes managed virtual network support generally available for evaluations, so customers can run cloud evaluation jobs against models and agents that sit behind private endpoints. The Foundry-managed VNET handles outbound connectivity to the model deployment, the evaluation dataset storage account, and any tool endpoints under test, with no need to maintain bastion hosts or self-hosted runners. Security teams keep network isolation, private DNS, and outbound traffic rules consistent with the rest of their Azure footprint, and audit traces flow through the same Defender and Purview pipelines as production agent traffic. Engineering teams can wire evaluation jobs into CI/CD without opening public network access on protected model endpoints. The capability is on by default for new evaluation runs in supported regions.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: OneLake catalog integration for Azure AI Search knowledge sources
items.description:
Azure AI Search makes OneLake catalog integration generally available for knowledge sources, so customers can register a OneLake item once and reuse it across multiple knowledge sources and agents. The integration honors existing OneLake item-level permissions, sensitivity labels, and lineage, so when a Fabric admin restricts access in OneLake the change flows through to every dependent agent on the next query. Developers pick a catalog entry instead of pasting a path, and the knowledge source picks up schema metadata, freshness signals, and item ownership without extra configuration. Teams already organizing data in OneLake can extend that catalog to Foundry agents and search workloads with no duplicate registration. The integration is available in all regions where Azure AI Search and OneLake operate together. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Image translation inside Office documents for batch document translation
items.description:
Azure AI Translator batch document translation now translates text inside images embedded in Word `.docx` files as a generally available capability. The service detects image regions, runs OCR, translates the recognized text, and re-renders it back into the document while preserving the original layout, font, and surrounding formatting. Image-aware translation works through the existing batch translation REST API and SDK paths, with the same source and target Azure Blob Storage container pattern. Pricing is calculated per image translated, alongside standard character-based pricing for the surrounding document text. Output documents are written to the target container in their translated form for downstream review.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Image file translation for batch document translation in Azure AI Translator
items.description:
Azure AI Translator batch document translation accepts image files as a generally available input type. Supported formats include `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.bmp`, and `.webp`. The service runs OCR on each image, translates the recognized text into the target language, and writes a translated image back to your Azure Blob Storage target container while keeping the original visual design and layout. Image inputs ride the same async batch REST API, SDK, and managed identity authentication path as Word, PowerPoint, PDF, and other supported formats. Pricing is calculated on a per-image basis. Status and per-document tracking continue through the existing batch translation status APIs.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Improved PDF batch document translation in Azure AI Translator
items.description:
Azure AI Translator batch document translation ships generally available improvements for PDF translation. The service uses Azure AI Document Intelligence to recover structure from both digital-native and scanned PDFs, then translates the recognized text and re-renders the document with the original reading order, tables, headings, and image placement preserved. The improved pipeline reduces formatting drift in long, multi-column reports and forms, and continues to flow through the standard batch translation REST API with source and target Azure Blob Storage containers. Authentication options stay the same, including shared access signature tokens and managed identity. Pricing follows the existing character-based document translation rates. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Databricks Lakebase branching with GitHub Copilot agent mode
items.description:
Developers in Azure Databricks can now create a copy-on-write branch of their Lakebase production database with a single command, connect GitHub Copilot agent mode to the branch endpoint, and debug AI apps and agents against real production data without ever touching production. The workflow is fully Azure-native across GitHub, and Azure Databricks with enterprise compliance workflows included. This reduces AI agent debug cycles from hours to minutes while keeping production data completely safe.

Learn more,

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Databricks workspace-wide Genie MCP for Microsoft Copilot Studio
items.description:
A new workspace-wide Genie MCP endpoint enables any Microsoft Copilot Studio agent to query natural-language questions across an entire Azure Databricks workspace through a single endpoint. The endpoint auto-routes across all connected Genie spaces and Unity Catalog data, replacing the previous per-space configuration requirement and reducing integration overhead significantly. Business users get governed, workspace-wide data access directly inside Microsoft Teams and M365 Copilot.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Snapshot backup for SQL Server in Azure VMs
items.description:
Azure Backup now supports snapshot-based backup for SQL Server running on Azure Virtual Machines. This new capability uses Azure disk snapshots combined with native SQL transaction log backups to deliver near-instant, low-impact full backups for large SQL databases, significantly improving backup performance and reducing the load on production workloads compared to streaming backups. You can protect multiple databases under a SQL instance with a single policy and restore using different mechanisms with point-in-time recovery enabled by log chaining on top of snapshot recovery points.
All restore points get stored in Azure Recovery Services Vault which provides long term retention and added security for your data in case of Ransomware attacks and any other disasters.

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Azure VMware Solution AV36 node End of Support on September 30, 2027
items.description:
Reminder: Microsoft’s support lifecycle is evolving in alignment with VMware’s roadmap. Broadcom will end support for the current AV36 VCF version on September 30, 2027, and the AV36 SKU is not compatible with VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) 9, the next-generation platform.

As part of this transition, all AV36 SDDCs will be retired after September 30, 2027, regardless of individual RI expiration dates. On October 1, 2027, these SDDCs will no longer be accessible. Microsoft will securely retain customer data for a limited period (up to 60 days) to support retrieval if needed.

The details above only impact AV36 nodes. AVS AV36P, AV48, AV52 and AV64 remain available.

Key dates for existing AV36 subscriptions

June 30, 2026 Last day to buy a 1-year RI for AV36 VCF BYOL

September 30, 2027 Broadcom end of support for VCF 5.x, AV36 is not compatible with VCF 9

October 1, 2027 SDDC access will be removed. Microsoft will retain the data for up to 60 days so the customer can retrieve it.

Reach out to your Microsoft Account Team for key dates for AV36 PayGo subscriptions.

Recommended action:

At this time, we recommend that you review your current AV36 SDDCs and then work with your Microsoft Account Team. Identify available AVS node types on the Azure Product by Region page and visit the AVS Documentation page to learn about HCX migrations between AVS node types.

Help and support: 

If you have questions, please reach out to your Microsoft Account Team.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Functions Support for Node.js 24
items.description:
Azure Functions support for Node.js 24 is now generally available.   

You can now develop apps using Node.js 24 locally and deploy them to supported Azure Functions plans on Linux and Windows, including the Flex Consumption plan.     

Please note that Remote Build on Flex Consumption for Node.js 24 is rolling out and will be available in all public regions in the coming week.  

Learn more:  

  • Updating your app to Node.js 24  
  • Azure Functions Node.js versions end of support dates

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Site Recovery Support for Performance Plus Managed Disks
items.description:
Azure Site Recovery (ASR) now supports replication of virtual machines using Performance Plus enabled managed disks. With this update, virtual machines using Premium SSD, Standard SSD or Standard HDD managed disks with Performance Plus capability for higher IOPS and throughput for their workloads can be protected with ASR for disaster recovery in the Azure-to-Azure scenario. This support further ensures performance consistency between primary and secondary regions during replication, test failover and full failover for such disks. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Application Gateway for Containers – Service Mesh integration with Istio
items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers service mesh integration with Istio is now generally available. This capability simplifies secure north-south traffic into workloads running in an Istio service mesh by automating mutual TLS (mTLS) connectivity between Application Gateway for Containers and mesh-enabled services.  

With general availability, customers can use this integration with both upstream open-source Istio and the Istio-based service mesh add-on for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). This gives teams flexibility to adopt a managed AKS experience while using Application Gateway for Containers as their ingress path for services inside and outside the mesh.  

  • Single ingress solution: Route traffic to services both inside and outside the mesh through one gateway.  
  • Reduced operational overhead: Simplify ingress configuration and avoid repetitive mTLS definitions.  
  • Managed certificate lifecycle: Automate certificate trust and rotation for secure communication with mesh workloads.  
  • Flexible deployment options: Support both upstream Istio and the AKS Istio-based service mesh add-on.  

Learn more:  

  • Application Gateway for Containers + Istio service mesh  
  • Application Gateway for Containers overview  
  • Original public preview announcement

items.title: Generally Available: Multiparty private offers in Microsoft Marketplace expand to 30 countries in Europe
items.description:
Multiparty private offers give Microsoft partners a way to procure third-party cloud and AI solutions for customers through Marketplace. Software companies can expand into new markets by working with partners that bring established customer relationships, while customers rely on their trusted partners to manage their cloud and AI initiatives. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Virtual Network Manager integration with Virtual WAN
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network Manager integration with Virtual WAN is now in public preview, enabling you to use an Azure Virtual WAN hub as the hub in Azure Virtual Network Manager hub-and-spoke connectivity configurations, bringing together Azure Virtual Network Manager 's at-scale network management with Virtual WAN's managed routing, security, and hybrid connectivity.

With this capability, you can automatically connect hundreds of spoke virtual networks to a Virtual WAN hub using Azure Virtual Network Manager network groups and connectivity configurations, eliminating the need to manually create and manage individual Virtual WAN virtual network connections. You can apply consistent routing configuration through Virtual WAN connection policies, leverage dynamic group membership to onboard new spokes automatically as they appear in your environment, and optionally enable direct connectivity mesh between spokes for low-latency east-west traffic, while preserving your existing Virtual WAN routing intent, firewall integration, and on-premises connectivity.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Virtual network flow logs connector with Microsoft Sentinel
items.description:
Azure virtual network flow logs connector with Microsoft Sentinel is now generally available, enabling you to seamlessly export and analyze network traffic data within your security operations workflows. 

With this integration, you can bring rich, network-level visibility from virtual network flow logs directly into Microsoft Sentinel, empowering security teams to detect threats, investigate incidents, and correlate network activity with broader security signals across your environment. 

By combining detailed traffic insights with advanced analytics and threat detection capabilities from Microsoft Sentinel, you can strengthen your security posture, accelerate incident response, and gain a unified view of network and security data. 

Through a native Microsoft Sentinel connector for virtual network flow logs, you can now operationalize this data with out-of-the-box alerts on your log analytics workspaces, leveraging enriched flow log data for your SecOps workflows 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Entra-only identities with Azure Files
items.description:
Azure Files announces general availability of Entra-only identities for SMB access, enabling organizations to securely access file shares using cloud-native identities without requiring Active Directory or hybrid identity infrastructure. With Microsoft Entra ID as the authentication authority, users can access Azure Files using Kerberos-based authentication backed entirely by cloud identities - eliminating dependency on domain controllers and simplifying storage and identity architecture.  

Key capabilities 

  • Cloud-native authentication with Entra ID: Secure SMB access using Kerberos without Active Directory or domain controllers 
  • Simplified permissions management: Configure granular NTFS ACLs for Entra users and groups directly through the Azure portal 
  • Role-based access control (RBAC): Assign share-level access using built-in roles for least-privilege administration 
  • Secure access from anywhere: Enable identity-based access over the internet without VPN dependencies 
  • Support for modern workloads: Power Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), general-purpose file sharing, and distributed collaboration scenarios 

Please reach out to azurefiles@microsoft.com if you have any questions about adopting Entra-only Identities for secure SMB access with Azure Files. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement:  TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 in Azure App Service, Azure Functions, and Azure Logic Apps
items.description:
As part of Azure’s ongoing security improvements, App Service, Functions, and Logic Apps will no longer accept connections using TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 after May 31, 2027. Any client, application, or service that continues to use these legacy TLS versions will be unable to connect to these services after his date. 

Customers should review the applications and services that connect to App Service, Functions, or Logic Apps and ensure they support TLS 1.2 or later prior to this date. 

View the resources in your subscription that still allow TLS 1.0 or 1.1 in the Azure Retirement Workbook.

Next steps 

Test client compatibility with TLS 1.2 or later. Review the TLS version deprecation overview for configuration guidance and see the service‑specific Q&A links below for common questions. 

Learn more:

  • App Service TLS deprecation Q&A  
  • Functions TLS deprecation Q&A  
  • Logic Apps TLS deprecation Q&A

items.title: Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files object REST API
items.description:
The Object REST API (an S3-compatible REST API) on Azure NetApp Files bridges the gap between traditional file-based storage and modern cloud services, enabling you to use your existing data in new ways. With the Object REST API, you can seamlessly integrate Azure NetApp Files data with Microsoft Fabric, Azure AI services, and other Azure offerings without the need to move or replicate data. This unlocks new use cases such as advanced analytics, machine learning, and real-time business intelligence, while reducing costs and accelerating innovation. 

The Object REST API introduces native S3-compatible read/write access, allowing modern applications to interact with your data directly and efficiently. Enterprises benefit from simplified integration, enhanced productivity, and improved data security, as data remains in place and protected by Azure NetApp Files’ robust security measures. This feature is ideal for organizations looking to leverage AI-driven insights, streamline workflows, and maintain compliance with industry standards.  

This feature is now generally available in all Azure NetApp Files regions. 

Learn more:  

  • What's new in Azure NetApp Files  
  • Understand Azure NetApp Files object REST API access  
  • Configure object REST API access in Azure NetApp Files  
  • Connect OneLake to an Azure NetApp Files volume using object REST API  
  • Connect Azure Databricks to an Azure NetApp Files object REST API-enabled volume

items.title: Public Preview: TLS/SSL certificate support for Azure Functions Flex Consumption
items.description:
Flex Consumption introduces a site-scoped certificate model in public preview in all the regions where Flex Consumption is available. Unlike webspace-scoped certificates on other hosting plans which are shared across apps in the same region + resource group, Flex certificates are scoped to an individual function app. 

Each function app can hold up to 3 private (.pfx) and 3 public (.cer) certificates uploaded directly, imported from Azure Key Vault, or issued as free App Service Managed Certificates to enable custom domains, client-certificate authentication, and mutual TLS scenarios on Flex Consumption. 

To access certificates from code Flex Consumption uses a per-certificate "Accessible to app code" toggle in the portal instead of the WEBSITE_LOAD_CERTIFICATES app setting used on other plans. Because Flex Consumption runs on Linux, code reads certificates from file paths (/var/ssl/certs for public, /var/ssl/private for private) rather than from a Windows certificate store.  

Currently, the Azure portal is the recommended path for configuring certificates during preview. Apps migrating from another plan should add their certificates to the new Flex Consumption app rather than carrying webspace-scoped certificates across.  

Learn more: 

  • Configure site-scoped certificates  
  • Infrastructure as code instructions  
  • Cross-plan certificate comparison

items.title: Generally Available: User Groups and IP address pools for P2S connections
items.description:
User Groups and IP Address Pools for Point-to-Site connections in VPN Gateway enable customers to assign distinct IP address pools to remote users based on their credentials. 

With this capability, customers can organize remote users into separate groups and assign a unique IP address range to each group, enabling more granular access control for Azure workloads. User groups within a VPN Gateway can be defined based on Microsoft Entra ID group membership, certificate common name domains, or custom RADIUS attributes. 

This feature helps customers strengthen security, enabling finer-grained access segmentation and policy enforcement for Azure workloads. 

Learn more.

items.title: Update: Microsoft Entra ID token refresh support for Python, .NET, and JavaScript in Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
You can now take advantage of Microsoft Entra ID token refresh support in Python, .NET, and JavaScript client libraries to simplify authentication in your applications backed by Azure Database for PostgreSQL. With this release, your applications can automatically refresh access tokens, helping you avoid authentication interruptions caused by token expiration. This update makes it easier for you to build resilient, long‑running services and background workloads without adding custom token‑management logic.   

Learn more: 

  • Token refresh with Python 
  • Token refresh with .NET  
  • Token refresh with JavaScript

products: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
items.title: Generally Available: SQL Server on Azure VMs in Malaysia West, Indonesia Central
items.description:
SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines is now generally available in the Malaysia West and Indonesia Central Azure regions. With this regional expansion, you can deploy and manage SQL Server workloads closer to your users while helping meet data residency requirements in Malaysia and Indonesia.

Note: SQL Server unified management is not included in this regional enablement. You can learn more in the SQL Server Unified Management documentation.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: langchain-azure-cosmosdb python package for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can now build production-ready AI and agent applications faster using the new LangChain and LangGraph integration for Azure Cosmos DB. This Python package enables you to directly use Cosmos DB for vector and hybrid search, semantic caching, chat history storage, checkpointing, and long-term memory, all within familiar LangChain and LangGraph workflows.

You can store and retrieve embeddings, combine full-text and vector search for more relevant results, cache LLM responses to reduce cost and latency, persist conversational history, and manage agent state with checkpointing for reliable execution. You no longer need to stitch together multiple services or databases for retrieval, memory, and orchestration. With Cosmos DB’s global distribution, scalability, and enterprise-grade reliability, you can build copilots, multi-agent systems, and knowledge assistants that operate efficiently at scale while keeping your operational and agentic data all in one place.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Schedule one-time or recurring migrations with Azure Storage Mover
items.description:
Azure Storage Mover now supports built-in job scheduling, giving customers more control over when migrations run and making it easier to automate repeatable data transfers into Azure. Customers can configure jobs to start automatically at a specific date and time, or set up recurring runs to keep their target storage in sync with data from on-premises environments.

In the portal, customers can choose No schedule, a one-time schedule, or a recurring schedule. Recurring schedules support daily, weekly, and monthly frequency options. Schedules can also be enabled or disabled as needed, giving teams flexibility to align migrations with maintenance windows, business operations, or phased cutover plans. 

Scheduling is designed to help teams reduce manual intervention while improving operational consistency for ongoing migrations and sync scenarios. This capability is positioned for scenarios such as off-hours movement, staged cutovers, and incremental syncs before final migration completion.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Storage Mover Blob-to-Blob migration
items.description:
Azure Storage Mover now supports Blob container-to-Blob container data transfers, enabling customers to move data seamlessly across regions, subscriptions, and accounts with a fully managed experience.  

Customers can now use Azure Storage Mover to migrate data directly between Azure Blob containers with: 

  • Agentless, fully managed transfers—no infrastructure deployment required 
  • Support for large-scale parallel data movement, optimized for high throughput migrations 
  • Integrated job management, including progress tracking, resumability, and reliability controls across migrations. 
  • Support for both flat namespace (FNS) and hierarchical namespace (HNS) accounts  

Azure Storage Mover is optimized for high-throughput data transfer scenarios: 

  • Proven performance with multi-GB/s transfer speeds depending on workload characteristics and region topology  
  • Ability to handle large object counts and deep directory structures, enabling enterprise-grade migrations at scale  
  • Support for parallel job execution to maximize throughput across multiple workloads  

Getting started: 

Blob-to-Blob migrations can be configured directly in the Azure portal with just a few steps, allowing customers to quickly initiate transfers without deploying or managing infrastructure.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: site-to-site VPN connections with certificate authentication
items.description:
Azure Site-to-Site VPN with digital certificate authentication provides an alternative to the traditional pre-shared key (PSK) model by using a certificate-based asymmetric trust model. In this configuration, Azure and the on-premises VPN device authenticate each other by using separate inbound and outbound certificates. The outbound authentication certificate is stored in Azure Key Vault and is accessed by the VPN Gateway through a user-assigned managed identity with the required Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) permissions. Because X.509 certificates use asymmetric keys and a trusted certificate chain to validate identity, this approach helps reduce the risk of impersonation and Internet Key Exchange (IKE) negotiation tampering. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Summarized advertised gateway prefixes for route advertisement
items.description:
Summarized advertised gateway prefixes for route advertisement is now in public preview, enabling you to define summarized prefixes that Azure gateways, including ExpressRoute and VPN Gateway, advertise to on-premises networks, instead of advertising all individual virtual network address spaces.

With this capability, you can reduce the number of prefixes advertised to on-premises in large hub-and-spoke topologies, staying within ExpressRoute and VPN Gateway advertised-prefix quota. Instead of advertising hundreds of individual spoke prefixes, you can advertise covering prefixes (for example, 10.0.0.0/16), enabling larger-scale Azure environments without redesigning address plans or splitting virtual networks. Spoke address spaces not covered by the summarized prefix continue to be advertised individually, ensuring backward compatibility.

It supports both IPv4 and IPv6 configurations and works across ExpressRoute Gateway and VPN Gateway.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Event Grid releases for April 2026
items.description:
Azure Event Grid namespaces are expanding MQTT capabilities to help organizations build more connected, scalable, and MQTT V5 standards-based real-time solutions. These updates make it easier to deliver responsive device experiences, simplify backend integration, and accelerate modern IoT application development. 
  • MQTT Retain support: Deliver a better subscriber experience by ensuring new subscribers can immediately receive the latest known state for a topic, without waiting for the next message. 
  • Shared Subscriptions: Scale message processing more efficiently by distributing traffic across multiple consumers in the same subscription group, helping support higher throughput and more resilient architectures. 
  • HTTP Publish of MQTT messages: Bring HTTP-based applications into MQTT workflows with a simple publishing path that helps connect backend services, business applications, and device ecosystems more seamlessly.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Event Grid Subscription Identifiers
items.description:
Gain more flexibility in message handling with Subscription Identifiers by enabling subscribers to identify which subscription triggered delivery, helping streamline client-side processing in more advanced MQTT scenarios.  

Together, these enhancements strengthen Azure Event Grid namespaces as a powerful foundation for modern MQTT messaging—making it easier to connect devices, applications, and cloud services with greater scale, flexibility, and operational simplicity. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Evaluate feature rollouts with Azure App Configuration Scorecards
items.description:
Azure App Configuration now supports a scorecards capability in public preview. Scorecards provide a telemetry-driven view of how feature flag variants are performing in production, helping teams identify measurable changes after a rollout without manually comparing telemetry across dashboards.

Built on Azure App Configuration Feature Management and Application Insights telemetry, scorecards help teams use production signals to evaluate rollout impact and guide next steps. Learn how scorecards can help evaluate feature rollouts.

With scorecards, teams can:

  • Compare feature variants against key performance indicators
  • Detect potential issues introduced by new or updated feature behavior
  • Evaluate adoption and usage of features
  • Use telemetry insights to support rollout, optimization, and deprecation decisions
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files cache volumes
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files cache volumes is now Generally Available. Azure NetApp Files now support cache volumes, which are cloud-based caches of an external origin volume, containing only the most actively accessed data on the volume. This brings data and files closer to the user for faster throughput with a smaller footprint. Azure NetApp Files cache volumes simplify file distribution, reduces WAN latency, and lowers WAN/ExpressRoute bandwidth costs. 

Cache volumes is available in these regions.

Learn more: 

  • What's new in Azure NetApp Files 
  • Configure a cache volume for Azure NetApp Files 
  • Understand Azure NetApp Files cache volumes 
  • Change the service level of an Azure NetApp Files cache volume 
  • Manage file access logs in Azure NetApp Files cache volume 
  • Break file locks for an Azure NetApp Files cache volume 
  • Reset SMB password for an Azure NetApp Files cache volume

items.title: Generally Available: Network Watcher rule impact analyser
items.description:
Azure Network Watcher rule impact analyzer is now generally available, enabling you to assess the potential impact of your network security group (NSG) or security admin rule changes on live network traffic before applying them. 

With this capability, you can evaluate how proposed NSG or network manager rule modifications would affect your existing traffic patterns, helping you fine-tune configurations, avoid unintended disruptions, and deploy changes with confidence. 

This feature is accessible through the Azure portal and leverages Azure Network Watcher traffic analytics and virtual network flow logs to deliver data-driven visibility into how NSG or network manager rule updates could influence your current network behavior. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network updates – default limits increased for NSGs and route tables
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network has increased the default platform limits for network security groups (NSGs) and route tables. The new defaults are now 2,000 security rules per NSG, 6,000 addresses or ports per NSG rule, 1,000 routes per route table, and 600 route tables per subscription. 

This update enables customers to: 

  • Scale security policies with confidence: Enterprises managing hundreds of application tiers and subnets can define more granular NSG rules without hitting default ceilings or opening support cases. 

  • Support larger routing topologies out of the box: Customers with complex hub-and-spoke architectures can configure more routes per route table and deploy more route tables per subscription. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Mock runs for Azure Storage Actions – Validate before you execute
items.description:
Azure Storage Actions, our fully managed platform that transforms how organizations automate data management tasks for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage, now supports mock runs - a new way to simulate task execution at full scale without modifying any data. 

Mock runs enable you to validate your task conditions by scanning and evaluating billions of objects against your storage accounts, generating a detailed report showing exactly which blobs would be affected and what operations would be performed without making any changes. Mock runs validate across every blob in scope, giving you complete confidence before committing to irreversible blob operations. Combining full-scale validation with detailed CSV reporting, mock runs eliminate guesswork and drive safe, predictable automation. 

Supported use cases include validating retention and expiry policies, previewing cost optimization through down tiering or up tiering, confirming compliance enforcement such as legal holds and immutability, and verifying large-scale cleanup or tagging operations before execution. You can create a mock run by selecting it as the trigger type when creating a storage task assignment, review the results, and then seamlessly transition the assignment to a real run without recreating it.  

Learn more: 

  • Mock runs documentation 
  • Azure Storage Actions overview

items.title: Generally Available: Auto activation for SaaS subscriptions in Microsoft Marketplace
items.description:
Auto activation for SaaS solutions is now available in Microsoft Marketplace, making it faster and easier to get the value from your SaaS products. When auto activation is enabled, your subscription—and billing cycle—begins the moment you complete your purchase, removing the need for post-purchase activation steps.  

Because auto activation is a partner‑controlled setting, availability may vary by offer. You can confirm this with the partner in advance or see the auto activation status in the public or private offer purchase flow.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Application Insights Auto-instrumentation for Azure Kubernetes Service apps
items.description:
Azure Monitor Application Insights auto-instrumentation for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) apps is now generally available, making it easier to monitor your applications without modifying source code. With just a few configuration steps, you can automatically instrument Java and Node.js workloads running on AKS and start collecting telemetry with Application Insights.

This capability helps teams quickly unlock Application Insights experiences such as application maps, end-to-end transaction diagnostics, distributed tracing, and log analysis without the time and effort of manual code changes. By using auto-instrumentation with the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro, you can accelerate troubleshooting, improve visibility into application health, and simplify observability for cloud-native workloads on AKS.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Front Door WebSocket
items.description:
Azure Front Door Standard and Premium now support WebSocket in general availability. WebSocket is enabled by default and requires no additional configuration. 

WebSocket provides full-duplex communication over a single, long-lived TCP connection, enabling efficient, low-latency data exchange without the need for polling. This reduces overhead and improves resource utilization for real-time applications. 

With native WebSocket support, Azure Front Door can power interactive and real-time scenarios such as chat applications, live dashboards, financial data streaming, gaming, and other continuous data workloads.  

Learn more.

items.title: Update: Microsoft Foundry built-in RBAC role naming and enhancements
items.description:
Role names in Microsoft Foundry have been updated to align with the product brand. The following built-in roles are now renamed:

  • Azure AI Account Owner → Foundry Account Owner
  • Azure AI Owner → Foundry Owner
  • Azure AI User → Foundry User
  • Azure AI Project Manager → Foundry Project Manager

In addition, role management capabilities have been enhanced to support evolving Foundry scenarios. Foundry Account Owner and Foundry Owner roles now include the ability to assign select dependent roles needed for common workflows, such as deploying hosted agents and accessing trace data. These roles can assign the following roles to themselves and others (conditional access):

  • Foundry User
  • Container Registry Contributor and Data Access Configuration Administrator
  • Container Registry Repository Writer
  • Log Analytics Reader

Permissions for Foundry User and Foundry Project Manager remain unchanged.

Learn More.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Blob Storage SDK for Rust
items.description:
The Azure Blob Storage SDK for Rust is now generally available. The Rust SDK allows you to connect to an Azure Blob Storage account and perform operations on containers and blobs, including uploading, downloading, listing, and managing blobs. This release brings production-grade capabilities for secure, reliable access to Blob Storage from Rust, such as Microsoft Entra ID authentication, automatic retries on transient failures, and distributed tracing through OpenTelemetry. You now have stable APIs backed by semver guarantees, a pluggable async runtime, and the same familiar design patterns used across the Azure SDKs for .NET, Java, Python, JavaScript, Go, and C++. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Support for workloads with large files in Azure NetApp Files
items.description:
To support seamless migration and operation of workloads that use large files including Azure VMware Solution (AVS) virtual machines with large VMDK disks, Azure NetApp Files now supports file sizes of up to 64 TiB for regular volumes. This enhancement enables the migration of on‑premises workloads with large virtual machine disks to Azure VMware Solution and supports ongoing operation of data‑intensive workloads in Azure. The capability is available in all Azure NetApp Files enabled regions across the Flexible, Standard, Premium, and Ultra service levels.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Managed Identity Support for Azure Files SMB Is now GA
items.description:
Azure Files now supports Managed Identities for SMB access, enabling applications and services to authenticate without storing static credentials or account keys. This feature aligns with Zero Trust principles, allowing workloads to use Entra-issued tokens for secure, short-lived access to file shares.  

By leveraging Managed Identities, organizations can eliminate service principal secrets and reduce credential sprawl, simplifying compliance and improving security posture.
This capability is especially impactful for cloud-native workloads that require persistent storage, including:  

  • AKS clusters with persistent volumes with managed and workload identities  
  • CI/CD pipelines and automation scripts  
  • Native Application or VM (device) identity access  

Managed Identities provide seamless integration with Azure RBAC, enabling fine-grained access control and centralized policy enforcement without manual key rotation. Please reach out to azurefiles@microsoft.com or customers interested in adopting Managed Identities for secure SMB access with Azure Files. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Container Apps Express
items.description:
Azure Container Apps Express is now available in public preview. It is the simplest and fastest way to launch and scale powerful applications on Azure, from zero to hyperscale, without infrastructure decisions. It represents the first Azure compute platform purpose-built for agent and developer use alike. 

Express is based on years of experience running Azure Container Apps at a large scale. We have learned that most developers working on web apps, APIs and agents want to deploy quickly, have automatic scaling, and avoid dealing with complex infrastructure. Express provides these features. It sets up your environment in seconds, can handle any amount of traffic, and removes complicated settings. This helps teams move from writing code to having a production-ready app in just minutes, not hours. 

Express is purpose-built for workloads serving developers and agents alike. It provides opinionated, production-grade defaults: autoscaling, per-second billing, managed identity, secrets management, custom domains, container registry integration, revision management, and built-in observability. Just bring your container, Azure Container Apps Express handles everything else. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor dashboards with Grafana in Public, Government (Fairfax) and China
items.description:
Azure Monitor dashboards with Grafana are generally available, bringing the power of Grafana’s open and composable visualization platform directly into the Azure Portal. This capability enables developers and operators to create, edit, and share Grafana dashboards without needing to deploy or manage additional infrastructure. Users can seamlessly visualize Azure Monitor metrics, logs and traces, alongside Prometheus, Azure Resource Graph and Azure Data Explorer data using familiar Grafana experiences with Azure-native security and governance through RBAC and ARM-based deployment.

With general availability, Azure Monitor dashboards with Grafana introduces new capabilities including expanded Azure service integrations (such as AKS, Application Insights and PostgreSQL), additional prebuilt dashboards, and support for advanced workflows like Grafana Explore and enhanced Kubernetes monitoring. Just as importantly, this release is now broadly available across Azure clouds, including Azure Public, US Government (Fairfax), and China, ensuring consistent observability experiences for customers operating in sovereign and regulated environments.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Confidential computing for Azure Service Bus Premium
items.description:
Confidential computing for Azure Service Bus Premium is now generally available in Korea Central and UAE North. This capability enables Service Bus to process messages inside hardware-based trusted execution environments (TEEs), adding protection for data in use on top of existing encryption at rest and in transit. The TEE prevents unauthorized access to data while it is being processed, bringing hardware-level isolation to message handling. 

Confidential computing works alongside the security features you can already use with Service Bus today, such as TLS encryption for data in transit, encryption at rest with support for customer-managed keys (CMK), private endpoints, and managed identities. For workloads with the strictest requirements, pairing confidential computing with customer-managed keys backed by Azure Key Vault Managed HSM provides defense in depth across data at rest, in transit, and in use. 

Confidential computing is enabled at the namespace level during creation. After it is enabled, all queues, topics, and subscriptions in the namespace benefit from hardware-isolated message processing. No application changes are required, so existing clients and messaging patterns continue to work. 

Learn more: 

  • Confidential Computing for Azure Service Bus Premium blog 
  • Documentation

items.title: Update: 99.99% uptime for all Azure Service Bus Premium namespaces in Availability Zone regions
items.description:
Starting May 1, 2026, all Azure Service Bus Premium namespaces deployed in regions with Availability Zone support now qualify for a 99.99% uptime SLA. Premium is the tier customers choose for their most important workloads, and this update brings the SLA in line with the zone-redundant infrastructure those namespaces already run on. Previously, the 99.99% SLA required partitioned namespaces to be enabled. That requirement has been removed - any Premium namespace in an AZ region now receives the higher SLA automatically. 

Availability Zones are physically separate datacenters within an Azure region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking. A Premium namespace deployed in an AZ region is automatically replicated across multiple zones, so the messaging service stays available even if a full datacenter goes offline. No configuration changes are required for existing deployments to benefit from the higher SLA. 

Partitioned namespaces remain fully supported for workloads that need higher throughput through multi-broker distribution. The change is purely about SLA eligibility - partitioning is no longer a prerequisite for the 99.99% commitment. 

Learn more: 

  • SLA for Azure Service Bus  
  • Service Bus Premium tier documentation. 
  • Azure Service Bus blog

items.title: Generally Available: Sentinel TI - improved pattern parsing & revoke reliability
items.description:
We’ve rolled out two important improvements to enhance accuracy and control in pattern-based workflows: 

  • Revoke fix: Resolved an issue where revoke actions were not consistently applied, ensuring changes now take effect reliably and as intended. 
  • Support for AND in pattern parsing: You can now combine conditions using AND, enabling more precise and expressive pattern definitions. 

These updates help you manage indicators and patterns with greater confidence and precision.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager rule impact analyzer
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network Manager rule impact analyzer is now generally available, empowering you to simulate the impact of your security admin rules on your virtual networks before deploying your rules. 

With this capability, you can simulate the effects of your security admin rules on your virtual networks’ existing traffic flows and modify rules as needed to ensure your desired traffic flows are maintained and reduce the risk of unexpected connectivity issues. 

This feature is available in the Azure portal and is powered by Azure Network Watcher traffic analytics and virtual network flow logs, providing data-driven insights into how security admin rule deployments could affect your existing virtual network traffic. 

Learn more.
